body.text: Śaṃkara: Upadeśasāhasrī
body.translated_text: <s>Śaṃkara</s>: <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s>

children.text: caitanyaṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaṃ sarvabhūtaguhāśayam /
children.translated_text: Consciousness, all-pervading, everything, dwelling in the cave of all beings,

children.text: yat sarvaviṣayātītaṃ tasmai sarvavide namaḥ // SamUpad_I,1.1 //
children.translated_text: which transcends all objects — salutation to that omniscient one! // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.1 //

children.text: samāpayya kriyāḥ sarvā dārāgnyādhānapūrvikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having completed all rites beginning with marriage and the establishment of the sacred fires,

children.text: brahmavidyām athedānīṃ vaktuṃ vedaḥ pracakrame // SamUpad_I,1.2 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s> now proceeded to teach the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.2 //

children.text: karmāṇi dehayogārthaṃ dehayoge priyāpriye /
children.translated_text: Actions are for the purpose of union with a body; in the union with a body, the pleasant and unpleasant

children.text: dhruve syātāṃ tato rāgo dveṣaś caiva tataḥ kriyāḥ // SamUpad_I,1.3 //
children.translated_text: are certain to arise; from that come attachment and aversion, and from these, actions. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.3 //

body.text: dharmādharmau tato 'jñasya dehayogas tathā punaḥ

children.text: evaṃ nityapravṛtto 'yaṃ saṃsāraś cakravad bhṛśam // SamUpad_I,1.4 //
children.translated_text: thus this cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) revolves perpetually like a wheel, with great force. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.4 //

body.translated_text: From that arise merit and demerit for the ignorant one, and thus again union with a body —

children.text: ajñānaṃ tasya mūlaṃ syād iti taddhānam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Ignorance is its root — therefore the destruction of that [ignorance] is desired;

children.text: brahmavidyāta ārabdhā tato niḥśreyasaṃ bhavet // SamUpad_I,1.5 //
children.translated_text: having commenced from the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, from that the highest good would arise. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.5 //

children.text: vidyaivājñānahānāya na karmāpratikūlataḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowledge alone is for the destruction of ignorance, not action, since it is not opposed [to ignorance];

children.text: nājñānasyāprahāṇe hi rāgadveṣakṣayo bhavet // SamUpad_I,1.6 //
children.translated_text: for without the destruction of ignorance, the destruction of attachment and aversion cannot occur. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.6 //

children.text: rāgadveṣakṣayābhāve karma doṣodbhavaṃ dhruvam /
children.translated_text: In the absence of the destruction of attachment and aversion, action born of defect is certain;

children.text: tasmān niḥśreyasārthāya vidyaivātra vidhīyate // SamUpad_I,1.7 //
children.translated_text: therefore, for the sake of the highest good, knowledge alone is prescribed here. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.7 //

children.text: nanu karma tathā nityaṃ kartavyaṃ jīvane sati /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But action too must always be performed as long as one lives;

children.text: vidyāyāḥ sahakāritvaṃ mokṣaṃ prati hi tad vrajet // SamUpad_I,1.8 //
children.translated_text: it would serve as an auxiliary to knowledge with respect to liberation. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.8 //

children.text: yathā vidyā tathā karma coditatvāviśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as knowledge, so too action, since there is no difference in their being enjoined;

children.text: pratyavāyasmṛteś caiva kāryaṃ karma mumukṣubhiḥ // SamUpad_I,1.9 //
children.translated_text: and from the remembrance of adverse consequences, action must be performed by seekers of liberation. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.9 //

children.text: nanu dhruvaphalā vidyā nānyat kiṃcid apekṣate /
children.translated_text: [Reply:] But knowledge, having a certain result, does not depend on anything else,

children.text: nāgniṣṭomo yathaivānyad dhruvakāryo 'py apekṣate // SamUpad_I,1.10 //
children.translated_text: unlike the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, which, though having a certain purpose, requires other [accessories]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.10 //

children.text: tathā dhruvaphalā vidyā karma nityam apekṣate /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Similarly, knowledge, though having a certain result, requires constant action.

children.text: ity evaṃ kecid icchanti na karma pratikūlataḥ // SamUpad_I,1.11 //
children.translated_text: Thus some maintain — [but] action is not [an auxiliary, being] opposed [to knowledge]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.11 //

children.text: vidyāyāḥ pratikūlaṃ hi karma syāt sābhimānataḥ /
children.translated_text: For action would be opposed to knowledge, since it involves the notion of agency (<s>abhimāna</s>);

children.text: nirvikārātmabuddhiś ca vidyetīha prakīrtitā // SamUpad_I,1.12 //
children.translated_text: and the understanding of the Self as changeless is proclaimed here as knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.12 //

children.text: ahaṃ kartā mamedaṃ syād iti karma pravartate /
children.translated_text: 'I am the doer, this is mine' — thus action proceeds;

children.text: vastvadhīnā bhaved vidyā kartradhīno bhaved vidhiḥ // SamUpad_I,1.13 //
children.translated_text: knowledge depends on the reality [of the object], while injunction depends on the agent. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.13 //

children.text: kārakāṇy upamṛdnāti vidyābbuddhim ivoṣare /
children.translated_text: Knowledge crushes the [notion of] agency, like [the sun dissolves] a mirage in a desert;

children.text: tatsatyamatim ādāya karma kartuṃ vyavasyati // SamUpad_I,1.14 //
children.translated_text: taking that [agency] as real, one resolves to perform action. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.14 //

children.text: viruddhatvād ataḥ śakyaṃ karma kartuṃ na vidyayā /
children.translated_text: Due to their mutual opposition, therefore, it is not possible to perform action together with knowledge;

children.text: sahaivaṃ viduṣā tasmāt karma heyaṃ mumukṣuṇā // SamUpad_I,1.15 //
children.translated_text: therefore, by the wise person who seeks liberation, action is to be abandoned. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.15 //

children.text: dehādyair aviśeṣeṇa dehino grahaṇaṃ nijam /
children.translated_text: The identification of the embodied self with the body and the rest without distinction

children.text: prāṇināṃ tad avidyotthaṃ tāvat karmavidhir bhavet // SamUpad_I,1.16 //
children.translated_text: arises from ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) in living beings — so long [as that lasts], the injunction to act remains operative. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.16 //

children.text: neti netīti dehādīn apohyātmāvaśeṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By negating the body and the rest through '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), the Self alone remains;

children.text: aviśeṣātmabodhārthaṃ tenāvidyā nivartitā // SamUpad_I,1.17 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of the knowledge of the undifferentiated Self, thereby ignorance is removed. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.17 //

children.text: nivṛttā sā kathaṃ bhūyaḥ prasūyeta pramāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: Once removed, how could it arise again, according to valid means of knowledge,

children.text: asaty evāviśeṣe hi pratyagātmani kevale // SamUpad_I,1.18 //
children.translated_text: [since it would arise only] when non-differentiation is absent in the inner Self which is pure [consciousness]? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.18 //

children.text: na ced bhūyaḥ prasūyeta kartā bhokteti dhīḥ katham /
children.translated_text: If it does not arise again, how could the notion 'I am the doer, I am the enjoyer' [arise]?

children.text: sad asmīti ca vijñāne tasmād vidyāsahāyikā // SamUpad_I,1.19 //
children.translated_text: And in the knowledge 'I am existence' — therefore [no action is] an auxiliary to knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.19 //

children.text: atyarecayad ity ukto nyāsaḥ śrutyāta eva hi /
children.translated_text: Renunciation (<s>nyāsa</s>) is declared [by the <s>śruti</s>] to surpass [all actions], for from the <s>śruti</s> alone [it is known]:

children.text: karmabhyo mānasāntebhya etāvad iti vājinām // SamUpad_I,1.20 //
children.translated_text: 'Above the mental [sacrifices] and all other actions' — thus [say] the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.20 //

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ śrutaṃ tasmāt tyājyaṃ karma mumukṣubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Immortality is heard [from the <s>śruti</s>]; therefore action is to be abandoned by seekers of liberation.

children.text: agniṣṭomavad ity uktaṃ tatredam abhidhīyate // SamUpad_I,1.21 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] 'Like the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>' was said — to that the following is stated: // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.21 //

children.text: naikakārakasādhyatvāt phalānyatvāc ca karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since [the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>] is accomplished not by a single agent, and since the fruit of action is different [from the action],

children.text: vidyā tadviparītāto dṛṣṭānto viṣamo bhavet // SamUpad_I,1.22 //
children.translated_text: while knowledge is the opposite of that — therefore the analogy is unequal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.22 //

children.text: kṛṣyādivat phalārthatvād anyakarmopabṛṃhaṇam /
children.translated_text: Like agriculture and such, because [the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>] has its fruit as its purpose, it requires supplementation by other actions;

children.text: agniṣṭomas tv apekṣeta vidyānyat kim apekṣate // SamUpad_I,1.23 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> indeed requires [such accessories] — but what else does knowledge require? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.23 //

children.text: pratyavāyas tu tasyaiva yasyāhaṃkāra iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Adverse consequences apply only to one in whom egoism (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) is accepted;

children.text: ahaṃkāraphalārthitve vidyete nātmavedinaḥ // SamUpad_I,1.24 //
children.translated_text: egoism and the desire for fruits are not found in the knower of the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.24 //

children.text: tasmād ajñānahānāya saṃsāravinivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the destruction of ignorance and for the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration),

children.text: brahmavidyāvidhānāya prārabdhopaniṣat tv iyam // SamUpad_I,1.25 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Upaniṣad</s> is commenced for the teaching of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.25 //

children.text: sader upanipūrvasya kvipi copaniṣad bhavet /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>upaniṣad</s>' is derived from the root 'sad' (to sit) with the prefixes 'upa' and 'ni' in the <s>kvip</s> suffix,

children.text: mandīkaraṇabhāvāc ca garbhādeḥ śātanāt tathā // SamUpad_I,1.26 //
children.translated_text: [and it means] the weakening and the destruction of [bondage such as] the womb and the like. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1.26 //

body.text: iti caitanyaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,1 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on Consciousness (<s>Caitanyaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.1 //

children.text: pratiṣeddhum aśakyatvān neti netīti śeṣitam /
children.translated_text: Because it cannot be negated, the Self remains through '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this);

children.text: idaṃ nāham idaṃ nāham ity addhā pratipadyate // SamUpad_I,2,1 //
children.translated_text: 'This I am not, this I am not' — thus one truly realizes. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.2.1 //

children.text: idaṃdhīr idamātmotthā vācārambhaṇagocarā /
children.translated_text: The notion 'this' arises from the self [as reflected in] 'this,' and pertains to the sphere of verbal expression;

children.text: niṣiddhātmodbhavatvāt sā na punar mānatāṃ vrajet // SamUpad_I,2.2 //
children.translated_text: since its origin in the Self has been negated, it cannot again attain the status of a valid cognition. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.2.2 //

children.text: pūrvabuddhim abādhitvā nottarā jāyate matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Without sublating the prior cognition, a subsequent understanding does not arise;

children.text: dṛśir ekaḥ svayaṃsiddhaḥ phalatvāt sa na bādhyate // SamUpad_I,2.3 //
children.translated_text: the one seer is self-established — being the result [of all cognition], it cannot be sublated. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.2.3 //

children.text: idaṃvanam atikramya śokamohādidūṣitam /
children.translated_text: Having crossed beyond this forest [of objectivity] tainted by grief, delusion, and the like,

children.text: vanād gāndhārako yadvat svam ātmānaṃ prapadyate // SamUpad_I,2.4 //
children.translated_text: just as a man from <s>Gāndhāra</s> [returns to] his own self from the forest. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.2.4 //

body.text: iti pratiṣedhaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,2 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on Negation (<s>Pratiṣedhaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.2 //

children.text: īśvaraś ced anātmā syān nāsāv asmīti dhārayet /
children.translated_text: If the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) were not the Self, one would hold 'I am not that';

children.text: ātmā ced īśvaro 'smīti vidyā sānyanivartikā // SamUpad_I,3.1 //
children.translated_text: but if the Lord is the Self, 'I am [the Lord]' — this knowledge removes [the perception of] otherness. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.3.1 //

children.text: ātmano 'nyasya ced dharmā asthūlatvādayo matāḥ /
children.translated_text: If attributes such as 'not gross' are considered to belong to something other than the Self,

children.text: ajñeyatve 'sya kiṃ taiḥ syād ātmatve tv anyadhīhnutiḥ // SamUpad_I,3.2 //
children.translated_text: if it is unknowable, what use would they be? But if it is the Self, the notion of otherness is negated. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.3.2 //

children.text: mithyādhyāsaniṣedhārthaṃ tato 'sthūlādi gṛhyatām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let 'not gross' and the like be understood for the purpose of negating false superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>);

children.text: paratra cen niṣedhārthaṃ śūnyatāvarṇanaṃ hi tat // SamUpad_I,3.3 //
children.translated_text: if [they are taken] as negation of something other [than the Self], that would be a description of voidness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.3.3 //

children.text: bubhutsor yadi cānyatra pratyagātmana iṣyate /
children.translated_text: If for one who desires to know, [the object of knowledge] is accepted as something other than the inner Self,

children.text: aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhra iti cānarthakaṃ vacaḥ // SamUpad_I,3.4 //
children.translated_text: then 'without breath, without mind, pure' — such words would be meaningless. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.3.4 //

body.text: itīśvaraprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the Lord (<s>Īśvaraprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.3 //

children.text: ahaṃpratyayabījaṃ yad ahaṃpratyayavatsthitam /
children.translated_text: That which is the seed of the I-notion, which abides as possessed of the I-notion —

children.text: nāhaṃpratyayavahnyuṣṭaṃ kathaṃ karma prarohati // SamUpad_I,4.1 //
children.translated_text: when burnt by the fire of the [negation of the] I-notion, how can action sprout? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4.1 //

children.text: dṛṣṭavac cet prarohaḥ syān nānyakarmā sa iṣyate /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If sprouting were possible as seen [in the world] — [Reply:] That is not accepted as the action of another;

children.text: tannirodhe kathaṃ tat syāt pṛcchāmo vas tad ucyatām // SamUpad_I,4.2 //
children.translated_text: upon the cessation of that [I-notion], how could it be? We ask you — let it be stated! // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4.2 //

children.text: dehādyārambhasāmarthyāj jñānaṃ sadviṣayaṃ tvayi /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Due to the capacity to initiate the body and the rest, knowledge of existence in you

children.text: abhibhūya phalaṃ kuryāt karmānte jñānam udbhavet // SamUpad_I,4.3 //
children.translated_text: would be overpowered and produce its fruit; at the end of [such] action, knowledge would arise. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4.3 //

children.text: ārabdhasya phale hy ete bhogo jñānaṃ ca karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Reply:] For these — experience and knowledge — are the fruits of action that has already begun;

children.text: avirodhas tayor yukto vaidharmyaṃ cetarasya tu // SamUpad_I,4.4 //
children.translated_text: their non-contradiction is logical, but the dissimilarity with the other [case] is [also to be recognized]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4.4 //

children.text: dehātmajñānavaj jñānaṃ dehātmajñānabādhakam /
children.translated_text: Knowledge that sublates the identification of the Self with the body, just like [earlier] knowledge of the body-self [identification],

children.text: ātmany eya bhaved yasya sa necchann api mucyate // SamUpad_I,4.5 //
children.translated_text: one in whom this arises in the Self is liberated even without desiring it. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4.5 //

body.text: tataḥ sarvam idaṃ siddhaṃ prayogo 'smābhir īritaḥ // SamUpad_I,4.5 //
body.translated_text: Thus all this is established; the method has been stated by us. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4.5 //

body.text: ity ahaṃpratyayaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,4 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the I-notion (<s>Ahaṃpratyayaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.4 //

children.text: mūtrāśaṅko yathodaṅko nāgrahīd amṛtaṃ muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the sage, suspecting urine, did not accept the nectar that was [offered] from a pot,

children.text: karmanāśabhayāj jantor ātmajñānāgrahas tathā // SamUpad_I,5.1 //
children.translated_text: so too a person's refusal to accept Self-knowledge is due to fear of the destruction of [ritual] action. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.5.1 //

children.text: buddhisthaś calatīvātmā dhyāyatīva ca dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: The Self, [reflected] in the intellect, appears as if it moves and as if it meditates;

children.text: naugatasya yathā vṛkṣās tadvat saṃsāravibhramaḥ // SamUpad_I,5.2 //
children.translated_text: just as trees [appear to move] for one on a boat — such is the delusion of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.5.2 //

children.text: nausthasya prātilomyena nagānāṃ gamanaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as for one standing on a boat, the mountains appear to move in the opposite direction,

children.text: ātmanaḥ saṃsṛtis tadvad dhyāyatīveti hi śrutiḥ // SamUpad_I,5.3 //
children.translated_text: so too is the transmigration of the Self — 'as if it meditates,' thus says the <s>śruti</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.5.3 //

children.text: caitanyapratibimbena vyāpto bodho hi jāyate /
children.translated_text: Cognition arises pervaded by the reflection of consciousness;

children.text: buddheḥ śabdādinirbhāsas tena momuhyate jagat // SamUpad_I,5.4 //
children.translated_text: from the intellect arises the appearance of sound and the like — by this the world is deluded. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.5.4 //

children.text: caitanyābhāsatāhamas tādarthyaṃ ca tad asya yat /
children.translated_text: The I-notion is the semblance of consciousness, and its purposefulness is that

children.text: idamaṃśaprahāṇe na paraḥ so 'nubhavo bhavet // SamUpad_I,5.5 //
children.translated_text: upon the abandonment of the 'this' aspect, the experience of the Supreme would [certainly] arise. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.5.5 //

body.text: iti mūtrāśaṅkaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,5 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the Suspicion of Urine (<s>Mūtrāśaṅkaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.5 //

children.text: chittvā tyaktena hastena svayaṃ nātmā viśeṣyate /
children.translated_text: By a hand that has been cut off and discarded, the Self is not qualified;

children.text: tathā śiṣṭena sarveṇa yena yena viśeṣyate // SamUpad_I,6.1 //
children.translated_text: likewise with all that remains — by whatever it is qualified. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6.1 //

children.text: tasmāt tyaktena hastena tulyaṃ sarvaṃ viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, all qualification is equal to [qualification by] a discarded hand;

children.text: anātmatvena tasmāj jño muktaḥ sarvaviśeṣaṇaiḥ // SamUpad_I,6.2 //
children.translated_text: since they are not-self, therefore the knower is free from all qualifications. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6.2 //

children.text: viśeṣaṇam idaṃ sarvaṃ sādhvalaṃkaraṇaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: All this qualification is like the ornamentation of a virtuous woman;

children.text: avidyāstam ataḥ sarvaṃ jñāta ātmany asad bhavet // SamUpad_I,6.3 //
children.translated_text: therefore all this has ignorance as its basis; when the Self is known, it becomes unreal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6.3 //

children.text: jñātaivātmā sadā grāhyo jñeyam utsṛjya kevalaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Self, once known, is always to be grasped as pure [consciousness] alone, having abandoned the knowable;

children.text: aham ity api yad grāhyaṃ vyapetāṅgasamaṃ hi tat // SamUpad_I,6.4 //
children.translated_text: even what is grasped as 'I' is equal to a severed limb. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6.4 //

children.text: yāvān syād idamaṃśo yaḥ sa svato 'nyo viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Whatever constitutes the 'this' aspect — that is other than the Self and is a qualification;

children.text: viśeṣaprakṣayo yatra siddho jñaś citragur yathā // SamUpad_I,6.5 //
children.translated_text: where the destruction of distinctions is accomplished, the knower is like a dappled cow [whose markings are irrelevant to its nature]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6.5 //

children.text: idam aṃśo 'ham ity atra tyājyo nātmeti paṇḍitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The 'this' aspect in the [cognition] 'I' is to be abandoned as 'not the Self' by the wise;

children.text: ahaṃ brahmeti śiṣṭo 'ṃśo bhūtapūrvagater bhavet // SamUpad_I,6.6 //
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' — the remaining aspect [of the 'I'] would be [recognized] from its having existed before [as one's true nature]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6.6 //

body.text: iti chittvāprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,6 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the Severed [Hand] (<s>Chittvāprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.6 //

children.text: buddhyārūḍhaṃ sadā sarvaṃ dṛśyate yatra tatra vā /
children.translated_text: Everything always rests upon the intellect and is perceived here or there;

children.text: mayā tasmāt paraṃ brahma sarvajñaś cāsmi sarvagaḥ // SamUpad_I,7.1 //
children.translated_text: therefore I am the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, omniscient and all-pervading. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7.1 //

children.text: yathātmabuddhicārāṇāṃ sākṣī tadvat pareṣv api /
children.translated_text: Just as I am the witness of my own mental activities, so too of others';

children.text: naivāpoḍhuṃ na vādātuṃ śakyas tasmāt paro hy aham // SamUpad_I,7.2 //
children.translated_text: I can neither be removed nor taken; therefore I am indeed the Supreme. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7.2 //

children.text: vikāritvam aśuddhatvaṃ bhautikatvaṃ na cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Changeability, impurity, and materiality do not belong to the Self;

children.text: aśeṣabuddhisākṣitvād buddhivac cālpavedanā // SamUpad_I,7.3 //
children.translated_text: since it witnesses all cognitions, [the attribution of] limited awareness like that of the intellect [is incorrect]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7.3 //

children.text: maṇau prakāśyate yadvad raktādyākāratātape /
children.translated_text: Just as in a jewel the forms of red and the like are illuminated by sunlight,

children.text: mayi saṃdṛśyate sarvam ātapeneva tan mayā // SamUpad_I,7.4 //
children.translated_text: so in me everything is perceived — all that, as if by [my] radiance, [is illuminated] by me. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7.4 //

children.text: buddhau dṛśyaṃ bhaved buddhau satyāṃ nāsti viparyaye /
children.translated_text: The visible [world] exists in the intellect; when the intellect exists, [the world appears]; in its absence, it does not.

children.text: draṣṭā yasmāt sadā draṣṭā tasmād dvaitaṃ na vidyate // SamUpad_I,7.5 //
children.translated_text: Since the seer is always the seer, therefore duality does not exist. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7.5 //

children.text: avivekāt parābhāvaṃ yathā buddhir avet tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as, due to non-discrimination, the intellect perceives the appearance of the other [as real],

children.text: vivekāt tu parād anyaḥ svayaṃ cāpi na vidyate // SamUpad_I,7.6 //
children.translated_text: so through discrimination, nothing other than the Supreme, nor [anything separate] itself, is found to exist. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7.6 //

body.text: iti buddhyārūḍhaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,7 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on What Rests upon the Intellect (<s>Buddhyārūḍhaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.7 //

children.text: citisvarūpaṃ svata eva me mate rasādiyogas tava mohakāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: The nature of consciousness (<s>citi</s>) is inherently my nature, in my view; your association with taste and the like is caused by delusion.

children.text: ato na kiṃcit tava ceṣṭitena me phalaṃ bhavet sarvaviśeṣahānataḥ // SamUpad_I,8.1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, nothing done by you can produce any result for me, since all distinctions have been relinquished. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8.1 //

children.text: vimucya māyāmayakāryatām iha praśāntim āyāhy asadīhitāt sadā /
children.translated_text: Releasing [yourself] from the functioning caused by <s>māyā</s> (illusion) here, attain peace, [freed] from unreal pursuits always;

children.text: ahaṃ paraṃ brahma sadā vimuktavat tathājam ekaṃ dvayavarjitaṃ yataḥ // SamUpad_I,8.2 //
children.translated_text: for I am the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, ever liberated, unborn, one, devoid of duality. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8.2 //

children.text: sadā ca bhūteṣu samo 'smi kevalo yathā ca khaṃ sarvagam akṣaraṃ śivam /
children.translated_text: I am always the same in all beings, pure, just as space is all-pervading, imperishable, and auspicious;

children.text: nirantaraṃ niṣkalam akriyaṃ paraṃ tato na me 'stīha phalaṃ tavehitaiḥ // SamUpad_I,8.3 //
children.translated_text: continuous, without parts, without action, supreme — therefore no result from your endeavors exists for me here. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8.3 //

children.text: ahaṃ mamaiko na tadanyad iṣyate tathā na kasyāpy aham asmy asaṅgataḥ /
children.translated_text: I am mine alone; nothing other than that is accepted. Likewise, I do not belong to anyone, being unattached.

children.text: asaṅgarūpo 'ham ato na me tvayā kṛtena kāryaṃ tava cādvayatvataḥ // SamUpad_I,8.4 //
children.translated_text: Being of the nature of non-attachment, I have no purpose served by your action, and you [have no separate purpose] due to non-duality. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8.4 //

children.text: phale ca hetau ca jano viṣaktavān iti pracintyāham ato vimokṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: Reflecting thus — 'People are attached to both the fruit and the cause' — I, for the sake of liberation,

children.text: janasya saṃvādam imaṃ prakḷptavān svarūpatattvārthavibodhakāraṇam // SamUpad_I,8.5 //
children.translated_text: have composed this dialogue for the awakening of people to the truth of their own nature. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8.5 //

children.text: saṃvādam etaṃ yadi cintayen naro vimucyate 'jñānamahābhayāgamāt /
children.translated_text: If a person contemplates this dialogue, they are freed from the great fear arising from ignorance;

children.text: vimuktakāmaś ca tathā janaḥ sadā caraty aśokaḥ sama ātmavit sukhī // SamUpad_I,8.6 //
children.translated_text: and such a person, free from desire, always moves about sorrowless, equanimous, a knower of the Self, and happy. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8.6 //

body.text: iti citisvarūpaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,8 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the Nature of Consciousness (<s>Citisvarūpaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.8 //

children.text: sūkṣmatāvyāpite jñeye gandhāder uttarottaram /
children.translated_text: In the knowable, pervaded by increasing subtlety — from smell and the rest, each successively more [subtle],

children.text: pratyagātmāvasāneṣu pūrvapūrvaprahāṇataḥ // SamUpad_I,9.1 //
children.translated_text: terminating in the inner Self, through the successive abandonment of each preceding [element]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.9.1 //

children.text: śārīrā pṛthivī tāvad yāvad bāhyā pramāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: The earth in the body is as extensive as the external earth, according to valid cognition;

children.text: abādīni ca tattvāni tāvaj jñeyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ // SamUpad_I,9.2 //
children.translated_text: and the principles beginning with water are to be known completely in the same way. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.9.2 //

children.text: vāyvādīnāṃ yathotpatteḥ pūrvaṃ khaṃ sarvagaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as space is all-pervading before the origination of wind and the rest,

children.text: aham ekaḥ sadā sarvaś cinmātraḥ sarvago 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,9.3 //
children.translated_text: so I am one, always everything, pure consciousness alone, all-pervading, and non-dual. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.9.3 //

children.text: brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāntā ye prāṇino mama pūḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: All living beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable things, are known as my city (<s>pūḥ</s>);

children.text: kāmakrodhādayo doṣā jāyeran me kuto 'nyataḥ // SamUpad_I,9.4 //
children.translated_text: how could faults such as desire and anger arise in me from any other [source]? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9.4 //

children.text: bhūtadoṣaiḥ sadāspṛṣṭaṃ sarvabhūtastham īśvaram /
children.translated_text: The Lord, ever untouched by the faults of beings, dwelling in all beings—

children.text: nīlaṃ vyoma yathā bālo duṣṭaṃ māṃ vīkṣate janaḥ // SamUpad_I,9.5 //
children.translated_text: people perceive me as tainted, just as a child sees the sky as blue. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9.5 //

children.text: maccaitanyāvabhāsyatvāt sarvaprāṇidhiyāṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Since the intellects of all living beings are always illumined by my consciousness,

children.text: pūr mama prāṇinaḥ sarve sarvajñasya vipāpmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,9.6 //
children.translated_text: all living beings are my city—[the city] of the omniscient one, free from evil. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9.6 //

children.text: janimaj jñānavijñeyaṃ svapnajñānavad iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Knowledge that has origination, together with its object, is considered like dream-knowledge;

children.text: nityaṃ nirviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tasmād dvaitaṃ na vidyate // SamUpad_I,9.7 //
children.translated_text: [True] knowledge is eternal and objectless; therefore duality does not exist. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9.7 //

children.text: jñātur jñātir hi nityoktā suṣupte tv anyaśūnyataḥ /
children.translated_text: The knowing capacity of the knower is declared eternal, since in deep sleep there is absence of everything else;

children.text: jāgrajjñātis tv avidyātas tad grāhyaṃ cāsad iṣyatām // SamUpad_I,9.8 //
children.translated_text: but waking cognition is due to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); let its object of cognition be accepted as unreal. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9.8 //

children.text: rūpavattvādyasattvān na dṛṣṭyādeḥ karmatā yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as seeing and the like cannot have objecthood, because of the unreality of color-possessing things and so forth,

children.text: evaṃ vijñānakarmatvaṃ bhūmno nāstīti gamyate // SamUpad_I,9.9 //
children.translated_text: so it is understood that the <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite) cannot be an object of consciousness. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9.9 //

body.text: iti sūkṣmatāprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,9 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Sūkṣmatā-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Subtlety). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,9 //

children.text: dṛśisvarūpaṃ gaganopamaṃ paraṃ sakṛdvibhātaṃ tv ajam ekam akṣaram /
children.translated_text: Of the nature of pure seeing, like space, supreme, shining once and for all, unborn, one, imperishable,

children.text: alepakaṃ sarvagataṃ yad advayaṃ tad eva cāhaṃ satataṃ vimukta om // SamUpad_I,10.1 //
children.translated_text: unstained, all-pervading, non-dual—that indeed am I, ever liberated. <s>Om</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.1 //

children.text: dṛśis tu śuddho 'ham avikriyātmako na me 'sti kaścid viṣayaḥ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: I am pure seeing, of unchanging nature; no object exists for me by nature;

children.text: puras tiraś cordhvam adhaś ca sarvataḥ supūrṇabhūmā tv aja ātmani sthitaḥ // SamUpad_I,10.2 //
children.translated_text: in front, behind, above, below, and in all directions—supremely full, infinite, unborn, established in the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.2 //

children.text: ajo 'maraś caiva tathājaro 'mṛtaḥ svayaṃprabhaḥ sarvagato 'ham advayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Unborn, undying, ageless, immortal, self-luminous, all-pervading, I am non-dual;

children.text: na kāraṇaṃ kāryam atīva nirmalaḥ sadaiva tṛptaś ca tato vimukta om // SamUpad_I,10.3 //
children.translated_text: neither cause nor effect, supremely pure, ever content, and therefore liberated. <s>Om</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.3 //

children.text: suṣuptajāgratsvapataś ca darśanaṃ na me 'sti kiṃcit svam iveha mohanam /
children.translated_text: The perception of deep sleep, waking, and dream does not belong to me—nothing is my own, as it were, [all is] delusion here;

children.text: svataś ca teṣāṃ parato 'py asattvatas turīya evāsmi sadā dṛg advayaḥ // SamUpad_I,10.4 //
children.translated_text: since those [states] are unreal both in themselves and from [the standpoint of] another, I am always the <s>Turīya</s> (fourth state), pure seeing, non-dual. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.4 //

children.text: śarīrabuddhīndriyaduḥkhasaṃtatir na me na cāhaṃ mama nirvikārataḥ /
children.translated_text: The succession of body, intellect, senses, and suffering is not mine, nor am I [theirs], because I am changeless;

children.text: asattvahetoś ca tathaiva saṃtater asattvam asyāḥ svapato hi dṛśyavat // SamUpad_I,10.5 //
children.translated_text: and because of the unreality of such succession, its unreality [is established], like objects seen by a dreamer. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.5 //

children.text: idaṃ tu satyaṃ mama nāsti vikriyā vikārahetur na hi me 'dvayatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: But this is true: I have no modification; there is no cause of change in me, due to my non-duality;

children.text: na puṇyapāpe na ca mokṣabandhane na cāsti varṇāśramatāśarīrataḥ // SamUpad_I,10.6 //
children.translated_text: neither merit nor sin, neither liberation nor bondage, nor caste nor life-stage, since I am bodiless. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.6 //

children.text: anādito nirguṇato na karma me phalaṃ ca tasmāt paramo 'ham advayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since I am beginningless and without qualities, no action belongs to me, nor its fruit; therefore I am supreme, non-dual;

children.text: yathā nabhaḥ sarvagataṃ na lipyate tathā hy ahaṃ dehagato 'pi sūkṣmataḥ // SamUpad_I,10.7 //
children.translated_text: just as space, all-pervading, is not tainted, so too I, though dwelling in the body, [remain untainted] due to my subtlety. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.7 //

children.text: sadā ca bhūteṣu samo 'ham īśvaraḥ kṣarākṣarābhyāṃ paramo hy athottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am always the same in all beings, the Lord, higher than both the perishable and the imperishable, supreme;

children.text: parātmatattvaś ca tathādvayo 'pi san viparyayeṇābhivṛtas tv avidyayā // SamUpad_I,10.8 //
children.translated_text: being the reality of the Supreme Self, non-dual, yet [I appear] enveloped by the contrary through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.8 //

children.text: avidyayā bhāvanayā ca karmabhir vivikta ātmāvyavadhiḥ sunirmalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), imagination, and actions, the Self—which is isolated, unlimited, supremely pure—

children.text: dṛgādiśaktipracito 'ham advayaḥ sthitaḥ svarūpe gaganaṃ yathācalam // SamUpad_I,10.9 //
children.translated_text: I, non-dual, endowed with the powers of seeing and so forth, abide in my own nature, immovable like space. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.9 //

children.text: ahaṃ paraṃ brahma viniścayātmadṛṅ na jāyate bhūya iti śruter vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, of the nature of certain self-knowledge; 'He is not born again'—such is the declaration of <s>Śruti</s>;

children.text: na caiva bīje tv asati prajāyate phalaṃ na janmāsti tato hy amohatā // SamUpad_I,10.10 //
children.translated_text: and when the seed is absent, no fruit is produced; there is no birth, and hence freedom from delusion. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.10 //

children.text: mamedam itthaṃ ca tavāda īdṛśaṃ tathāham evaṃ na paro 'pi cānyathā /
children.translated_text: 'This is mine, thus,' and 'Yours is like this,' 'I am thus, and another is otherwise'—

children.text: vimūḍhataivāsya janasya kalpanā sadā same brahmaṇi vādvaye śive // SamUpad_I,10.11 //
children.translated_text: this is merely the confused imagination of people about <s>Brahman</s>, which is always equal, non-dual, and auspicious. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.11 //

children.text: yad advayaṃ jñānam atīva nirmalaṃ mahātmanāṃ tatra na śokamohatā /
children.translated_text: That non-dual knowledge, supremely pure—for great souls, there is no sorrow or delusion therein;

children.text: tayor abhāve na hi karma janma vā bhaved ayaṃ vedavidāṃ viniścayaḥ // SamUpad_I,10.12 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of those two, neither action nor birth can occur—this is the settled conclusion of the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.12 //

children.text: suṣuptavaj jāgrati yo na paśyati dvayaṃ tu paśyann api cādvayatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: He who while waking does not see duality, as in deep sleep, though seeing, because of non-duality—

children.text: tathā ca kurvann api niṣkriyaś ca yaḥ sa ātmavin nānya itīha niścayaḥ // SamUpad_I,10.13 //
children.translated_text: and who, though acting, is actionless—he is a knower of the Self, none other; such is the firm conclusion here. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.13 //

children.text: itīdam uktaṃ paramārthadarśanaṃ mayā hi vedāntaviniścitaṃ param /
children.translated_text: Thus has been stated this vision of the supreme truth, ascertained by me from the <s>Vedānta</s>, the highest;

children.text: vimucyate 'smin yadi niścito bhaven na lipyate vyomavad eva karmabhiḥ // SamUpad_I,10.14 //
children.translated_text: if one becomes firm in this, one is liberated; one is not tainted by actions, just like space. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10.14 //

body.text: iti dṛśiprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,10 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Dṛśi-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Seeing). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,10 //

children.text: īkṣitṛtvaṃ svataḥsiddhaṃ jantūnāṃ ca tato 'nyatā /
children.translated_text: The nature of being a seer is self-established, and the otherness of creatures [from the Self is apparent];

children.text: ajñānād ity ato 'nyatvaṃ sad asīti nivartyate // SamUpad_I,11.1 //
children.translated_text: since [this otherness] is due to ignorance, that otherness is negated by [the teaching] '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (You are That). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.1 //

children.text: etāvad dhy amṛtatvaṃ na kiṃcid anyat sahāyakam /
children.translated_text: Immortality is just this much—nothing else is an aid [to it];

children.text: jñānasyeti bruvac chāstraṃ saliṅgaṃ karma bādhate // SamUpad_I,11.2 //
children.translated_text: the scripture, declaring this about knowledge, sublates action together with its marks. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.2 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ manaso vṛttam aviśeṣeṇa paśyataḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who sees the activity of all minds without distinction,

children.text: tasya me nirvikārasya viśeṣaḥ syāt kathaṃcana // SamUpad_I,11.3 //
children.translated_text: how could there be any distinction for me, who am changeless? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.3 //

children.text: manovṛttaṃ manaś caiva svapnavaj jāgratīkṣituḥ /
children.translated_text: The mental activity and the mind itself, like a dream, for the seer in the waking state;

children.text: saṃprasāde dvayāsattvāc cinmātraḥ sarvago 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,11.4 //
children.translated_text: in deep sleep (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), due to the absence of duality, [one is] pure consciousness alone, all-pervading, non-dual. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.4 //

children.text: svapnaḥ satyo yathābodhād dehātmatvaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a dream is real [only] until awakening, so too is identification with the body;

children.text: pratyakṣādeḥ pramāṇatvaṃ jāgrat syād ātmavedanāt // SamUpad_I,11.5 //
children.translated_text: the validity of perception and other means of knowledge in the waking state [ceases] upon realization of the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.5 //

children.text: vyomavat sarvabhūtastho bhūtadoṣair vivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like space, dwelling in all beings, free from the faults of beings,

children.text: sākṣī cetāguṇaḥ śuddho brahmaivāsmīti kevalaḥ // SamUpad_I,11.6 //
children.translated_text: the witness, conscious, beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), pure—'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.6 //

children.text: nāmarūpakriyābhyo 'nyo nityamuktasvarūpavān /
children.translated_text: Other than name, form, and action, possessing the nature of eternal freedom,

children.text: aham ātmā paraṃ brahma cinmātro 'haṃ sadādvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,11.7 //
children.translated_text: I am the Self, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, pure consciousness alone, ever non-dual. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.7 //

children.text: ahaṃ brahmāsmi kartā ca bhoktā cāsmīti ye viduḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' and [yet also think] 'I am the doer and the enjoyer'—

children.text: te naṣṭā jñanakarmabhyāṃ nāstikāḥ syur na saṃśayaḥ // SamUpad_I,11.8 //
children.translated_text: they are destroyed by [the contradiction between] knowledge and action, and are surely nihilists, without doubt. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.8 //

children.text: dharmādharmaphalair yoga iṣṭo 'dṛṣṭo yathātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the connection of the Self with the fruits of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) is unseen [i.e., accepted on scriptural authority],

children.text: śāstrād brahmatvam apy asya mokṣo jñānāt tatheṣyatām // SamUpad_I,11.9 //
children.translated_text: so too let the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of this [Self] and liberation through knowledge be accepted from scripture. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.9 //

children.text: yā māhārajanādyās tā vāsanāḥ svapnadarśibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>), such as Maharajana dye and the like,

children.text: anubhūyanta eveha tato 'nyaḥ kevalo dṛśiḥ // SamUpad_I,11.10 //
children.translated_text: experienced here by dream-seers—the pure seer is other than those. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.10 //

children.text: kośād iva viniṣkṛṣṭaḥ kāryakāraṇavarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: As if drawn out from a sheath, free from effect and cause—

children.text: yathāsir dṛśyate svapne tadvad boddhā svayaṃprabhaḥ // SamUpad_I,11.11 //
children.translated_text: just as a sword is seen in a dream, so too the knower is self-luminous. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.11 //

children.text: āpeṣāt pratibuddhasya jñasya svābhāvikaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: The natural state of the awakened knower, through thorough investigation,

children.text: uktaṃ netyādivākyena kalpitasyāpanetṛṇā // SamUpad_I,11.12 //
children.translated_text: is stated by the statement '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), which removes what is superimposed. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.12 //

children.text: mahārājādayo lokā mayi yadvat prakalpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as worlds such as Maharaja and others are imagined in me,

children.text: svapne tadvad dvayaṃ vidyād rūpaṃ vāsanayā saha // SamUpad_I,11.13 //
children.translated_text: so too one should know duality in a dream—form together with impression. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.13 //

children.text: dehaliṅgātmanā kāryā vāsanārūpiṇā kriyā /
children.translated_text: Action is to be performed by one whose nature is the body and its marks, whose form consists of impressions;

children.text: netinetyātmarūpatvān na me kāryā kriyā kvacit // SamUpad_I,11.14 //
children.translated_text: since my nature is [described as] '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), no action is ever to be performed by me. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.14 //

children.text: na tato 'mṛtatāśāsti karmaṇo 'jñānahetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no hope of immortality from action, since [action] has its cause in ignorance;

children.text: mokṣasya jñānahetutvān na tadanyad apekṣate // SamUpad_I,11.15 //
children.translated_text: since liberation has knowledge as its cause, it does not depend on anything else. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.15 //

children.text: amṛtaṃ cābhayaṃ nārtaṃ netītyātmā priyo mama /
children.translated_text: Immortal, fearless, free from affliction—the Self described as '<s>neti</s>' (not this) is dear to me;

children.text: viparītam ato 'nyad yat tyajet tat sakriyaṃ tataḥ // SamUpad_I,11.16 //
children.translated_text: whatever is contrary [to this] and other [than the Self], one should renounce that along with action. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11.16 //

body.text: itīkṣitṛtvaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,11 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Īkṣitṛtva-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on the Nature of Being a Seer). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,11 //

children.text: prakāśasthaṃ yathā dehaṃ sālokam abhimanyate /
children.translated_text: Just as one wrongly considers the body standing in light to possess that light,

children.text: draṣṭrābhāsaṃ tathā cittaṃ draṣṭāham iti manyate // SamUpad_I,12.1 //
children.translated_text: so too the mind, [merely] reflecting the seer, thinks 'I am the seer.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.1 //

children.text: yad eva dṛṣyate loke tenābhinnatvam ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is seen in the world—the Self's identity with that

children.text: prapadyate tato mūḍhas tenātmānaṃ na vindati // SamUpad_I,12.2 //
children.translated_text: is [wrongly] assumed; therefore the deluded one does not find the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.2 //

children.text: daśamasya navātmatvapratipattivad ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like the tenth man's mistaken identification of himself as [one of the] nine,

children.text: dṛśyeṣu tadvad evāyaṃ mūḍho loko na cānyathā // SamUpad_I,12.3 //
children.translated_text: so too in regard to perceived objects, this deluded world [mistakes itself]—it is not otherwise. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.3 //

children.text: tvaṃ kuru tvaṃ tad eveti pratyayāv ekakālikau /
children.translated_text: 'You act' and 'You are that very [<s>Brahman</s>]'—these two cognitions, occurring simultaneously,

children.text: ekanīḍau kathaṃ syātāṃ viruddhau nyāyato vada // SamUpad_I,12.4 //
children.translated_text: how could they coexist in one locus, being contradictory? Tell me, according to reason. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.4 //

children.text: dehābhimānino duḥkhaṃ nādehasya svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Suffering belongs to one identified with the body, not to the bodiless one by nature;

children.text: svāpavat tatprahāṇāya tat tvam ity ucyate dṛśeḥ // SamUpad_I,12.5 //
children.translated_text: as in sleep, for the removal of that [suffering], '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That you are) is declared regarding the seer. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.5 //

children.text: dṛśeś chāyā yadārūḍhā mukhacchāyeva darśane /
children.translated_text: When the reflection of the seer has ascended [into the intellect], like the reflection of a face in a mirror,

children.text: paśyaṃs taṃ pratyayaṃ yogī dṛṣṭa atmeti manyate // SamUpad_I,12.6 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s>, seeing that mental modification, thinks 'The Self has been seen.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.6 //

children.text: taṃ ca mūḍhaṃ ca yady anyaṃ pratyayaṃ vetti no dṛśeḥ /
children.translated_text: But if one knows that [reflection], as well as the deluded [mental modification], and any other mental modification, as not belonging to the seer,

children.text: sa eva yogināṃ śreṣṭho netaraḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ // SamUpad_I,12.7 //
children.translated_text: he alone is the best among <s>yogīs</s>, no other—there is no doubt. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.7 //

children.text: vijñāter yas tu vijñātā sa tvam ity ucyate yataḥ /
children.translated_text: The one who is the knower of cognition—since he is referred to as 'You' [in '<s>tat tvam asi</s>'],

children.text: sa syād anubhavas tasya tato 'nyo 'nubhavo mṛṣā // SamUpad_I,12.8 //
children.translated_text: that would be his [true] experience; any other experience is false. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.8 //

children.text: dṛśirūpe sadā nitye darśanādarśane mayi /
children.translated_text: Since seeing and not-seeing [occur] in me, who am of the nature of seeing, ever eternal,

children.text: kathaṃ syātāṃ tato nānya iṣyate 'nubhavas tataḥ // SamUpad_I,12.9 //
children.translated_text: how could they [affect me]? Therefore no experience other than that [pure seeing] is accepted. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.9 //

children.text: yatsthas tāpo raver dehe dṛśeḥ sa viṣayo yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the heat of the sun that abides in the body is an object of the seer,

children.text: sattvasthas tadvad eveha dṛśeḥ sa viṣayas tathā // SamUpad_I,12.10 //
children.translated_text: so too [the reflection] that abides in <s>sattva</s> (the intellect) is likewise an object of the seer here. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.10 //

children.text: pratiṣiddhedamaṃśo jñaḥ kham ivaikaraso 'dvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the 'this' portion [i.e., the objective element] is negated, the knower, like space, is of one essence, non-dual,

children.text: nityamuktas tathā śuddhaḥ so 'haṃ brahmāsmi kevalaḥ // SamUpad_I,12.11 //
children.translated_text: ever liberated, pure—'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.11 //

children.text: vijñātur naiva vijñātā paro 'nyaḥ saṃbhavaty ataḥ /
children.translated_text: No other, higher knower of the knower is possible; therefore,

children.text: vijñātāhaṃ paro muktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā // SamUpad_I,12.12 //
children.translated_text: I am the knower, supreme, liberated, in all beings always. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.12 //

children.text: yo vedāluptadṛṣṭitvam ātmano 'kartṛtāṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: He who knows the unobstructed seeing of the Self and its non-agency,

children.text: brahmavittvaṃ tathā muktvā sa ātmajño na cetaraḥ // SamUpad_I,12.13 //
children.translated_text: and likewise its nature as knower of <s>Brahman</s>—he, being liberated, is a knower of the Self, and no other. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.13 //

children.text: jñātaivāham avijñeyaḥ śuddho muktaḥ sadety api /
children.translated_text: 'I am the knower indeed, unknowable, pure, liberated, eternal'—even this

children.text: vivekī pratyayo buddher dṛśyatvān nāśavattvataḥ // SamUpad_I,12.14 //
children.translated_text: discriminating cognition belongs to the intellect, since it is an object and perishable. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.14 //

children.text: aluptā tv ātmano dṛṣṭir notpādyā kārakair yataḥ /
children.translated_text: The seeing of the Self is unobstructed and is not produced by any instruments, since

children.text: dṛśyayā cānyayā dṛṣṭyā janyatāsyāḥ prakalpitā // SamUpad_I,12.15 //
children.translated_text: its [supposed] producibility is imagined through another seeing that is [itself] an object. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.15 //

children.text: dehātmabuddhyapekṣatvād ātmanaḥ kartṛtā mṛṣā /
children.translated_text: Since doership of the Self depends on the notion of the body as Self, it is false;

children.text: naiva kiṃcit karomīti satyā buddhiḥ pramāṇajā // SamUpad_I,12.16 //
children.translated_text: 'I do nothing whatsoever'—this is the true understanding born of valid knowledge. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.16 //

children.text: kartṛtvaṃ kārakāpekṣam akartṛtvaṃ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Doership depends on instruments; non-doership is [the Self's] nature;

children.text: kartā bhokteti vijñānaṃ mṛṣaiveti suniścitam // SamUpad_I,12.17 //
children.translated_text: the cognition 'I am a doer, an enjoyer' is certainly false—this is well established. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.17 //

children.text: evaṃ śāstrānumānābhyāṃ svarūpe 'vagate sati /
children.translated_text: Thus, when one's own nature is known through scripture and reasoning,

children.text: niyojyo 'ham iti hy eṣā satyā buddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // SamUpad_I,12.18 //
children.translated_text: how could the understanding 'I am to be enjoined [to act]' be true? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.18 //

children.text: yathā sarvāntaraṃ vyoma vyomno 'py abhyantaro hy aham /
children.translated_text: As space is interior to all things, and I am interior even to space,

children.text: nirvikāro 'calaḥ śuddho 'jaro muktaḥ sadādvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,12.19 //
children.translated_text: changeless, immovable, pure, ageless, liberated, ever non-dual. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12.19 //

body.text: iti prakāśasthaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,12 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Prakāśastha-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on What Stands in Light). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,12 //

children.text: acakṣuṣṭvān na dṛṣṭir me tathāśrotrasya kā śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since I am without eyes, I have no sight; and being without ears, what hearing [can there be]?

children.text: avāktvān na tu vaktiḥ syād amanastvān matiḥ kutaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.1 //
children.translated_text: Being without speech, there can be no speaking; and being without mind, whence could thought [arise]? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.1 //

children.text: aprāṇasya na karmāsti buddhyabhāve na veditā /
children.translated_text: For one without breath, there is no action; in the absence of intellect, there is no knower;

children.text: vidyāvidye tato na staś cinmātrajyotiṣo mama // SamUpad_I,13.2 //
children.translated_text: therefore neither <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) nor <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) exist for me, who am the light of pure consciousness alone. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.2 //

children.text: nityamuktasya śuddhasya kūṭasthasyāvicālinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of one who is eternally liberated, pure, immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>), unshakable,

children.text: amṛtasyākṣarasyaivam aśarīrasya sarvadā // SamUpad_I,13.3 //
children.translated_text: immortal, imperishable—thus, always bodiless— // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.3 //

children.text: jighatsā vā pipāsā vā śokamohau jarāmṛtī /
children.translated_text: hunger or thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age, or death—

children.text: na vidyante 'śarīratvād vyomavad vyāpino mama // SamUpad_I,13.4 //
children.translated_text: these do not exist, since I am bodiless, all-pervading like space. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.4 //

children.text: asparśatvān na me spṛṣṭir nājihvatvād rasajñatā /
children.translated_text: Since I am intangible, I have no touch; and being tongueless, no taste-perception;

children.text: nityavijñānarūpasya jñānājñāne na me sadā // SamUpad_I,13.5 //
children.translated_text: for one whose nature is eternal consciousness, neither knowledge nor ignorance ever belong to me. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.5 //

children.text: yā tu syān mānasī vṛttiś cākṣuṣkā rūparañjanā /
children.translated_text: Whatever mental modification there may be, or visual [modification] colored by form—

children.text: nityam evātmano dṛṣṭyā nityayā dṛśyate hi sā // SamUpad_I,13.6 //
children.translated_text: it is always seen by the Self's eternal seeing; indeed, it is seen [by that eternal seeing]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.6 //

children.text: tathānyendriyayuktā yā vṛttayo viṣayāñjanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, those [modifications] connected with other senses, mental modifications colored by sense-objects,

children.text: smṛtī rāgādirūpa ca kevalāntar manasy api // SamUpad_I,13.7 //
children.translated_text: memory, and those of the nature of desire and the like, even within the mind alone— // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.7 //

children.text: mānasyas tadvad anyasya dṛśyante svapnavṛttayaḥ /
children.translated_text: those of the mind, like those of any other [organ], are seen, [like] dream-modifications;

children.text: draṣṭur dṛṣṭis tato nityā śuddhānantā ca kevalā // SamUpad_I,13.8 //
children.translated_text: the seeing of the seer is therefore eternal, pure, infinite, and absolute. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,13.8 //

children.text: anityā sāviśuddheti gṛhyate 'trāvivekataḥ /
children.translated_text: She [the intellect] is grasped as impermanent and impure due to non-discrimination here;

children.text: sukhī duḥkhī tathā cāhaṃ dṛśyayopādhibhūtayā // SamUpad_I,13.9 //
children.translated_text: and 'I am happy, I am unhappy'—so one thinks, because she [the intellect], being an <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct), is an object of perception. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.9 //

children.text: mūḍhayā mūḍha ity evaṃ śuddhayā śuddha ity api /
children.translated_text: When she is deluded, 'I am deluded'; when she is pure, 'I am pure'—

children.text: manyate sarvaloko 'yaṃ yena saṃsāram ṛcchati // SamUpad_I,13.10 //
children.translated_text: thus this entire world thinks, by which it enters <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.10 //

children.text: acakṣuṣṭvādiśāstroktaṃ sabāhyābhyantaraṃ hy ajam /
children.translated_text: As declared by scripture to be without eyes and so on, both external and internal, unborn—

children.text: nityamuktam ihātmānaṃ mumukṣuś cet sadā smaret // SamUpad_I,13.11 //
children.translated_text: the one seeking liberation should always remember the Self here as eternally free. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.11 //

children.text: acakṣuṣṭvādiśāstrāc ca nendriyāṇi sadā mama /
children.translated_text: And from the scripture declaring it to be without eyes and so on, the senses are never mine.

children.text: aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhra iti cātharvaṇe vacaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.12 //
children.translated_text: 'Without breath, without mind, pure'—thus is the word of the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> [Upaniṣad]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.12 //

children.text: śabdādīnām abhāvaś ca śrūyate mama kāṭhake /
children.translated_text: And the absence of sound and other sense-objects for me is heard in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [Upaniṣad].

children.text: aprāṇo hy amanā yasmād avikārī sadā hy aham // SamUpad_I,13.13 //
children.translated_text: Since I am without breath and without mind, I am always without modification. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.13 //

children.text: vikṣepo nāsti tasmān me na samādhis tato mama /
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no distraction for me, nor concentration for me.

children.text: vikṣepo vā samādhir vā manasaḥ syād vikāriṇaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.14 //
children.translated_text: Distraction or concentration would belong to the mind, which is subject to modification. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.14 //

children.text: amanaskasya śuddhasya kathaṃ tat syād dvayaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: How could that duality exist for me, who am mindless and pure?

children.text: amanastvāvikāritve videhavyāpino mama // SamUpad_I,13.15 //
children.translated_text: Since I am mindless and without modification, bodiless and all-pervading. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.15 //

children.text: ity etad yāvad ajñānaṃ tāvat kāryaṃ mamābhavat /
children.translated_text: Thus, so long as there was ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), so long was there action for me.

children.text: nityamuktasya śuddhasya buddhasya ca sadā mama // SamUpad_I,13.16 //
children.translated_text: For me, who am eternally free, pure, and always awakened— // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.16 //

children.text: samādhir vāsamādhir vā kāryaṃ vānyat kuto bhavet /
children.translated_text: how could there be concentration, non-concentration, or any other duty?

children.text: maṃ hi dhyātvā ca buddhvā ca manyante kṛtakṛtyatām // SamUpad_I,13.17 //
children.translated_text: For by meditating on me and by knowing me, they consider themselves to have accomplished their purpose. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.17 //

children.text: ahaṃ brahmāsmi sarvo 'smi śuddho buddho 'sitaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: I am <s>Brahman</s>, I am all, pure, awakened, unattached always.

children.text: ajaḥ sarvaga evāham ajaraś cāmṛto 'kṣayaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.18 //
children.translated_text: I am unborn, all-pervading indeed, undecaying, immortal, and imperishable. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.18 //

children.text: madanyaḥ sarvabhūteṣu boddhā kaścin na vidyate /
children.translated_text: No knower other than me is found among all beings.

children.text: karmādhyakṣaś ca sākṣī ca cetā nityo 'guṇo 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.19 //
children.translated_text: I am the overseer of actions, the witness, the conscious one, eternal, without qualities, non-dual. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.19 //

children.text: na sac cāhaṃ na cāsac ca nobhayaṃ kevalaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am neither existent nor non-existent, nor both—I am absolute, auspicious (<s>śiva</s>).

children.text: na me saṃdhyā na rātrir vā nāhar vā sarvadā dṛśeḥ // SamUpad_I,13.20 //
children.translated_text: There is no twilight for me, no night, and no day, for I am always pure awareness. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.20 //

children.text: sarvamūrtiviyuktaṃ yad yathā khaṃ sūkṣmam advayam /
children.translated_text: That which is devoid of all forms, subtle, non-dual, like space—

children.text: tenāpy asmi vinābhūtaṃ brahmaivāhaṃ tathādvayam // SamUpad_I,13.21 //
children.translated_text: I am beyond even that; I am <s>Brahman</s> itself, likewise non-dual. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.21 //

children.text: mamātmāsya ta ātmeti bhedo vyomno yathā bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'My Self, his Self'—just as there would be a division of space

children.text: ekasya suṣibhedena tathā mama vikalpitaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.22 //
children.translated_text: by cavities within one [space], so the differentiation in me is merely imagined. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.22 //

children.text: bhedo 'bhedas tathā caiko nānā ceti vikalpitam /
children.translated_text: Difference and non-difference, oneness and multiplicity—all this is imagined.

children.text: jñeyaṃ jñātā gatir gantā mayy ekasmin kuto bhavet // SamUpad_I,13.23 //
children.translated_text: How could the knowable, the knower, the path, and the traveler exist in me who am one? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.23 //

children.text: na me heyaṃ na cādeyam avikārī yato hy aham /
children.translated_text: There is nothing to be rejected nor accepted by me, since I am without modification.

children.text: sadā muktas tathā śuddhaḥ sadā buddho 'guṇo 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,13.24 //
children.translated_text: Always free, likewise pure, always awakened, without qualities, non-dual. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.24 //

children.text: ity evaṃ sarvadātmānaṃ vidyāt sarvaṃ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus one should always know the Self in all, with concentrated mind.

children.text: viditvā māṃ svadehastham ṛṣir mukto dhruvo bhavet // SamUpad_I,13.25 //
children.translated_text: Having known me as dwelling in one's own body, the sage becomes assuredly liberated. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.25 //

children.text: kṛtakṛtyaś ca siddhaś ca yogī brāhmaṇa eva ca /
children.translated_text: One is fulfilled, accomplished, a <s>yogin</s>, and a true <s>brāhmaṇa</s>

children.text: yadaivaṃ veda tattvārtham anyathā hy ātmahā bhavet // SamUpad_I,13.26 //
children.translated_text: when one thus knows the truth of reality; otherwise, one would be a slayer of the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.26 //

children.text: vedārtho niścito hy eṣa samāsena mayoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the established meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, declared by me in brief.

children.text: saṃnyāsibhyaḥ pravaktavyaḥ śāntebhyaḥ śiṣṭabuddhinā // SamUpad_I,13.27 //
children.translated_text: It is to be taught by one of refined understanding to <s>saṃnyāsins</s> (renunciants) who are at peace. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13.27 //

body.text: ity acakṣuṣṭvaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,13 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Acakṣuṣṭva-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Being Without Eyes). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.13 //

children.text: svapnasmṛtyor ghaṭāder hi rūpābhāsaḥ pradṛśyate /
children.translated_text: In dream and in memory, an appearance of forms such as a pot is perceived;

children.text: purā nūnaṃ tadākarā dhīr dṛṣṭety anumīyate // SamUpad_I,14.1 //
children.translated_text: it is thus inferred that formerly the intellect, having taken that form, was indeed perceived. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.1 //

children.text: bhikṣām aṭan yathā svapne dṛṣṭo deho na sa svayam /
children.translated_text: Just as the body seen in a dream wandering for alms is not oneself,

children.text: jāgraddṛśyāt tathā dehād draṣṭṛtvād anya eva saḥ // SamUpad_I,14.2 //
children.translated_text: so too he [the Self] is different from the body seen in the waking state, because he is the seer. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.2 //

children.text: mūṣāsiktaṃ yathā tāmraṃ tannibhaṃ jāyate tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as copper poured into a mold takes on the shape of that mold,

children.text: rūpādīn vyāpnuvac cittaṃ tannibhaṃ dṛśyate dhruvam // SamUpad_I,14.3 //
children.translated_text: so too the mind, pervading forms and other objects, is certainly seen to assume their likeness. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.3 //

children.text: vyañjako vā yathāloko vyaṅgyasyākāratām iyāt /
children.translated_text: Or just as light, the revealer, assumes the form of what it reveals,

children.text: sarvārthavyañjakatvād dhīr arthākarā pradṛśyate // SamUpad_I,14.4 //
children.translated_text: so too the intellect, being the revealer of all objects, appears to take on the form of objects. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.4 //

children.text: dhir evārthasvarūpā hi puṃsā dṛṣṭā purāpi ca /
children.translated_text: Indeed, the intellect itself, having the nature of objects, was perceived by the person previously too;

children.text: na cet svapne kathaṃ paśyet smarato vākṛtiḥ kutaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.5 //
children.translated_text: if not, how could one see them in a dream, and whence would form arise for one who remembers? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.5 //

children.text: vyañjakatvaṃ tad evāsya rūpādyākāradṛśyatā /
children.translated_text: Its revealing nature is precisely this—being seen in the form of color and other objects;

children.text: draṣṭṛtvaṃ ca dṛśes tadvad vyāptiḥ syād dhiya udbhave // SamUpad_I,14.6 //
children.translated_text: and the seer-ship of awareness is likewise its pervading power when the intellect arises. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.6 //

children.text: cinmātrajyotiṣā sarvaḥ sarvadeheṣu buddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since all cognitions in all bodies are illuminated by me,

children.text: mayā yasmāt prakāśyante sarvasyātmā tato hy aham // SamUpad_I,14.7 //
children.translated_text: the light of pure consciousness (<s>cinmātra</s>), therefore I am indeed the Self of all. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.7 //

children.text: karaṇaṃ karma kartā ca kriyā svapne phalaṃ ca dhīḥ /
children.translated_text: The instrument, the action, the agent, the activity, the result, and the cognition are all seen in dream;

children.text: jāgraty evaṃ yato dṛṣṭā draṣṭā tasmāt tato 'nyathā // SamUpad_I,14.8 //
children.translated_text: since the seer is likewise seen in the waking state, therefore he [the true seer] is different from these. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.8 //

children.text: buddhyādīnām anātmatvaṃ heyopādeyarūpataḥ /
children.translated_text: The non-selfhood of the intellect and so on is established from their nature as things to be rejected and accepted.

children.text: hānopādānakartātmā na tyājyo na ca gṛhyate // SamUpad_I,14.9 //
children.translated_text: The Self, the agent of rejection and acceptance, is itself neither to be rejected nor to be grasped. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.9 //

children.text: sabāhyābhyantare śuddhe prajñānaikarase ghane /
children.translated_text: When both external and internal are pure, of one taste of <s>prajñāna</s> (pure consciousness), dense with awareness—

children.text: bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ cānyat kathaṃ heyaṃ prakalpyate // SamUpad_I,14.10 //
children.translated_text: how can external, internal, or any other thing be imagined as something to be rejected? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.10 //

children.text: ya ātmā neti netīti parāpohena śeṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Self that remains after the removal of all else through '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this)—

children.text: sa ced brahmavidātmeṣṭo yatetātaḥ paraṃ katham // SamUpad_I,14.11 //
children.translated_text: if that is acknowledged as the Self by the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, how could one strive for anything beyond this? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.11 //

children.text: aśanāyādyatikrāntaṃ brahmaivāsmi nirantaram /
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Brahman</s> itself, beyond hunger and the rest, without interruption'—

children.text: kāryavān syāṃ kathaṃ cāhaṃ vimṛśed evam añjasā // SamUpad_I,14.12 //
children.translated_text: one should reflect thus directly: 'How could I have any duty to perform?' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.12 //

children.text: pāragas tu yathā nadyās tatsthaḥ paraṃ yiyāsati /
children.translated_text: Just as one who has reached the other shore of a river, while standing there, would absurdly wish to cross to the other shore again,

children.text: ātmajñaś cet tathā kāryaṃ kartum anyad ihecchati // SamUpad_I,14.13 //
children.translated_text: so too, if a knower of the Self should desire to perform some other duty here. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.13 //

children.text: ātmajñasyāpi yasya syād dhānopādānatā yadi /
children.translated_text: If even for one who has Self-knowledge there were the notion of rejection and acceptance,

children.text: na mokṣārhaḥ sa vijñeyo vānto 'sau brahmaṇā dhruvam // SamUpad_I,14.14 //
children.translated_text: he should be understood as not worthy of liberation—he has surely been cast out by <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.14 //

children.text: sādityaṃ hi jagat prāṇas tasmān nāhar niśaiva vā /
children.translated_text: The vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) illuminates the world together with the sun; therefore there is neither day nor night for it.

children.text: prāṇajñasyāpi na syātāṃ kuto brahmavido 'dvaye // SamUpad_I,14.15 //
children.translated_text: If even for the knower of <s>prāṇa</s> these do not exist, how much less for the knower of non-dual <s>Brahman</s>? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.15 //

children.text: na smaraty ātmano hy ātmā vismared vāpy aluptacit /
children.translated_text: The Self does not remember itself, nor does it forget, for its consciousness is unbroken.

children.text: mano 'pi smaratīty etaj jñānam ajñānahetujam // SamUpad_I,14.16 //
children.translated_text: 'Even the mind remembers'—this knowledge is born of ignorance. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.16 //

children.text: jñātur jñeyaḥ paro hy ātmā so 'vidyākalpitaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The supreme Self, as an object to be known by a knower, is regarded as a superimposition of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: apoḍhe vidyayā tasmin rajjvāṃ sarpa ivādvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.17 //
children.translated_text: When that superimposition is removed by knowledge, the Self is non-dual—like the rope when the snake upon it is negated. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.17 //

children.text: kartṛkarmaphalābhāvāt sabāhyābhyantaraṃ hy ajam /
children.translated_text: Since there is no agent, action, or result, the Self is both external and internal, and unborn.

children.text: mamāhaṃ ceti yo bhāvas tasmin kasya kuto bhavet // SamUpad_I,14.18 //
children.translated_text: In that Self, for whom and whence could the notions of 'mine' and 'I' arise? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.18 //

children.text: ātmā hy ātmīya ity eṣa bhāvo 'vidyāprakalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The Self' and 'belonging to the Self'—this notion is fabricated by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: ātmaikatve hy asau nāsti bījabhāve kutaḥ phalam // SamUpad_I,14.19 //
children.translated_text: When the Self is known to be one, that notion does not exist; when there is no seed, whence the fruit? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.19 //

children.text: draṣṭṛ srotṛ tathā mantṛ vijñātṛ eva tad akṣaram /
children.translated_text: The seer, the hearer, the thinker, the knower—that alone is the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>).

children.text: draṣṭrādyanyan na tad yasmāt tasmād draṣṭāham akṣaram // SamUpad_I,14.20 //
children.translated_text: Since that Imperishable is not other than the seer and so on, therefore I, the seer, am the Imperishable. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.20 //

children.text: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva draṣṭṛtvādikriyāyutam /
children.translated_text: The stationary and the moving, endowed with the activities of seeing and so on—

children.text: sarvam akṣaram evātaḥ sarvasyātmākṣaraṃ tv aham // SamUpad_I,14.21 //
children.translated_text: all this is indeed the Imperishable. Therefore I, the Imperishable, am the Self of all. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.21 //

children.text: akāryaśeṣam ātmānam akriyātmakriyāphalam /
children.translated_text: He who sees the Self as having no remaining duty, free from action, with action and its results belonging to the non-Self,

children.text: nirmamaṃ nirahaṃkāraṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati // SamUpad_I,14.22 //
children.translated_text: without possessiveness, without ego—he truly sees. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.22 //

children.text: mamāhaṃkārayatnecchāḥ śūnyā eva svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Mine,' ego, effort, and desire are by nature empty in the Self.

children.text: ātmanīti yadi jñātam ādhvaṃ svasthāḥ kim īhitaiḥ // SamUpad_I,14.23 //
children.translated_text: If this is known, then being established in oneself, what need is there for striving? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.23 //

children.text: yo 'haṃkartāram ātmānaṃ tathā vettāram eva yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who knows the Self as the agent of 'I'-sense and likewise as the knower—

children.text: vetty anātmajña evāsau yo 'nyathājñaḥ sa ātmavit // SamUpad_I,14.24 //
children.translated_text: he is indeed a non-knower of the Self; he who knows otherwise, though seemingly ignorant, he is the true knower of the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.24 //

children.text: yathānyatve 'pi tādātmyaṃ dehādiṣv ātmano matam /
children.translated_text: Just as identity of the Self with the body and so on is wrongly assumed despite their being different,

children.text: tathākartur avijñānāt phalakarmātmatātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.25 //
children.translated_text: so too, through ignorance of the Self as non-doer, the selfhood of results and actions is falsely attributed to the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.25 //

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ śrutir matir jñātiḥ svapne dṛṣṭā janaiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing are always observed by people in dreams.

children.text: tāsām ātmasvarūpatvād ataḥ pratyakṣatātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.26 //
children.translated_text: Since these are of the nature of the Self, therefore the Self is self-evident (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.26 //

children.text: paralokabhayaṃ yasya nāsti mṛtyubhayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: For one who has no fear of the next world, nor fear of death—

children.text: tasyātmajñasya śocyaḥ syuḥ sabrahmendrā apīśvarāḥ // SamUpad_I,14.27 //
children.translated_text: for that knower of the Self, even the lords including <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s> would be objects of pity. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.27 //

children.text: īśvaratvena kiṃ tasya brahmendratvena vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of what use is lordship to him, or the status of <s>Brahmā</s> or <s>Indra</s>?

children.text: tṛṣṇā cet sarvataś chinnā sarvadainyodbhavāśubhā // SamUpad_I,14.28 //
children.translated_text: For craving—the inauspicious source of all wretchedness—has been cut off from all sides. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.28 //

children.text: aham ity ātmadhīr yā ca mamety ātmīyadhīr api /
children.translated_text: When the notion of 'I' pertaining to the Self and the notion of 'mine' pertaining to what belongs to the Self

children.text: arthaśūnye yadā yasya sa ātmajño bhavet tadā // SamUpad_I,14.29 //
children.translated_text: are both devoid of real content for someone, then he becomes a knower of the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.29 //

children.text: buddhyādau saty upādhau ca tathāsaty aviśeṣatā /
children.translated_text: For one who has known the Self as being the same whether the <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct) of intellect and so on exists or does not—

children.text: yasya ced ātmano jñātā tasya kāryaṃ kathaṃ bhavet // SamUpad_I,14.30 //
children.translated_text: how could there be any duty for him? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.30 //

children.text: prasanne vimale vyomni prajñānaikarase 'dvaye /
children.translated_text: In the serene, stainless space of consciousness, of one taste of <s>prajñāna</s> (pure awareness), non-dual—

children.text: utpannātmadhiyo brūta kim anyat kāryam iṣyate // SamUpad_I,14.31 //
children.translated_text: tell me, for those in whom Self-knowledge has arisen, what other duty is desired? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.31 //

children.text: ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtastham amitraṃ cātmano 'pi yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, seeing the Self dwelling in all beings, yet treats even his own Self as an enemy—

children.text: paśyann icchaty asau nūnaṃ śītīkartuṃ vibhāvasum // SamUpad_I,14.32 //
children.translated_text: he surely wishes to cool down fire itself. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.32 //

children.text: prajñāprāṇānukāry ātmā chāyevākṣādigocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The Self, like a shadow, appears to follow the movements of intelligence and vital breath, appearing as the object of the eye and other senses.

children.text: dhyāyatīveti cokto hi śuddho muktaḥ svato hi saḥ // SamUpad_I,14.33 //
children.translated_text: It is said to 'meditate, as it were'—for it is by nature pure and free. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.33 //

children.text: aprāṇasyāmanaskasya tathāsaṃsargiṇo dṛśeḥ /
children.translated_text: For me, who am without breath, without mind, unassociated, pure awareness,

children.text: vyomavad vyāpino hy asya kathaṃ kāryaṃ bhaven mama // SamUpad_I,14.34 //
children.translated_text: all-pervading like space—how could there be any duty? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.34 //

children.text: asamādhiṃ na paśyāmi nirvikārasya sarvadā /
children.translated_text: I see no absence of concentration for me, who am <s>Brahman</s>, ever without modification,

children.text: brahmaṇo me viśuddhasya śodhyaṃ cānyad vipāpmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.35 //
children.translated_text: supremely pure and free from evil—nor is there anything else to be purified. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.35 //

children.text: gantavyaṃ ca tathaivāhaṃ sarvagasyācalasya ca /
children.translated_text: And likewise there is no destination for me, who am all-pervading and immovable—

children.text: nordhvaṃ nādhas tiro vāpi niṣkalasyāguṇatvataḥ // SamUpad_I,14.36 //
children.translated_text: neither above, nor below, nor across—since I am without parts and without qualities. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.36 //

children.text: cinmātrajyotiṣo nityaṃ tamas tasmin na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For the light of pure consciousness, eternal—darkness is never found in it.

children.text: kathaṃ kāryaṃ mamaivādya nityamuktasya śiṣyate // SamUpad_I,14.37 //
