children.translated_text: How could any duty remain now for me, who am eternally free? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.37 //

children.text: amanaskasya kā cintā kriyā vānindriyasya kā /
children.translated_text: What thought can there be for one without mind? What action for one without senses?

children.text: aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhra iti satyaṃ śruter vacaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.38 //
children.translated_text: 'Without breath, without mind, pure'—true indeed is the word of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.38 //

children.text: akālatvād adeśatvād adiktvād animittataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the Self is timeless, placeless, directionless, and without cause,

children.text: ātmano naiva kālāder apekṣā dhyāyataḥ sadā // SamUpad_I,14.39 //
children.translated_text: the Self, ever meditating, has no dependence on time and the rest. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.39 //

children.text: yasmin devāś ca vedāś ca pavitraṃ kṛtsnam ekatām /
children.translated_text: That in which the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, and all that is sacred become one—

children.text: vrajet tan mānasaṃ tīrthaṃ yasmin snātvāmṛto bhavet // SamUpad_I,14.40 //
children.translated_text: that is the mental pilgrimage place (<s>tīrtha</s>), bathing in which one becomes immortal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.40 //

children.text: na cāsti śabdādir ananyavedanaḥ paraspareṇāpi na caiva dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Sound and the like do not exist as self-known; nor are they perceived by one another.

children.text: pareṇa dṛśyās tu yathā rasādayas tathaiva dṛśyatvata eva daihikāḥ // SamUpad_I,14.41 //
children.translated_text: Just as taste and other qualities are perceived by something other than themselves, so too bodily constituents are objects precisely because of their perceivable nature. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.41 //

children.text: ahaṃ mamety eṣaṇayatnavikriyāḥ sukhādayas tadvad iha pradṛśyataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I,' 'mine,' desire, effort, modifications, pleasure and the rest—these likewise are perceived here.

children.text: dṛśyatvayogāc ca paraspareṇa te na dṛśyatāṃ yānti tataḥ paro bhavet // SamUpad_I,14.42 //
children.translated_text: And since they are objects of perception, they do not perceive one another; therefore there must be something transcendent. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.42 //

children.text: ahaṃkriyādyā hi samastavikriyā sakartṛkā karmaphalena saṃhitā /
children.translated_text: The ego-activity and all other modifications, having an agent and connected with the fruit of action,

children.text: citisvarūpeṇa samantato 'rkavat prakāśyamānāsitatātmano hy ataḥ // SamUpad_I,14.43 //
children.translated_text: are entirely illuminated by the nature of pure consciousness (<s>citi</s>) like objects by the sun on all sides; therefore the Self is of untainted nature. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.43 //

children.text: dṛśisvarūpeṇa hi sarvadehināṃ viyad yathā vyāpya manāṃsy avasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the very nature of awareness, pervading the minds of all embodied beings like space, the Self abides.

children.text: ato na tasmād aparo 'sti veditā paro 'pi tasmād ata eka īśvaraḥ // SamUpad_I,14.44 //
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no knower other than it, nor anything higher; hence it alone is the <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.44 //

children.text: śarīrabuddhyor yadi cānyadṛśyatā nirātmavādāḥ sunirākṛṭā mayā /
children.translated_text: If the perceivability of body and intellect as other than the Self is established, then the doctrines of no-Self have been thoroughly refuted by me.

children.text: paraś ca siddho hy aviśuddhikarmataḥ sunirmalaḥ sarvagato 'sito 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.45 //
children.translated_text: And the transcendent Self is established as free from impure action, supremely stainless, all-pervading, unattached, and non-dual. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.45 //

children.text: ghaṭādirūpaṃ yadi te na gṛhyate manaḥ pravṛttaṃ bahudhā svavṛttibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If the form of a pot and so on is not grasped by you, the mind, engaged in its various functions—

children.text: aśuddhyacidrūpavikāradoṣatā mater yathā vārayituṃ na pāryate // SamUpad_I,14.46 //
children.translated_text: its defects of impurity, non-consciousness, form, and modification cannot be warded off, just as for matter (<s>prakṛti</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.46 //

children.text: yathā viśuddhaṃ gaganaṃ nirantaraṃ na sajjate nāpi ca lipyate tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the pure sky, uninterrupted, is neither attached to nor stained by anything,

children.text: samastabhūteṣu sadaiva teṣv ayaṃ samaḥ sadātmā hy ajaro 'maro 'bhayaḥ // SamUpad_I,14.47 //
children.translated_text: so too this Self, ever the same in all beings, is always equal, undecaying, immortal, and fearless. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.14.47 //

children.text: amūrtamūrtāni ca karmavāsanā dṛśisvarūpasya bahiḥ prakalpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Both the formless and the formed, as well as the latent impressions of action (<s>karmavāsanā</s>), are externally projected upon the one whose nature is pure seeing (<s>dṛśi</s>);

children.text: avidyayā hy ātmani mūḍhadṛṣṭibhir apohya netīty avaśeṣito dṛśiḥ // SamUpad_I,14.48 //
children.translated_text: by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) indeed, upon the Self, by those of deluded vision; negating [them] by '<s>neti</s>' ('not this, not this'), what remains is pure seeing (<s>dṛśi</s>). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,14.48 //

children.text: prabodharūpaṃ manaso 'rthayogajaṃ smṛtau ca suptasya ca dṛśyate 'rthavat /
children.translated_text: The form of awakening, born from the mind's connection with objects, is seen in memory and in the sleeping state, as if [real] objects [were present];

children.text: tathaiva dehapratimānataḥ pṛthag dṛśeḥ śarīraṃ ca manaś ca dṛśyataḥ // SamUpad_I,14.49 //
children.translated_text: likewise, from the analogy of the body, separately from the Seer (<s>dṛśi</s>), both the body and the mind are objects of perception. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,14.49 //

children.text: svabhāvaśuddhe gagane ghanādike male 'payāte sati cāviśeṣatā /
children.translated_text: Just as in the sky, which is pure by nature, when impurities like clouds and the like have departed, there is no distinction;

children.text: yathā ca tadvac chrutivāritadvaye sadāviśeṣo gaganopame dṛśau // SamUpad_I,14.50 //
children.translated_text: so likewise, as declared by the twofold statement of scripture (<s>śruti</s>), there is always no distinction in the Seer (<s>dṛśi</s>), which is like the sky. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,14.50 //

body.text: iti svapnasmṛtiprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,14 //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the chapter on dream and memory. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,14 //

children.text: nānyad anyad bhaved yasmān nānyat kiṃcid vicintayet /
children.translated_text: Since nothing would be other than another, one should not think of anything as 'other';

children.text: anyasyānyatvabhāve hi nāśas tasya dhruvo bhavet // SamUpad_I,15.1 //
children.translated_text: for if otherness existed for anything, its destruction would be certain. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.1 //

children.text: smarato dṛśyate dṛṣṭaṃ paṭe citram ivārpitam /
children.translated_text: What was seen is perceived by one who remembers, like a picture painted on cloth;

children.text: yatra yena ca tau jñeyau sattvakṣetrajñasaṃjñakau // SamUpad_I,15.2 //
children.translated_text: the 'where' and the 'by whom'—those two should be known as designated <s>sattva</s> (being/matter) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.2 //

children.text: phalāntaṃ cānubhūtaṃ yad yuktaṃ kartrādikārakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And what was experienced, ending in its fruit, connected with the agent and other case-relations,

children.text: smaryamāṇaṃ hi karmasthaṃ pūrvaṃ karmaiva tat tataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.3 //
children.translated_text: when being remembered, abides in <s>karma</s>; therefore, that was indeed only <s>karma</s> from the beginning. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.3 //

children.text: draṣṭuś cānyad bhaved dṛśyaṃ dṛśyatvād ghaṭavat sadā /
children.translated_text: And the seen (object) would be other than the Seer, since it is always an object of perception, like a pot;

children.text: dṛśyād draṣṭāsajātīyo na dhīvat sākṣitānyathā // SamUpad_I,15.4 //
children.translated_text: the Seer is of a different kind from the seen; otherwise [it would be] like the intellect, not a witness. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.4 //

children.text: svātmabuddhim apekṣyāsau vidhīnāṃ syāt prayojakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Depending on the notion of self-identity, one would be the executor of [Vedic] injunctions;

children.text: jātyādiḥ śavavat tena tadvan nānātmatānyathā // SamUpad_I,15.5 //
children.translated_text: [but] birth and the like [belong to the body which is] like a corpse; therefore, [asserting] manifoldness of the Self would be like that, otherwise. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.5 //

children.text: na priyāpriya ity ukter nādehatvaṃ kriyāphalam /
children.translated_text: From the statement 'not pleasant, not unpleasant,' [it follows that] the fruit of action does not belong to the non-bodily [Self];

children.text: dehayogaḥ kriyāhetus tasmād vidvān kriyās tyajet // SamUpad_I,15.6 //
children.translated_text: connection with the body is the cause of action; therefore, the wise one should renounce actions. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.6 //

children.text: karmasv ātmā svatantraś cen nivṛttau ca tatheṣyatām /
children.translated_text: If the Self were independent in [performing] actions, let it be accepted as equally so in cessation [from action];

children.text: adehatve phale 'kārye jñāte kuryāt kathaṃ kriyāḥ // SamUpad_I,15.7 //
children.translated_text: when one knows that in the non-bodily [state] the fruit [of action] is without effect, how would one perform actions? // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.7 //

children.text: jātyādin saṃparityajya nimittaṃ karmaṇāṃ budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one, having completely renounced birth and the like, the causes of actions,

children.text: karmahetuviruddhaṃ yat svarūpaṃ śāstrataḥ smaret // SamUpad_I,15.8 //
children.translated_text: should remember from scripture one's own true nature, which is contrary to the causes of action. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.8 //

children.text: ātmaikaḥ sarvabhūteṣu tāni tasmiṃś ca khe yathā /
children.translated_text: The Self is one in all beings, and they [abide] in it, just as in space;

children.text: paryagād vyomavat sarvaṃ śukraṃ dīptimad iṣyate // SamUpad_I,15.9 //
children.translated_text: it pervades all like the sky, luminous and radiant—so it is declared. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.9 //

children.text: vraṇasnāyvor abhāvena sthūlaṃ dehaṃ nivārayet /
children.translated_text: By the absence of wounds and sinews [i.e., the factors binding the self to the gross body], one should negate the gross body;

children.text: śuddhāpāpatayā lepaṃ liṅgaṃ cākāyam ity uta // SamUpad_I,15.10 //
children.translated_text: through [recognizing] purity and freedom from taint, [one should negate] the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) as non-body, it is said. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.10 //

children.text: vāsudevo yathāśvatthe svadehe cābravit samam /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Vāsudeva</s> declared [himself to be] equal in the <s>aśvattha</s> tree and in his own body,

children.text: tadvad vetti ya ātmānaṃ samaṃ sa brahmavittamaḥ // SamUpad_I,15.11 //
children.translated_text: so too, one who knows the Self as equal [in all]—he is the greatest knower of <s>Brahman</s>. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.11 //

children.text: yathā hy anyaśarīreṣu mamāhantā na ceṣyate /
children.translated_text: Just as in other bodies, my sense of 'I' and 'mine' is not accepted,

children.text: asmiṃś cāpi tathā dehe dhīsākṣitvāviśeṣataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.12 //
children.translated_text: so too in this body, because there is no difference [in the Self's being] the witness of the intellect. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.12 //

children.text: rūpasaṃskāratulyādhi rāgadveṣau bhayaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: Attachment, aversion, and fear, which are afflictions comparable to form and mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>),

children.text: gṛhyate dhīśrayaṃ tasmāj jñātā śuddho 'bhayaḥ sadā // SamUpad_I,15.13 //
children.translated_text: are apprehended as depending on the intellect; therefore, the knower is always pure and fearless. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.13 //

children.text: yanmanās tanmayo 'nyatve nātmatvāptau kriyātmani /
children.translated_text: [The Self] becomes identified with whatever the mind [dwells on]; but in otherness, [there would be] no attainment of selfhood; and in the active self,

children.text: ātmatve cānapekṣatvāt sāpekṣaṃ hi na tat svayam // SamUpad_I,15.14 //
children.translated_text: if selfhood [is intrinsic], there is no dependence; for what is dependent is not itself [the Self]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.14 //

children.text: kham ivaikarasā jñaptir avibhaktājarāmalā /
children.translated_text: Consciousness (<s>jñapti</s>), like space, is of one essence, undivided, free from old age and impurity;

children.text: cakṣurādyupadhānāt sā viparītā vibhāvyate // SamUpad_I,15.15 //
children.translated_text: through the superimposition of the eye and other [sense organs], it is conceived as the opposite [i.e., as diverse and limited]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.15 //

children.text: dṛśyatvād aham ity eṣa nātmadharmo ghaṭādivat /
children.translated_text: Because it is an object of perception, this [notion of] 'I' is not a property of the Self, just like a pot and the like;

children.text: tathānye pratyayā jñeyā doṣāś cātmāmalo hy ataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.16 //
children.translated_text: likewise, other cognitions should be known [as non-Self], as well as defects—for the Self is stainless. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.16 //

children.text: sarvapratyayasākṣitvād avikārī ca sarvagaḥ /
children.translated_text: Being the witness of all cognitions, [the Self] is unchanging and all-pervading;

children.text: vikriyeta yadi draṣṭā buddhyādīvālpavid bhavet // SamUpad_I,15.17 //
children.translated_text: if the Seer were to undergo modification, it would be of limited knowledge, like the intellect and the rest. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.17 //

children.text: na dṛṣṭir lupyate draṣṭuś cakṣurāder yathaiva tu /
children.translated_text: The vision of the Seer is never destroyed, just as [vision persists] despite [the loss of] the eye and other [organs];

children.text: nahi draṣṭur iti hy uktaṃ tasmād draṣṭā sadaiva bhuk // SamUpad_I,15.18 //
children.translated_text: for it is said 'the vision of the Seer [is never lost]'; therefore, the Seer is ever the experiencer. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.18 //

children.text: saṃghāto vāsmi bhūtānāṃ karaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: 'Am I an aggregate of elements, or likewise of sense organs,

children.text: vyastaṃ vānyatamo vāsmi ko āsmīti vicārayet // SamUpad_I,15.19 //
children.translated_text: or am I one of them taken separately, or some other?'—thus one should inquire 'Who am I?' // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.19 //

children.text: vyastaṃ nāhaṃ samastaṃ vā bhūtam indriyam eva vā /
children.translated_text: 'I am neither [any element] taken separately, nor the aggregate, neither an element nor a sense organ;

children.text: jñeyatvāt karaṇatvāc ca jñātānyo 'smād ghaṭādivat // SamUpad_I,15.20 //
children.translated_text: because [they are] objects of knowledge and instruments, the knower is other than these, like a pot and the like.' // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.20 //

children.text: ātmāgner indhanā buddhir avidyākāmakarmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The intellect is the fuel for the fire of the Self; by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), desire, and action,

children.text: dīpitā prajvalaty eṣa dvāraiḥ śrotrādibhiḥ sadā // SamUpad_I,15.21 //
children.translated_text: being ignited, this [fire] blazes forth always through the gates of the ear and other [senses]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.21 //

children.text: dakṣiṇākṣipradhāneṣu yadā buddhir viceṣṭate /
children.translated_text: When the intellect operates predominantly through the right eye [and other organs],

children.text: viṣayair haviṣā dīptā ātmāgniḥ sthūlabhuk tadā // SamUpad_I,15.22 //
children.translated_text: kindled by sense-objects as oblations, then the fire of the Self is the <s>sthūlabhuk</s> (gross experiencer / <s>Vaiśvānara</s>). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.22 //

children.text: hūyante tu havīṃṣīti rūpādigrahaṇe smaran /
children.translated_text: Remembering that 'oblations are offered' when grasping form and other [sense-objects],

children.text: arāgadveṣa ātmāgnau jāgraddoṣair na lipyate // SamUpad_I,15.23 //
children.translated_text: one who is free from attachment and aversion is not tainted by the defects of the waking state in the fire of the Self. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.23 //

children.text: mānase tu gṛhe vyaktā avidyākarmavāsanāḥ /
children.translated_text: But in the mental abode, the latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of ignorance and action manifest;

children.text: paśyaṃs taijasa ātmoktaḥ svayaṃjyotiḥprakāśitāḥ // SamUpad_I,15.24 //
children.translated_text: the Self who perceives [them], illuminated by its own self-luminous light, is called <s>taijasa</s> (the luminous one). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.24 //

children.text: viṣayā vāsanā vāpi codyante naiva karmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: When neither sense-objects nor latent impressions are impelled by actions

children.text: yadā buddhau tadā jñeyaḥ prājña ātmā hy ananyadṛk // SamUpad_I,15.25 //
children.translated_text: in the intellect, then the Self should be known as <s>prājña</s> (the cognizer in deep sleep), for it sees nothing other [than itself]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.25 //

children.text: manobuddhīndriyāṇāṃ yā avasthāḥ karmacoditāḥ /
children.translated_text: The states of the mind, intellect, and sense organs, which are impelled by <s>karma</s>,

children.text: caitanyenaiva bhāsyante raviṇeva ghaṭādayaḥ // SamUpad_I,15.26 //
children.translated_text: are illuminated by consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) alone, just as pots and the like [are illuminated] by the sun. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.26 //

children.text: tatraivaṃ sati buddhīr jña ātmabhāsāvabhāsayan /
children.translated_text: This being so, the knower, illuminating the intellects by the light of the Self,

children.text: kartā tāsāṃ yadarthās tā mūḍhair evābhidhīyate // SamUpad_I,15.27 //
children.translated_text: is said by the deluded to be their agent and the one for whose purpose they [function]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.27 //

children.text: sarvajño 'py ata eva syāt svena bhāsāvabhāsayan /
children.translated_text: For this very reason it would also be omniscient, illuminating [all] by its own light;

children.text: sarvaṃ sarvakriyāhetoḥ sarvakṛttvaṃ tathātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,15.28 //
children.translated_text: [its] all-doing nature likewise [arises] because it is the cause of all activities of everything. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.28 //

children.text: sopādhiś caivam ātmokto nirupākhyo 'nupādhikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the Self with limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) has been described; without adjuncts, it is beyond designation,

children.text: niṣkalo nirguṇaḥ śuddhas taṃ mano vāk ca nāpnutaḥ // SamUpad_I,15.29 //
children.translated_text: without parts, without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), pure—mind and speech do not reach it. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.29 //

children.text: cetano 'cetano vāpi kartākartā gato 'gataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether conscious or unconscious, agent or non-agent, gone or not gone,

children.text: baddho muktas tathā caiko naikaḥ śuddho 'nyatheti vā // SamUpad_I,15.30 //
children.translated_text: bound or liberated, one or not one, pure or otherwise— // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.30 //

children.text: aprāpyaiva nivartante vāco dhībhiḥ sahaiva tu /
children.translated_text: words turn back without reaching [it], together with the intellect indeed;

children.text: nirguṇatvāt kriyābhāvād viśeṣāṇāṃ hy abhāvataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.31 //
children.translated_text: because it is without qualities, because there is no activity, because there are no distinctions. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.31 //

children.text: vyāpakaṃ sarvato vyoma mūrtaiḥ sarvair viyojitam /
children.translated_text: Space is all-pervading everywhere, separated from all material forms;

children.text: yathā tadvad ihātmānaṃ vidyāc chuddhaṃ paraṃ padam // SamUpad_I,15.32 //
children.translated_text: just so, one should know the Self here as pure, the supreme abode (<s>paraṃ padam</s>). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.32 //

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ hitvā smṛtiṃ tasmin sarvagraś ca tamas tyajet /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned [clinging to] what is seen and memory thereof, one should relinquish all-consuming darkness [of ignorance];

children.text: sarvadṛg jyotiṣā yukto dinakṛc chārvaraṃ yathā // SamUpad_I,15.33 //
children.translated_text: endowed with the light that sees all, like the sun [dispelling] darkness. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.33 //

children.text: rūpasmṛtyandhakārārthāḥ pratyayā yasya gocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Forms, memories, darkness, and objects—cognitions whose range these are—

children.text: sa evātmā samo draṣṭā sarvabhūteṣu sarvagaḥ // SamUpad_I,15.34 //
children.translated_text: that very Self is the equal Seer, all-pervading in all beings. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.34 //

children.text: ātmabuddhimanaścakṣurviṣayālokasaṃgamāt /
children.translated_text: From the conjunction of the Self, intellect, mind, eye, object, and light,

children.text: vicitro jāyate buddheḥ pratyayo 'jñānalakṣaṇaḥ // SamUpad_I,15.35 //
children.translated_text: a variegated cognition arises in the intellect, characterized by ignorance. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.35 //

children.text: vivicyāsmāt svam ātmānaṃ vidyāc chuddhaṃ paraṃ padam /
children.translated_text: Discriminating from this, one should know one's own Self as pure, the supreme abode (<s>paraṃ padam</s>),

children.text: draṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtasthaṃ samaṃ sarvabhayātigam // SamUpad_I,15.36 //
children.translated_text: the Seer dwelling in all beings, equal, having transcended all fear. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.36 //

children.text: samastaṃ sarvagaṃ śāntaṃ vimalaṃ vyomavat sthitam /
children.translated_text: Complete, all-pervading, tranquil, stainless, abiding like space,

children.text: niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ sarvaṃ nityaṃ dvandvair vivarjitam // SamUpad_I,15.37 //
children.translated_text: without parts, without action, all-encompassing, eternal, free from all pairs of opposites. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.37 //

children.text: sarvapratyayasākṣī jñaḥ kathaṃ jñeyo mayety uta /
children.translated_text: 'The knower, the witness of all cognitions—how is it to be known by me?' one may ask.

children.text: vimṛśyaivaṃ vijānīyāj jñātaṃ brahma na veti vā // SamUpad_I,15.38 //
children.translated_text: Reflecting thus, one should discern whether <s>Brahman</s> is known or not. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.38 //

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭr avijñātaṃ dabhram ityādiśāsanāt /
children.translated_text: From the scriptural teaching 'the unseen Seer, the unknown, the minute,' and so forth,

children.text: naiva jñeyaṃ mayānyair vā paraṃ brahma kathaṃcana // SamUpad_I,15.39 //
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is never to be known by me or by others in any way [as an object]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.39 //

children.text: svarūpāvyavadhānābhyāṃ jñānālokasvabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: By virtue of its own nature and the absence of obstruction, being of the nature of the light of knowledge,

children.text: anyajñānānapekṣatvāj jñātaṃ caiva sadā mayā // SamUpad_I,15.40 //
children.translated_text: and because it does not depend on any other knowledge—it is indeed always known by me. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.40 //

children.text: nānyena jyotiṣā kāryaṃ raver ātmaprakāśane /
children.translated_text: No other light is needed for the sun's self-illumination;

children.text: svabodhān nānyabodhecchā bodhasyātmaprakāśane // SamUpad_I,15.41 //
children.translated_text: from self-knowledge, there is no desire for another's knowledge, for consciousness is self-illuminating. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.41 //

children.text: na tasyaivānyato 'pekṣā svarūpaṃ yasya yad bhavet /
children.translated_text: There is no dependence on another for that whose nature is what it is;

children.text: prakāśāntaradṛśyo na prakāśo hy asti kaścana // SamUpad_I,15.42 //
children.translated_text: for there is no light whatsoever that is seen by another light. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.42 //

children.text: vyaktiḥ syād aprakāśasya prakāśātmasamāgamāt /
children.translated_text: The manifestation of the non-luminous would arise from its contact with the luminous self;

children.text: prakāśas tv arkakāryaḥ syād iti mithya vaco hy ataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.43 //
children.translated_text: but [to say] 'light would be an effect of the sun' is a false statement. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.43 //

children.text: yato 'bhūtvā bhaved yac ca tasya tat kāryam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: That which, not having existed [before], comes into being from something—that is considered its effect;

children.text: svarūpatvād abhūtvā na prakāśo jāyate raveḥ // SamUpad_I,15.44 //
children.translated_text: since [light] is the very nature [of the sun], it is not the case that light, having not existed, is born from the sun. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.44 //

children.text: sattāmātre prakāśasya kartādityādir iṣyate /
children.translated_text: With regard to the mere existence of light, the sun and the like are considered its cause;

children.text: ghaṭādivyaktito yadvat tadvad bodhātmanīṣyatām // SamUpad_I,15.45 //
children.translated_text: just as [a lamp causes] the manifestation of a pot and the like, so too let it be accepted regarding the Self whose nature is consciousness (<s>bodha</s>). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.45 //

children.text: bilāt sarpasya niryāṇe sūryo yadvat prakāśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the sun is the illuminator when a serpent emerges from its hole,

children.text: prayatnena vinā tadvaj jñātātmā bodharūpataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.46 //
children.translated_text: so too, without effort, the Self is the knower, by virtue of its nature as consciousness. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.46 //

children.text: dagdhaivam uṣṇaḥ sattāyāṃ tadvad bodhātmanīṣyatām /
children.translated_text: Just as fire is hot in its very existence, so too let it be accepted for the Self whose nature is consciousness;

children.text: saty eva yad upādhau tu jñāte sarpa ivotthite // SamUpad_I,15.47 //
children.translated_text: when a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) is present, [the Self appears to be] a knower, like a rope [appearing as] a snake when it rises up [before one's vision]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.47 //

children.text: jñātāyatno 'pi tadvaj jñaḥ kartā bhrāmakavad bhavet /
children.translated_text: The knower, even without effort, would [appear to] be a doer, like a magician;

children.text: svarūpeṇa svayaṃ nātmā jñeyo 'jñeyo 'thavā tataḥ // SamUpad_I,15.48 //
children.translated_text: by its own nature, the Self itself is neither knowable nor unknowable. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.48 //

children.text: viditāviditābhyāṃ tad anyad eveti śāsanāt /
children.translated_text: From the scriptural teaching 'that is indeed other than both the known and the unknown,'

children.text: bandhamokṣādayo bhāvās tadvad ātmani kalpitāḥ // SamUpad_I,15.49 //
children.translated_text: bondage, liberation, and other states are likewise superimposed upon the Self. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.49 //

children.text: nāhorātre yathā sūrye prabhārūpāviśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as day and night do not [truly exist] in the sun, because there is no difference in the nature of its light,

children.text: bodharūpāviśeṣān na bodhābodhau tathātmani // SamUpad_I,15.50 //
children.translated_text: so too, because there is no difference in the nature of consciousness, knowledge and ignorance do not [truly exist] in the Self. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.50 //

children.text: yathoktaṃ brahma yo veda hānopādānavarjitam /
children.translated_text: One who knows <s>Brahman</s> as described—free from loss and acquisition—

children.text: yathoktena vidhānena sa satyaṃ naiva jāyate // SamUpad_I,15.51 //
children.translated_text: by the method as taught, truly is never born. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.51 //

children.text: janmamṛtyupravāheṣu patito naiva śaknuyāt /
children.translated_text: One who has fallen into the streams of birth and death can never

children.text: ita uddhartum ātmānaṃ jñānād anyena kenacit // SamUpad_I,15.52 //
children.translated_text: lift oneself up from here by any means other than knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.52 //

children.text: "bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś chidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The knot of the heart is broken, all doubts are cut asunder,

children.text: kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭa" iti śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,15.53 //
children.translated_text: and one's <s>karmas</s> are destroyed when That is seen'—so says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture). // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.53 //

children.text: mamāham ity etad apohya sarvato vimuktadehaṃ padam ambaropamam /
children.translated_text: Having removed everywhere [the notions of] 'mine' and 'I,' [one attains] the state free from the body, like the sky—

children.text: sudṛṣṭaśāstrānumitibhya īritaṃ vimucyate 'smin yadi niścito naraḥ // SamUpad_I,15.54 //
children.translated_text: as declared by direct vision, scripture, and inference; a person is liberated in this, if firmly resolved. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15.54 //

body.text: iti nānyadanyatprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,15 //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the chapter on 'Nothing is Other [than the Self].' // Upadeśasāhasrī I,15 //

children.text: pārthivaḥ kaṭhino dhātur dravo dehe smṛto 'mmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The earthy element is hard; the watery element in the body is remembered as fluid;

children.text: pakticeṣṭāvakāśāḥ syur vahnivāyvambarodbhavāḥ // SamUpad_I,16.1 //
children.translated_text: digestion, movement, and space arise from fire, wind, and ether respectively. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.1 //

children.text: ghrāṇādīni tadarthāś ca pṛthivyādiguṇāḥ kramāt /
children.translated_text: The nose and other [sense organs], and their respective objects, are qualities of earth and the other [elements] in order;

children.text: rūpālokavad iṣṭaṃ hi sajātīyārtham indriyam // SamUpad_I,16.2 //
children.translated_text: for it is accepted that a sense organ [perceives] an object of the same class, like form and light. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.2 //

children.text: buddhyarthāny āhur etāni vākpāṇyādīni karmaṇe /
children.translated_text: These [five organs of knowledge] are said to be for the purpose of cognition; speech, hands, and the rest are for action;

children.text: tadvikalpārtham antasthaṃ mana ekādaśaṃ bhavet // SamUpad_I,16.3 //
children.translated_text: the mind, situated internally, for the purpose of their discrimination, would be the eleventh [organ]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.3 //

children.text: niścayārthā bhaved buddhis tāṃ sarvārthānubhāvinīm /
children.translated_text: The intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) exists for the purpose of determination; that [intellect], which experiences all objects,

children.text: jñātātmoktaḥ svarūpeṇa jyotiṣā vyañjayan sadā // SamUpad_I,16.4 //
children.translated_text: the Self, called the knower, always illuminates by its own inherent light. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.4 //

children.text: vyañjakas tu yathāloko vyaṅgyasyākāratāṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as an illuminator, though assuming the form of what it illuminates,

children.text: vyatikīrṇo 'py asaṃkīrṇas tadvaj jñaḥ pratyayaiḥ sadā // SamUpad_I,16.5 //
children.translated_text: though pervaded, is never mixed [with what it illuminates]—so too the knower [is never mixed] with cognitions, always. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.5 //

children.text: sthito dīpo yathāyatnaḥ prāptaṃ sarvaṃ prakāśayet /
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp, standing without effort, illuminates everything within its reach,

children.text: śabdādyākārabuddhīr jñaḥ prāptās tadvat prapaśyati // SamUpad_I,16.6 //
children.translated_text: so too the knower perceives the intellects that have taken the form of sound and other [objects], when they come [within range]. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.6 //

children.text: śarīrendriyasaṃghāta ātmatvena gatāṃ dhiyam /
children.translated_text: The intellect that has identified [itself] with the aggregate of body and sense organs as the self,

children.text: nityātmajyotiṣā dīptāṃ viśiṃṣanti sukhādayaḥ // SamUpad_I,16.7 //
children.translated_text: illuminated by the eternal light of the Self, is differentiated by pleasure and the like. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.7 //

children.text: śiroduḥkhādinātmānaṃ duḥkhy asmīti hi paśyati /
children.translated_text: Through headache and other [pains], one perceives the Self as 'I am in pain';

children.text: draṣṭānyo duḥkhino dṛśyād draṣṭṛtvac ca na duḥkhy asau // SamUpad_I,16.8 //
children.translated_text: but the Seer is other than the suffering seen; and because of being the Seer, it does not suffer. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.8 //

children.text: duḥkhī syād duḥkhyahaṃmānād duḥkhino darśanān na vā /
children.translated_text: Would one be a sufferer from the ego-notion 'I suffer,' or from the perception of one who suffers?

children.text: saṃhate 'ṅgādibhir draṣṭā duḥkhī duḥkhasya naiva saḥ // SamUpad_I,16.9 //
children.translated_text: Though connected with limbs and the like, the Seer is never a sufferer of suffering. // Upadeśasāhasrī I,16.9 //

children.text: cakṣurvat karmakartṛtvaṃ syāc cen nānekam eva tat /
children.translated_text: If agentship of action were [attributed to the Self] like the eye, that [agentship] would not be just one [i.e., it would be manifold and contradictory]—

children.text: saṃhataṃ ca tato nātmā draṣṭṛtvāt karmatāṃ vrajet // SamUpad_I,16.10 //
children.translated_text: and being composite, the Self, by virtue of being the seer, would not become an object of action. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.10 //

children.text: jñānayatnādyanekatvam ātmano 'pi mataṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If the multiplicity of knowledge, effort, and the like is admitted of the Self also,

children.text: naikajñānaguṇatvāt tu jyotirvat tasya karmatā // SamUpad_I,16.11 //
children.translated_text: then, since it is not the quality of a single cognition, its objecthood [would follow] like light. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.11 //

children.text: jyotiṣo dyotakatve 'pi yadvan nātmaprakāśanam /
children.translated_text: Just as light, even though illuminating, does not illuminate itself,

children.text: bhede 'py evaṃ samatvāj jña ātmānaṃ naiva paśyati // SamUpad_I,16.12 //
children.translated_text: so too, even if [subject and object are] different, due to their equality, the knower does not perceive the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.12 //

children.text: yaddharmā yaḥ padārtho na tasyaiveyāt sa karmatām /
children.translated_text: That entity whose properties belong to it would not itself become an object of action;

children.text: na hy ātmānaṃ dahaty agnis tathā naiva prakāśayet // SamUpad_I,16.13 //
children.translated_text: for fire does not burn itself, and likewise it does not illuminate itself. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.13 //

children.text: etenaivātmanātmano graho buddher nirākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this very [reasoning], the Self's grasping of itself through the intellect has been refuted;

children.text: aṃśo 'py evaṃ samatvād dhi nirbhedatvān na yujyate // SamUpad_I,16.14 //
children.translated_text: even a part [of the Self] likewise, due to their equality and because there is no differentiation, is not logically possible. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.14 //

children.text: śūnyatāpi na yuktaivaṃ buddher anyena dṛśyatā /
children.translated_text: Voidness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is also not tenable in this way — that the intellect is perceived by something other [than itself]

children.text: uktāto ghaṭavat tasyāḥ prāk siddheś ca vikalpataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.15 //
children.translated_text: has been stated; like a pot, [its existence is established] prior to [its] cognition, and through conceptual construction. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.15 //

children.text: avikalpaṃ tad asty eva yat pūrvaṃ syād vikalpataḥ /
children.translated_text: That non-conceptual [reality] certainly exists which would exist prior to conceptualization;

children.text: vikalpotpattihetutvād yady asyaiva ca kāraṇam // SamUpad_I,16.16 //
children.translated_text: and if it is the very cause of the arising of conceptualization, then it is indeed the cause. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.16 //

children.text: ajñānaṃ kalpanāmūlaṃ saṃsārasya niyāmakam /
children.translated_text: Ignorance, the root of conceptual construction, governs <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration);

children.text: hitvātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma vidyān muktaṃ sadābhayam // SamUpad_I,16.17 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned that, one should know the Self as the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, liberated and eternally fearless. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.17 //

children.text: jāgratsvapnau tayor bījaṃ suṣuptākhyaṃ tamomayam /
children.translated_text: Waking and dreaming, and their seed called deep sleep, which is made of darkness —

children.text: anyonyasminn asattvāc ca nāstīty etat trayaṃ tyajet // SamUpad_I,16.18 //
children.translated_text: since each does not exist in the other, one should abandon all three as 'it does not exist.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.18 //

body.text: ātmabuddhimanaścakṣurālokārthādisaṃkarāt

children.text: bhrāntiḥ syād ātmakarmeti kriyāṇāṃ saṃnipātataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.19 //
children.translated_text: the delusion arises that the Self is an agent, from the conflation of [various] activities. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.19 //

body.translated_text: Due to the confusion of the Self, intellect, mind, eye, light, object, and the like,

children.text: nimīlonmīlane sthāne vāyavye te na cakṣuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Closing and opening [of the eyes] belong to the eyelids due to wind [impulse], and are not of the eye;

children.text: prakāśatvān manasy evaṃ buddhau na staḥ prakāśataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.20 //
children.translated_text: being illuminative, they do not belong to the mind either, nor to the intellect, since [these] are [merely] illuminative. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.20 //

children.text: saṃkalpādhyavasāyau tu manobuddhyor yathākramāt /
children.translated_text: Volition and determination belong to the mind and intellect respectively, in due order;

children.text: netaretaradharmatvaṃ sarvaṃ cātmani kalpitam // SamUpad_I,16.21 //
children.translated_text: neither has the properties of the other, and all [such properties] are superimposed on the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.21 //

children.text: sthānāvacchedadṛṣṭiḥ syād indriyāṇāṃ tadātmatām /
children.translated_text: The perception delimited by location [leads one to] identify with the sense-organs;

children.text: gatā dhīs taṃ hi paśyañ jño dehamātra ivekṣyate // SamUpad_I,16.22 //
children.translated_text: the intellect, having assumed their identity, seeing that, the knower appears as if merely the body. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.22 //

children.text: kṣaṇikaṃ hi tad atyarthaṃ dharmamātraṃ nirantaram /
children.translated_text: For that [cognition] is extremely momentary, consisting of mere properties, and continuous [only in appearance];

children.text: sādṛśyād dīpavat taddhīs tacchāntiḥ puruṣārthatā // SamUpad_I,16.23 //
children.translated_text: due to similarity, like a lamp — the cessation of that cognition is the highest human goal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.23 //

children.text: svākārānyāvabhāsaṃ ca yeṣāṃ rūpādi vidyate /
children.translated_text: For those [cognitions] in which form and the like, appearing as their own form and as the appearance of another, exist,

children.text: yeṣāṃ nāsti tataś cānyat pūrvāsaṃgatir ucyate // SamUpad_I,16.24 //
children.translated_text: and for those in which it does not exist — the prior non-connection is stated for those [latter cognitions]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.24 //

children.text: bāhyākāratvato jñapteḥ smṛtyabhāvaḥ sadā kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Since cognition has an external form, memory would always be absent due to momentariness;

children.text: kṣaṇikatvāc ca saṃskāraṃ naivādhatte kvacit tu dhiḥ // SamUpad_I,16.25 //
children.translated_text: and due to being momentary, the cognition can never retain any impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.25 //

children.text: ādhārasyāpy asattvāc ca tulyatānirnimittataḥ /
children.translated_text: And due to the non-existence of a substratum, the equality [of moments] would be without cause;

children.text: sthāne vā kṣaṇikatvasya hānaṃ syān na tad iṣyate // SamUpad_I,16.26 //
children.translated_text: or else, the momentariness would have to be abandoned — but that is not accepted [by the Buddhists]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.26 //

children.text: śānteś cāyatnasiddhatvāt sādhanoktir anarthikā /
children.translated_text: And since cessation is achieved without effort, the mention of means would be purposeless;

children.text: ekaikasmin samāptatvāc chānter anyānapekṣatā // SamUpad_I,16.27 //
children.translated_text: since cessation is complete in each single [moment], it requires nothing else. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.27 //

children.text: apekṣā yadi bhinne 'pi parasaṃtāna iṣyatām /
children.translated_text: If dependence is admitted even in a different [moment], let it be accepted in another's continuum;

children.text: sarvārthe kṣaṇike kasmiṃs tathāpy anyānapekṣatā // SamUpad_I,16.28 //
children.translated_text: even so, when everything is momentary, there would still be no dependence on anything else. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.28 //

children.text: tulyakālasamudbhūtāv itaretarayoginau /
children.translated_text: Two [things] arising at the same time, each connected with the other —

children.text: yogāc ca saṃskṛto yas tu so 'nyaṃ hīkṣitum arhati // SamUpad_I,16.29 //
children.translated_text: the one that is modified by the connection can indeed perceive the other. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.29 //

children.text: mṛṣādhyāsas tu yatra syāt tannāśas tatra no mataḥ /
children.translated_text: But where there is false superimposition, the destruction of that is not our view;

children.text: sarvanāśo bhaved yasya mokṣaḥ kasya phalaṃ vada // SamUpad_I,16.30 //
children.translated_text: if one for whom everything is destroyed [attains liberation], tell — liberation would be the fruit of whom? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.30 //

children.text: asti tāvat svayaṃ nāma jñānaṃ vātmānyad eva vā /
children.translated_text: There certainly exists, by its own nature, something called knowledge — whether it is the Self or something else;

children.text: bhāvābhāvajñatas tasya nābhāvas tv adhigamyate // SamUpad_I,16.31 //
children.translated_text: from the knowledge of its existence and non-existence, its non-existence cannot be ascertained. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.31 //

children.text: yenādhigamyate 'bhāvas tat sat syāt tan na ced bhavet /
children.translated_text: That by which non-existence is ascertained must itself be real; if it were not,

children.text: bhāvābhāvānabhijñatvaṃ lokasya syān na ceṣyate // SamUpad_I,16.32 //
children.translated_text: the world would be ignorant of both existence and non-existence — but that is not accepted. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.32 //

children.text: sad asat sadasac ceti vikalpāt prāg yad iṣyate /
children.translated_text: That which is accepted prior to the conceptual construction of 'existent,' 'non-existent,' and 'both existent and non-existent'

children.text: tad advaitaṃ samatvāt tu nityaṃ cānyad vikalpitāt // SamUpad_I,16.33 //
children.translated_text: is non-dual, due to its equality, and eternal, being different from the conceptually constructed. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.33 //

children.text: vikalpodbhavato 'sattvaṃ svapnadṛśyavad iṣyatām /
children.translated_text: Let the non-existence of [what arises from] conceptual construction be accepted, like objects seen in a dream;

children.text: dvaitasya prāg asattvāc ca sadasattvādikalpanāt // SamUpad_I,16.34 //
children.translated_text: since duality does not exist prior [to conceptualization], the imagining of existence, non-existence, and the like [is baseless]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.34 //

children.text: vācārambhaṇaśāstrāc ca vikārāṇāṃ hy abhāvatā /
children.translated_text: From the scriptural teaching 'mere verbal expression,' the non-existence of modifications [is established];

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum ityāder mama māyeti ca smṛteḥ // SamUpad_I,16.35 //
children.translated_text: from 'he goes from death to death' and the like, and from the <s>smṛti</s> statement 'my <s>māyā</s>.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.35 //

children.text: viśuddhiś cāta evāsya vikalpāc ca vilakṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: And therefore its purity is [established], being different from conceptual construction;

children.text: upādeyo na heyo 'ta ātmā nānyair akalpitaḥ // SamUpad_I,16.36 //
children.translated_text: therefore the Self is to be accepted, not rejected — the Self is not imagined by others. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.36 //

children.text: aprakāśo yathāditye nāsti jyotiḥsvabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as darkness does not exist in the sun due to its nature of being light,

children.text: nityabodhasvarūpatvān nājñānaṃ tadvad ātmani // SamUpad_I,16.37 //
children.translated_text: so too ignorance does not exist in the Self, due to its nature of being eternal consciousness. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.37 //

children.text: tathāvikriyarūpatvān nāvasthāntaram ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, due to its nature being changeless, there is no other state for the Self;

children.text: avasthāntaravattve hi nāśo 'sya syān na saṃśayaḥ // SamUpad_I,16.38 //
children.translated_text: for if there were another state, its destruction would certainly follow — there is no doubt. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.38 //

children.text: mokṣo 'vasthāntaraṃ yasya kṛtakaḥ sa calo hy ataḥ /
children.translated_text: If liberation is another state, it would be produced and therefore transient;

children.text: na saṃyogo viyogo vā mokṣo yuktaḥ kathaṃcana // SamUpad_I,16.39 //
children.translated_text: neither conjunction nor separation is tenable as liberation in any way. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.39 //

children.text: saṃyogasyāpy anityatvād viyogasya tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Since conjunction too is impermanent, and separation likewise,

children.text: gamanāgamane caiva svarūpaṃ tu na hīyate // SamUpad_I,16.40 //
children.translated_text: and even going and coming — the true nature is never diminished. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.40 //

children.text: svarūpasyānimittatvāt sanimittā hi cāpare /
children.translated_text: Since one's own nature is causeless, while other [states] have a cause;

children.text: anupāttaṃ svarūpaṃ hi svenātyaktaṃ tathaiva ca // SamUpad_I,16.41 //
children.translated_text: one's own nature is indeed not acquired, nor is it abandoned by oneself. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.41 //

children.text: svarūpatvān na sarvasya tyaktuṃ śakyo hy ananyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Being one's own nature, it cannot be abandoned by anything, since there is nothing other;

children.text: gṛhītuṃ vā tato nityo 'viṣayatvāpṛthaktvataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.42 //
children.translated_text: nor can it be grasped — therefore it is eternal, being beyond objectification and non-separate. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.42 //

children.text: ātmārthatvāc ca sarvasya nitya ātmaiva kevalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since everything exists for the sake of the Self, the eternal Self alone is pure [reality];

children.text: tyajet tasmāt kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sādhanaiḥ saha mokṣavit // SamUpad_I,16.43 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the knower of liberation should abandon all actions together with their means. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.43 //

children.text: ātmalābhaḥ paro lābha iti śāstropapattayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The attainment of the Self is the supreme attainment — thus say the scriptures and reasoning;

children.text: alābho 'nyātmalābhas tu tyajet tasmād anātmatām // SamUpad_I,16.44 //
children.translated_text: the attainment of the non-Self is indeed non-attainment — therefore one should abandon [identification with] what is not the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.44 //

children.text: guṇānāṃ samabhāvasya bhraṃśo na hy upapadyate /
children.translated_text: The disruption of the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of <s>Prakṛti</s>) is indeed not tenable,

children.text: avidyādeḥ prasuptatvān na cānyo hetur iṣyate // SamUpad_I,16.45 //
children.translated_text: since <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest are in a dormant state, and no other cause is accepted. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.45 //

children.text: itaretarahetutve pravṛttiḥ syāt sadā na vā /
children.translated_text: If they are mutually causal, activity would either always exist or never exist;

children.text: niyamo na pravṛttīnāṃ guṇeṣv ātmani vā bhavet // SamUpad_I,16.46 //
children.translated_text: there would be no regularity of activities either in the <s>guṇas</s> or in the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.46 //

children.text: viśeṣo muktabaddhānāṃ tādarthye ca na yujyate /
children.translated_text: The distinction between the liberated and the bound is not tenable in the [Sāṃkhya] purposefulness [doctrine];

children.text: arthārthinoś ca saṃbandho nārthī jño netaro 'pi vā // SamUpad_I,16.47 //
children.translated_text: and the connection between the one who has a purpose and the purposeful is not [established] — the knower is not a seeker, nor is the other. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.47 //

children.text: pradhānasya ca pārārthyaṃ puruṣasyāvikārataḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) serves another's purpose, given the changelessness of <s>Puruṣa</s>,

children.text: na yuktaṃ sāṃkhyaśāstre 'pi vikāre 'pi na yujyate // SamUpad_I,16.48 //
children.translated_text: is not tenable even in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system, and is not tenable even with modification. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.48 //

children.text: saṃbandhānupapatteś ca prakṛteḥ puruṣasya ca /
children.translated_text: And due to the impossibility of establishing a connection between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>,

children.text: mitho 'yuktaṃ tadarthatvaṃ pradhānasyācititvataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.49 //
children.translated_text: their mutual purposefulness is not tenable, since <s>Pradhāna</s> is unconscious. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.49 //

children.text: kriyotpattau vināśitvaṃ jñānamātre ca pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: In the origination of activity, there would be destruction, and in mere knowledge, [the situation would be] as before;

children.text: nirnimitte tv anirmokṣaḥ pradhānasya prasajyate // SamUpad_I,16.50 //
children.translated_text: but if there is no cause [for cessation], the non-liberation of <s>Pradhāna</s> would follow. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.50 //

children.text: na prakāśyaṃ yathoṣṇatvaṃ jñānenaivaṃ sukhādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as heat is not made manifest [by something else], so pleasure and the like [are not revealed] by knowledge;

children.text: ekanīḍatvato 'grāhyāḥ syuḥ kaṇādādivartmanām // SamUpad_I,16.51 //
children.translated_text: since they share a single locus, they cannot be grasped — [this holds] for the followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and others. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.51 //

children.text: yugapac cāsametatvāt sukhavijñānayor api /
children.translated_text: And since pleasure and cognition do not arise simultaneously,

children.text: manoyogaikahetutvād agrāhyatvaṃ sukhasya ca // SamUpad_I,16.52 //
children.translated_text: and since [both] have the connection with the mind as their single cause, the non-graspability of pleasure [follows]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.52 //

children.text: tathānyeṣāṃ ca bhinnatvād yugapajjanma neṣyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, since the others are different, simultaneous origination is not accepted;

children.text: guṇānāṃ samavetatvaṃ jñānaṃ cen na viśeṣaṇāt // SamUpad_I,16.53 //
children.translated_text: if the inherence of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) is [the answer] — no, because of [the objection from] qualification by knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.53 //

children.text: jñānenaiva viśeṣyatvāj jñānāpyatvaṃ smṛtes tathā /
children.translated_text: Since it is qualified by knowledge alone, the non-pervasion by knowledge [follows]; likewise from <s>smṛti</s> (memory);

children.text: sukhaṃ jñātaṃ mayety evaṃ tavājñānātmakatvataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.54 //
children.translated_text: 'Pleasure is known by me' — such [cognition] is due to your [system's] Self being non-conscious. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.54 //

children.text: sukhāder nātmadharmatvam ātmanas te 'vikārataḥ /
children.translated_text: Pleasure and the like are not properties of the Self, since the Self, according to you, is changeless;

children.text: bhedād anyasya kasmān na manaso vāviśeṣataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.55 //
children.translated_text: since it is different, why not [attribute them] to something else — or to the mind, which is no different [in this regard]? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.55 //

children.text: syān mālāparihāryā tu jñānaṃ cej jñeyatāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: There would be an unavoidable infinite regress if knowledge were to become an object of knowledge;

children.text: yugapad vāpi cotpattir abhyupete 'nta iṣyate // SamUpad_I,16.56 //
children.translated_text: or if simultaneous origination is admitted, the end [i.e., destruction] is accepted. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.56 //

children.text: anavasthāntaratvāc ca bandho nātmani vidyate /
children.translated_text: And since there is no change of state, bondage does not exist in the Self;

children.text: nāśuddhiś cāpy asaṅgatvād asaṅgo hīti ca śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,16.57 //
children.translated_text: nor impurity, due to its unattached nature — for the <s>śruti</s> says 'it is unattached.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.57 //

children.text: sūkṣmaikāgocarebhyaś ca na lipyata iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: And from the <s>śruti</s> 'it is not tainted' by the subtle and singular objects;

children.text: evaṃ tarhi na mokṣo 'sti bandhābhāvāt kathaṃcana // SamUpad_I,16.58 //
children.translated_text: if so, then liberation does not exist either, due to the absence of bondage in any way. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.58 //

children.text: śāstrānarthakyam evaṃ syān na buddher bhrāntir iṣyate /
children.translated_text: The scriptures would thus become purposeless — [but] the delusion of the intellect is not accepted [as real];

children.text: bandho mokṣaś ca tannāśaḥ sa yathokto na cānyathā // SamUpad_I,16.59 //
children.translated_text: bondage, liberation, and the destruction of that [delusion] are as stated [by us], and not otherwise. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.59 //

children.text: bodhātmajyotiṣā dīptā bodham ātmani manyate /
children.translated_text: The intellect, illuminated by the light of the Self which is consciousness, thinks there is consciousness in itself;

children.text: buddhir nānyo 'sti boddheti seyaṃ bhrāntir hi dhīgatā // SamUpad_I,16.60 //
children.translated_text: 'There is no other knower' — this indeed is the delusion residing in the intellect. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.60 //

children.text: bodhasyātmasvarūpatvān nityaṃ tatropacaryate /
children.translated_text: Since consciousness is the nature of the Self, it is always figuratively attributed [to the intellect];

children.text: aviveko 'py anādyo 'yaṃ saṃsāro nānya iṣyate // SamUpad_I,16.61 //
children.translated_text: this non-discrimination, which is beginningless, is [what constitutes] <s>saṃsāra</s> — no other [cause] is accepted. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.61 //

children.text: mokṣas tannāśa eva syān nānyathānupapattitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Liberation is simply the destruction of that [non-discrimination] — there is no other logical possibility;

children.text: yeṣāṃ vastvantarāpattir mokṣo nāśas tu tair mataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.62 //
children.translated_text: those for whom liberation is the attainment of some other reality consider it to be destruction [of the Self]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.62 //

children.text: avasthāntaram apy evam avikārān na yujyate /
children.translated_text: And thus a change of state too is not tenable for the changeless [Self];

children.text: vikāre 'vayavitvaṃ syāt tato nāśo ghaṭādivat // SamUpad_I,16.63 //
children.translated_text: if there were modification, it would have parts, and then destruction [would follow] like a pot and the like. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.63 //

children.text: tasmād bhrāntir ato 'nyā hi bandhamokṣādikalpanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the imaginations of bondage, liberation, and the like other than [the removal of] delusion

children.text: sāṃkhyakāṇādabauddhānāṃ mīmāṃsāhatakalpanāḥ // SamUpad_I,16.64 //
children.translated_text: are the fabrications of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Kaṇādas</s> (Vaiśeṣikas), Buddhists, and <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> [that are to be] rejected. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.64 //

children.text: śāstrayuktivirodhāt tā nādartavyāḥ kadācana /
children.translated_text: Since they contradict scripture and reasoning, they should never be regarded;

children.text: śakyante śataśo vaktuṃ doṣās tāsāṃ sahasraśaḥ // SamUpad_I,16.65 //
children.translated_text: the faults in those [doctrines] can be stated by the hundreds and thousands. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.65 //

children.text: api nindopapatteś ca yāny ato 'nyāni cety ataḥ /
children.translated_text: And since censure is justified for those and whatever other [doctrines] there may be,

children.text: tyaktvāto hy anyaśāstroktīr matiṃ kuryād dṛḍhāṃ budhaḥ // SamUpad_I,16.66 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having abandoned the teachings of other scriptures, the wise person should establish firm conviction. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.66 //

children.text: śraddhābhaktī puraskṛtya hitvā sarvam anārjavam /
children.translated_text: With faith and devotion placed foremost, having abandoned all crookedness,

children.text: vedāntasyaiva tattvārthe vyāsasyāpi matau tathā // SamUpad_I,16.67 //
children.translated_text: [one should focus] on the truth of <s>Vedānta</s> alone, and likewise on the view of <s>Vyāsa</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.67 //

children.text: iti praṇunnā dvayavādakalpanā nirātmavādāś ca tathā hi yuktitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the fabrications of the dualists have been refuted, as well as the doctrines of non-self, through reasoning;

children.text: vyapetaśaṅkāḥ paravādataḥ sthirā mumukṣavo jñānapathe syur ity uta // SamUpad_I,16.63 //
children.translated_text: free from doubt, firm against rival doctrines, may seekers of liberation be established on the path of knowledge! // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.68 //

children.text: svasākṣikaṃ jñānam atīva nirmalaṃ vikalpanābhyo viparītam advayam /
children.translated_text: Having attained completely the knowledge that is self-witnessed, supremely pure, opposite to conceptualization, and non-dual,

children.text: avāpya samyag yadi niścito bhaven niranvayo nirvṛtim eti śāśvatīm // SamUpad_I,16.69 //
children.translated_text: if one becomes firmly established, one without residue attains eternal bliss. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.69 //

children.text: idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ parāyaṇaṃ vyapetadoṣair abhimānavarjitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This supreme secret, the highest refuge, [should be contemplated] by those free from defects and devoid of pride;

children.text: samīkṣya kāryā matir ārjave sadā na tattvadṛk svānyamatir hi kaścana // SamUpad_I,16.70 //
children.translated_text: having examined it, one should always keep the mind fixed on directness — for no one who sees the truth holds the view of another. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.70 //

children.text: anekajanmāntarasaṃcitair naro vimucyate 'jñānanimittapātakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: A person is freed from sins caused by ignorance accumulated over many births,

children.text: idaṃ viditvā paramaṃ hi pāvanaṃ na lipyate vyoma iveha karmabhiḥ // SamUpad_I,16.71 //
children.translated_text: having known this supreme purifier — one is not tainted by actions, like space. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.71 //

children.text: praśāntacittāya jitendriyāya ca prahīṇadoṣāya yathoktakāriṇe /
children.translated_text: To one whose mind is tranquil, whose senses are conquered, whose faults are abandoned, who acts as instructed,

children.text: guṇānvitāyānugatāya sarvadā pradeyam etat satataṃ mumukṣave // SamUpad_I,16.72 //
children.translated_text: who is endowed with virtues and is always devoted — this [teaching] should be constantly given to the seeker of liberation. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.72 //

children.text: parasya dehe na yathābhimānitā parasya tadvat paramārtham īkṣya ca /
children.translated_text: Just as one does not identify with another's body, so too, having seen the ultimate truth,

children.text: idaṃ hi vijñānam atīva nirmalaṃ saṃprāpya mukto 'tha bhavec ca sarvataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.73 //
children.translated_text: having attained this supremely pure knowledge, one becomes liberated from everything. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.73 //

children.text: na hīha lābho 'bhyadhiko 'sti kaścana svarūpalābhāt sa ita hi nānyataḥ /
children.translated_text: There is indeed no gain here greater than the attainment of one's own nature, and it comes from this [teaching], not from anything else;

children.text: na deyam aindrād api rājyato 'dhikaṃ svarūpalābhaṃ tv aparīkṣya yatnataḥ // SamUpad_I,16.74 //
children.translated_text: not even something greater than the kingdom of <s>Indra</s> should be given [in exchange], without carefully examining the attainment of one's own nature. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16.74 //

body.text: iti pārthivaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,16 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the Earthly [Elements] (<s>Pārthivaprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.16 //

children.text: ātmā jñeyaḥ paro hy ātmā yasmād anyan na vidyate /
children.translated_text: The Self is to be known — the supreme Self, since nothing other than it exists;

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvadṛk śuddhas tasmai jñeyātmane namaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.1 //
children.translated_text: omniscient, all-seeing, pure — salutation to that Self which is to be known! // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.17.1 //

children.text: padavākyapramāṇajñair dīpabhūtaiḥ prakāśitam /
children.translated_text: Illuminated by those who are like lamps, who know words, sentences, and means of valid knowledge,

children.text: brahma vedarahasyaṃ yais tān nityaṃ praṇato 'smy aham // SamUpad_I,17.2 //
children.translated_text: I constantly bow to those who [know] <s>Brahman</s>, the secret of the <s>Vedas</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.2 //

children.text: yadvāksūryāṃśusaṃpātapraṇaṣṭadhvāntakalmaṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the contact of whose speech-rays the darkness of impurity is destroyed—

children.text: praṇamya tān gurūn vakṣye brahmavidyāviniścayam // SamUpad_I,17.3 //
children.translated_text: bowing to those teachers, I shall state the ascertainment of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.3 //

children.text: ātmalābhāt paro nānyo lābhaḥ kaścana vidyate /
children.translated_text: No gain whatsoever exists that is higher than the attainment of the Self,

children.text: yadarthā vedavādāś ca smārtāś cāpi tu yāḥ kriyāḥ // SamUpad_I,4 //
children.translated_text: for whose sake are the Vedic declarations and also the <s>smārta</s> (traditional) rituals. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.4 //

children.text: ātmārtho 'pi hi yo lābhaḥ sukhāyeṣṭo viparyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even that gain which is for the Self's sake, desired for the sake of happiness—the opposite [is the case];

children.text: ātmalābhaḥ paraḥ prokto nityatvād brahmavedibhiḥ // SamUpad_I,17.5 //
children.translated_text: the attainment of the Self is declared supreme by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, because of its eternality. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.5 //

children.text: svayaṃ labdhasvabhāvatvāl lābhas tasya na cānyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since its nature is self-obtained, its attainment is not from elsewhere;

children.text: anyāpekṣas tu yo lābhaḥ so 'nyadṛṣṭisamudbhavaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.6 //
children.translated_text: any gain that depends on something else arises from seeing otherness. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.6 //

children.text: anyadṛṣṭis tv avidyā syāt tannāśo mokṣa ucyate /
children.translated_text: Seeing otherness is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); its destruction is called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);

children.text: jñānenaiva tu so 'pi syād virodhitvān na karmaṇā // SamUpad_I,17.7 //
children.translated_text: and that too is by knowledge alone, being opposed [to ignorance], not by action. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.7 //

children.text: karmakāryas tv anityaḥ syād avidyākāmakāraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The effect of action is non-eternal, having <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and desire as its causes;

children.text: pramāṇaṃ veda evātra jñānasyādhigame smṛtaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.8 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s> alone is the authority here, recognized as the means for attaining knowledge. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.8 //

children.text: jñānaikārthaparatvāt taṃ vākyam ekaṃ tato viduḥ /
children.translated_text: Since [the Vedas] have knowledge as their sole aim, therefore [the wise] know that sentence [of the Vedas] as one;

children.text: ekatvaṃ hy ātmano jñeyaṃ vākyārthapratipattitaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.9 //
children.translated_text: for the oneness of the Self is to be known from the understanding of the sentence's meaning. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.9 //

children.text: vācyabhedāt tu tadbhedaḥ kalpyo vācyo 'pi tacchruteḥ /
children.translated_text: The differentiation of that [<s>Brahman</s>] should be imagined as due to the differentiation of what is expressed; and the expressible [has its differentiation] from its perception [in scripture];

children.text: trayaṃ tv etat tataḥ proktaṃ rūpaṃ nāma ca karma ca // SamUpad_I,17.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore this threefold [manifestation] has been stated: form, name, and action. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.10 //

children.text: asad etat trayaṃ tasmād anyonyena hi kalpitam /
children.translated_text: This threefold [manifestation] is unreal, for it is mutually imagined;

children.text: kṛto varṇo yathā śabdāc chruto 'nyatra dhiyā bahiḥ // SamUpad_I,17.11 //
children.translated_text: just as a sound is produced from a letter, heard elsewhere, [and conceived] by the mind externally. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.11 //

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ cāpi yathā rūpaṃ buddheḥ śabdāya kalpate /
children.translated_text: And just as a seen form is imagined [to belong] to a word by the intellect,

children.text: evam etaj jagat sarvaṃ bhrāntibuddhivikalpitam // SamUpad_I,17.12 //
children.translated_text: so too this entire world is imagined by the deluded mind. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.12 //

children.text: asad etat tato yuktaṃ saccinmātraṃ na kalpitam /
children.translated_text: This [world] is unreal; therefore what is real is Being-Consciousness (<s>saccit</s>) alone, not imagined;

children.text: vedaś cāpi sa evādyo vedyaś cānyas tu kalpitaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.13 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s> too is that very primordial [reality], while what is known [as distinct] is imagined. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.13 //

children.text: yena vetti sa vedaḥ syāt svapne sarvaṃ tu māyayā /
children.translated_text: That by which one knows is the <s>Veda</s> (knowledge); in dream, everything is [created] by <s>māyā</s>;

children.text: yena paśyati tac cakṣuḥ śṛṇoti śrotram ucyate // SamUpad_I,17.14 //
children.translated_text: that by which one sees is the eye; that by which one hears is called the ear. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.14 //

children.text: yena svapnagato vakti sā vāg ghrāṇaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: That by which one speaks while in dream is speech; likewise the sense of smell;

children.text: rasanasparśane caiva manaś cānyat tathendriyam // SamUpad_I,17.15 //
children.translated_text: and also taste and touch, and the mind, and the other senses. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.15 //

children.text: kalpyopādhibhir evaitad bhinnaṃ jñānam anekadhā /
children.translated_text: By imagined limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), this knowledge is differentiated in many ways;

children.text: ādhibhedād yathā bhedo maṇer ekasya jāyate // SamUpad_I,17.16 //
children.translated_text: just as a single gem appears differentiated due to differences in its base. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.16 //

children.text: jāgrataś ca tathā bhedo jñānasyāsya vikalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the waking state, this differentiation of knowledge is imagined;

children.text: buddhisthaṃ vyākaroty arthaṃ bhrāntyā tṛṣṇodbhavakriyaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.17 //
children.translated_text: [the one who] discriminates the object existing in the intellect—his actions arise from delusion and craving. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.17 //

children.text: svapne yadvat prabodhe ca bahiś cāntas tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Just as in dream and in waking, and externally and internally,

children.text: ālekhyādhyayane yadvat tad anyonyadhiyodbhavam // SamUpad_I,17.18 //
children.translated_text: just as in drawing and in study—that arises from mutual mental superimposition. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.18 //

children.text: yadāyaṃ kalpayed bhedaṃ tatkāmaḥ san yathākratuḥ /
children.translated_text: When one imagines differentiation, being of such desire, 'as one's intention [so one becomes]' (<s>yathākratuḥ</s>);

children.text: yatkāmas tatkratur bhūtvā kṛtaṃ yat tat prapadyate // SamUpad_I,17.19 //
children.translated_text: having become of that intention, one attains what one has done. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.19 //

children.text: avidyāprabhavaṃ sarvam asat tasmād idaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: All that arises from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is unreal; therefore this world—

children.text: tadvatā dṛśyate yasmāt suṣupte na ca gṛhyate // SamUpad_I,17.20 //
children.translated_text: since it is seen by one who possesses that [ignorance], and in deep sleep it is not perceived. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.20 //

children.text: vidyāvidye śrutiprokte ekatvānyadhiyau hi naḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are declared by <s>Śruti</s>; they are the cognitions of unity and otherness for us;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaprayatnena śāstre vidyā vidhīyate // SamUpad_I,17.21 //
children.translated_text: therefore, with every effort, knowledge is enjoined in the scripture. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.21 //

children.text: citte hy ādarśavad yasmāc chuddhe vidyā prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Since knowledge shines forth in a pure mind, like [in] a mirror,

children.text: yamair nityaiś ca yajñaiś ca tapobhis tasya śodhanam // SamUpad_I,17.22 //
children.translated_text: its purification is [achieved] through eternal observances (<s>yamas</s>), sacrifices (<s>yajñas</s>), and austerities (<s>tapas</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.22 //

children.text: śārīrāditapaḥ kuryāt tadviśuddhyartham uttamam /
children.translated_text: One should perform the supreme austerity of the body and the like for the purpose of its purification;

children.text: manaādisamādhānaṃ tattaddehaviśoṣaṇam // SamUpad_I,17.23 //
children.translated_text: [this includes] concentration of the mind and the like, [and] the desiccation of the respective body [through asceticism]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.23 //

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ jāgaritaṃ vidyāt smṛtaṃ svapnaṃ tad eva tu /
children.translated_text: What is perceived should be known as the waking state; what is remembered is indeed dream;

children.text: suṣuptaṃ tadabhavaṃ ca svam ātmānaṃ paraṃ padam // SamUpad_I,17.24 //
children.translated_text: deep sleep is the absence of that; and the Self itself is the supreme state (<s>paraṃ padam</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.24 //

children.text: suṣuptākhyaṃ tamo 'jñānaṃ bījaṃ svapnaprabodhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The darkness of ignorance called deep sleep is the seed of dream and waking;

children.text: svātmabodhapradagdhaṃ syād bījaṃ dagdhaṃ yathābhavam // SamUpad_I,17.25 //
children.translated_text: it is burned by the knowledge of one's own Self, just as a seed, once burned, [cannot sprout] again. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.25 //

children.text: tad evaikaṃ tridhā jñeyaṃ māyābījaṃ punaḥ kramāt /
children.translated_text: That very one seed of <s>māyā</s>, to be known in three forms again in succession;

children.text: māyāvy ātmāvikāro 'pi bahudhaiko jalārkavat // SamUpad_I,17.26 //
children.translated_text: the <s>māyāvin</s> (magician), the Self, though without modification, [appears as] many, like a single sun [reflected] in water. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.26 //

children.text: bījaṃ caikaṃ yathā bhinnaṃ prāṇasvapnādibhis tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as one seed is [apparently] divided by <s>prāṇa</s>, dream, and so forth,

children.text: svapnajāgraccharīreṣu tadvac cātmā jalenduvat // SamUpad_I,17.27 //
children.translated_text: so too the Self in the bodies of dream and waking, like the moon [reflected] in water. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.27 //

children.text: māyāhastinam āruhya māyāvy eko yathā vrajet /
children.translated_text: Just as a magician, riding a magical elephant, travels,

children.text: āgacchaṃs tadvad evātmā prāṇasvapnādigo 'calaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.28 //
children.translated_text: so too the Self, associating with <s>prāṇa</s>, dream, and so forth, [remains] coming and going yet immovable. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.28 //

children.text: na hastī na tadārūḍho māyāvy anyo yathā sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no elephant, nor one mounted on it; the magician stands apart [from them];

children.text: na prāṇādi na taddraṣṭā tathā jño 'nyaḥ sadā dṛśiḥ // SamUpad_I,17.29 //
children.translated_text: so too there is no <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, nor their seer—the knower is other, always pure seeing. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.29 //

children.text: abaddhacakṣuṣo nāsti māyā māyāvino 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: For one whose eyes are not bound [i.e., who has knowledge], there is no <s>māyā</s>, nor a magician either;

children.text: baddhākṣasyaiva sā māyāmāyāvy eva tato bhavet // SamUpad_I,17.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> exists only for one whose eyes are bound; what appears as the magician would then be [<s>māyā</s>] itself. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.30 //

children.text: sākṣād eva sa vijñeyaḥ sākṣād ātmeti ca śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: He is to be known directly; and from <s>Śruti</s>: 'directly the Self';

children.text: bhidyate hṛdayagranthir na ced ityāditaḥ śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,17.31 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Śruti</s> beginning with 'the knot of the heart is broken' and so forth. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.31 //

children.text: aśabdāditvato nāsya grahaṇaṃ cendriyair bhavet /
children.translated_text: Since it is not of the nature of sound and the like, it cannot be grasped by the senses;

children.text: sukhādibhyas tathānyatvād buddhyā vāpi kathaṃ bhavet // SamUpad_I,17.32 //
children.translated_text: and since it is different from pleasure and the like, how could it [be grasped] even by the intellect? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.32 //

children.text: adṛśyo 'pi yathā rāhuś candre bimbaṃ yathāmbhasi /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rāhu</s>, though invisible [by itself], [is perceived] in the moon, just as a reflection in water,

children.text: sarvago 'pi tathaivātmā buddhāv eva sa gṛhyate // SamUpad_I,17.33 //
children.translated_text: so too the Self, though all-pervading, is grasped only in the intellect. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.33 //

children.text: bhānor bimbaṃ yathā cauṣṇyaṃ jale dṛṣṭaṃ na cāmbhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the reflection and heat of the sun are seen in water, not belonging to the water,

children.text: buddhau bodho na taddharmas tathaiva syād vidharmataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.34 //
children.translated_text: so too awareness in the intellect is not its property—due to the difference in nature. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.34 //

children.text: cakṣuryuktā dhiyo vṛttir yā tāṃ paśyann aluptadṛk /
children.translated_text: The modification of the intellect connected with the eye—he who sees that, with unimpaired seeing,

children.text: dṛṣṭer draṣṭā bhaved ātmā śruteḥ śrotā tathā śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,17.35 //
children.translated_text: the Self would be the seer of seeing, the hearer of hearing—from <s>Śruti</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.35 //

children.text: kevalāṃ manaso vṛttiṃ paśyan mantā mater ajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the modification of the mind alone, [he is] the thinker of thought, unborn;

children.text: vijñātāluptaśaktitvāt tathā śāstraṃ na hīty ataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.36 //
children.translated_text: since the capacity of the knower is unimpaired, therefore the scripture does not [say otherwise]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.36 //

children.text: dhyāyatīty avikāritvaṃ tathā lelāyatīty api /
children.translated_text: 'He meditates, as it were'—[this indicates] unchangeableness; likewise 'He moves, as it were';

children.text: atra steneti śuddhatvaṃ tathānanvāgataṃ śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,17.37 //
children.translated_text: 'Here there is no thief'—thus purity; likewise 'untouched'—from <s>Śruti</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.37 //

children.text: śaktyalopāt suṣupte jñas tathā bodhe 'vikārataḥ /
children.translated_text: In deep sleep, the knower [exists] due to the non-loss of capacity; likewise in waking, due to unchangeableness;

children.text: jñeyasyaiva viśeṣas tu yatra veti śruter mataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.38 //
children.translated_text: the distinction is only of the knowable—'where he seems to see'—such is the view of <s>Śruti</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.38 //

children.text: vyavadhānād dhi pārokṣyaṃ lokadṛṣṭer anātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indirectness [of knowledge] arises from obstruction, pertaining to the worldly vision of the non-Self;

children.text: dṛṣṭer ātmasvarūpatvāt pratyakṣaṃ brahma tat smṛtam // SamUpad_I,17.39 //
children.translated_text: since seeing is of the nature of the Self, <s>Brahman</s> is remembered as directly known (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.39 //

children.text: na hi dīpāntarāpekṣā yadvad dīpaprakāśane /
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp requires no other lamp for its illumination,

children.text: bodhasyātmasvarūpatvān na bodho 'nyas tatheṣyate // SamUpad_I,17.40 //
children.translated_text: since awareness is of the nature of the Self, no other awareness is accepted. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.40 //

children.text: viṣayatvaṃ vikāritvaṃ nānātvaṃ vā na hīṣyate /
children.translated_text: Being an object, undergoing modification, or being manifold—none of these are accepted [for the Self];

children.text: na heyo nāpy upādeya ātmā nānyena vā tataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.41 //
children.translated_text: the Self is neither to be abandoned nor to be taken up, nor [affected] by anything else. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.41 //

children.text: sabāhyābhyantaro 'jīrṇo janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ /
children.translated_text: Encompassing both external and internal, unaging, beyond birth, death, and old age—

children.text: aham ātmeti yo vetti kuto nv eva bibheti saḥ // SamUpad_I,17.42 //
children.translated_text: he who knows 'I am the Self,' from what indeed could he fear? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.42 //

children.text: prāg evaitadvidheḥ karma varṇitvāder apohanāt /
