children.translated_text: Even before the injunction [of knowledge], action [ceases] through the negation of being a householder (<s>varṇin</s>) and the like;

children.text: tad asthūlādiśāstrebhyas tat tvam eveti niścayāt // SamUpad_I,17.43 //
children.translated_text: because from the scriptures [declaring <s>Brahman</s> to be] 'not gross' and the like, [there is] the certainty '<s>tat tvam eva</s>' (You are That indeed). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.43 //

children.text: pūrvadehaparityāge jātyādīnāṃ prahāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: Upon abandoning the former body, through the removal of caste and the like—

children.text: dehasyaiva tu jātyādis tasyāpy evaṃ hy anātmatā // SamUpad_I,17.44 //
children.translated_text: for caste and the like belong only to the body, and thus its non-Self nature [is established]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.44 //

children.text: mamāhaṃ cety ato 'vidyā śarīrādiṣv anātmasu /
children.translated_text: 'Mine' and 'I'—thus <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) [operates] with respect to the body and the like, which are non-Self;

children.text: ātmajñānena heyā syād asurāṇām iti śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,17.45 //
children.translated_text: it is to be removed by Self-knowledge, as [shown by] the <s>Śruti</s> regarding the <s>Asuras</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.45 //

children.text: daśāhāśaucakāryāṇāṃ pārivrājye nivartanam /
children.translated_text: Just as the observances of ten days' impurity cease in the state of <s>pārivrājya</s> (renunciation),

children.text: yathā jñānasya saṃprāptau tadvaj jātyādikarmaṇām // SamUpad_I,17.46 //
children.translated_text: so too is the cessation of actions based on caste and the like upon the attainment of knowledge. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.46 //

children.text: yatkāmas tatkratur bhūtvā kṛtaṃ tv ajñaḥ prapadyate /
children.translated_text: 'As one's desire, so one's intention becomes'—thus the ignorant person attains what has been done;

children.text: yadā svātmadṛśaḥ kāmāḥ pramucyante 'mṛtas tadā // SamUpad_I,17.47 //
children.translated_text: when desires directed toward one's own Self are released, then one becomes immortal. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.47 //

children.text: ātmarūpavidheḥ kāryaṃ kriyādibhyo nivartanam /
children.translated_text: The purpose of the injunction regarding the Self's nature is the cessation from action and the like;

children.text: na sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ vātmā nityatṛptaḥ śruter mataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.48 //
children.translated_text: the Self is neither something to be achieved nor a means of achievement; it is ever satisfied—such is the view of <s>Śruti</s>. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.48 //

children.text: utpādyāpyavikāryāṇi saṃskāryaṃ ca kriyāphalam /
children.translated_text: Production, modification, and refinement—these are the [only] results of action;

children.text: nāto 'nyat karmaṇaḥ kāryaṃ tyajet tasmāt sasādhanam // SamUpad_I,17.49 //
children.translated_text: there is no other effect of action; therefore one should renounce [action] together with its means. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.49 //

children.text: tāpāntatvād anityatvād ātmārthatvāc ca yā bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since [outward pleasure] ends in affliction, is non-eternal, and is directed toward the Self [i.e., self-centered], one who seeks the truth

children.text: saṃhṛtyātmani tāṃ prītiṃ satyārthī gurum āśrayet // SamUpad_I,17.50 //
children.translated_text: should withdraw that outward-directed delight into the Self and resort to a teacher (<s>guru</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.50 //

children.text: śāntaṃ prājñaṃ tathā muktaṃ niṣkriyaṃ brahmaṇi sthitam /
children.translated_text: [The teacher should be] peaceful, wise, liberated, actionless, established in <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: śruter ācāryavān veda tad viddhīti smṛtes tathā // SamUpad_I,17.51 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Śruti</s>: 'one who has a teacher knows'; from <s>Smṛti</s> likewise: 'know that.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.51 //

children.text: sa gurus tārayed yuktaṃ śiṣyaṃ śiṣyaguṇānvitam /
children.translated_text: That teacher should ferry across the fit disciple, endowed with the qualities of a disciple,

children.text: brahmavidyāplavenāśu svāntadhvāntamahodadhim // SamUpad_I,17.52 //
children.translated_text: by the boat of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>), the great ocean of inner darkness. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.52 //

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ spṛṣṭiḥ śrutir ghrātir matir vijñātir eva ca /
children.translated_text: Seeing, touching, hearing, smelling, thinking, and knowing—

children.text: śaktayo 'nyāś ca bhidyante cidrūpatve 'py upādhibhiḥ // SamUpad_I,17.53 //
children.translated_text: these and other powers are differentiated through <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts), though [the Self] is of the nature of consciousness. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.53 //

children.text: apāyodbhūtihīnābhir nityaṃ dīpyan ravir yathā /
children.translated_text: Free from setting, rising, and diminution, ever shining like the sun,

children.text: sarvagaḥ sarvadṛk śuddhaḥ sarvaṃ jānāti sarvadā // SamUpad_I,17.54 //
children.translated_text: all-pervading, all-seeing, pure—[the Self] knows all, always. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.54 //

children.text: anyadṛṣṭiḥ śarīrasthas tāvanmātro hy avidyayā /
children.translated_text: Due to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), one who sees otherness, dwelling in the body, is limited to that extent;

children.text: jalendvādyupamābhis tu taddharmā ca vibhāvyate // SamUpad_I,17.55 //
children.translated_text: but through analogies like the moon in water, its [true] nature is made clear. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.55 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā bāhyaṃ nimīlyātha smṛtvā tat pravihāya ca /
children.translated_text: Having seen the external, closing [the eyes], remembering that and then abandoning [the memory],

children.text: athonmīlyātmano dṛṣṭiṃ brahma prāpnoty anadhvagaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.56 //
children.translated_text: then opening [the eyes]—one who does not travel [any path] attains <s>Brahman</s> through the Self's own seeing. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.56 //

children.text: prāṇādy evaṃ trikaṃ hitvā tīrṇo 'jñānamahodadhim /
children.translated_text: Thus, having abandoned the threefold [state] of <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, having crossed the great ocean of ignorance,

children.text: svātmastho nirguṇaḥ śuddho buddho muktaḥ svato hi saḥ // SamUpad_I,17.57 //
children.translated_text: established in one's own Self, without qualities, pure, awakened, liberated—such is he, by his own [nature]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.57 //

children.text: ajo 'haṃ cāmaro 'mṛtyur ajaro 'bhaya eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'I am unborn, undying, deathless, ageless, and indeed fearless,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvadṛk śuddha iti buddho na jāyate // SamUpad_I,17.58 //
children.translated_text: omniscient, all-seeing, pure'—thus the awakened one is not [re]born. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.58 //

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ yat tamobījaṃ tan nāstīti viniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The certainty that the previously mentioned seed of darkness does not exist—

children.text: tadabhāve kuto janma brahmaikatvaṃ vijānataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.59 //
children.translated_text: in its absence, whence could there be birth for one who knows the oneness of <s>Brahman</s>? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.59 //

children.text: kṣīrāt sarpir yathoddhṛtya kṣiptaṃ tasmin na pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: Just as clarified butter, having been extracted from milk and placed back in it, does not become as before,

children.text: buddhyāder jñas tathāsatyān na dehī pūrvavad bhavet // SamUpad_I,17.60 //
children.translated_text: so too the knower, [having been extracted] from the unreal intellect and the like, does not become an embodied being as before. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.60 //

children.text: satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ ca rasādeḥ pañcakāt param /
children.translated_text: Truth, knowledge, and infinity—beyond the fivefold [sheaths] beginning with food;

children.text: syām adṛśyādiśāstroktam ahaṃ brahmeti nirbhayaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.61 //
children.translated_text: 'I am that which is described in scripture as invisible and so forth—I am <s>Brahman</s>'—thus [one becomes] fearless. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.61 //

children.text: yasmād bhītāḥ pravartante vāṅmanaḥpāvakādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [That] from fear of which speech, mind, fire, and the like proceed—

children.text: tadātmānandatattvajño na bibheti kutaścana // SamUpad_I,17.62 //
children.translated_text: one who knows the truth of the bliss of that Self does not fear anything whatsoever. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.62 //

children.text: nāmādibhyaḥ pare bhūmni svārājye cet sthito 'dvaye /
children.translated_text: If established in the supreme <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite), beyond name and the like, in self-sovereignty, in the non-dual—

children.text: praṇamet kaṃ tadātmajño na kāryaṃ karmaṇā tadā // SamUpad_I,17.63 //
children.translated_text: whom would a knower of the Self then bow to? No action need be done then. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.63 //

children.text: virāḍ vaiśvānaro bāhyaḥ smarann antaḥ prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Externally, [the Self is] <s>Virāj</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [in the waking state]; remembering inwardly, <s>Prajāpati</s> [in the dream state];

children.text: pravilīne tu sarvasmin prājño 'vyākṛtam ucyate // SamUpad_I,17.64 //
children.translated_text: but when all is dissolved, the knower (<s>Prājña</s>) is called the Unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.64 //

children.text: vācārambhaṇamātratvāt suṣuptāditrikaṃ tv asat /
children.translated_text: Since [the world] is a mere verbal elaboration (<s>vācārambhaṇamātra</s>), the threefold [states] of deep sleep and the like are unreal;

children.text: satyo jñaś cāham ity evaṃ satyasandho vimucyate // SamUpad_I,17.65 //
children.translated_text: 'I am real and a knower'—thus one who is true to truth is liberated. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.65 //

children.text: bhārūpatvād yathā bhānor nāhorātre tathaiva tu /
children.translated_text: Just as, since the sun is of the nature of light, day and night do not [belong to it],

children.text: jñānājñāne na me syātāṃ cidrūpatvāviśeṣataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.66 //
children.translated_text: so too knowledge and ignorance do not belong to me, since there is no distinction from my nature as consciousness. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.66 //

children.text: śāstrasyānatiśaṅkyatvād brahmaiva syām ahaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Since scripture is not to be doubted, I would always be <s>Brahman</s> alone;

children.text: brahmaṇo me na heyaṃ syād grāhyaṃ veti ca saṃsmaret // SamUpad_I,17.67 //
children.translated_text: one should remember: 'For me, who am <s>Brahman</s>, there is nothing to be abandoned nor anything to be acquired.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.67 //

children.text: aham eva ca bhūteṣu sarveṣv eko nabho yathā /
children.translated_text: I alone am in all beings, one, like space;

children.text: mayi sarvāṇi bhūtāni paśyann evaṃ na jāyate // SamUpad_I,17.68 //
children.translated_text: seeing all beings in me—thus seeing, one is not [re]born. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.68 //

children.text: na bāhyaṃ madhyato vāntar vidyate 'nyat svataḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: Nothing exists outside, nor in the middle, nor inside, that is other [than the Self] by its own nature, anywhere;

children.text: abāhyāntaḥśruteḥ kiṃcit tasmāc chuddhaḥ svayaṃprabhaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.69 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Śruti</s>: 'without exterior or interior'—therefore [one is] pure, self-luminous. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.69 //

children.text: netinetyādiśāstrebhyaḥ prapañcopaśamo 'dvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the scriptures beginning with '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), the cessation of the phenomenal world is non-dual,

children.text: avijñātādiśāstrāc ca naiva jñeyo hy ato 'nyathā // SamUpad_I,17.70 //
children.translated_text: and from the scriptures beginning with 'the unknowable'—the Self is indeed not to be known otherwise. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.70 //

children.text: sarvasyātmāham eveti brahma ced viditaṃ param /
children.translated_text: If the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is known as 'I am indeed the Self of all,'

children.text: sa ātmā sarvabhūtānām ātmā hy eṣām iti śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,17.71 //
children.translated_text: then it is the Self of all beings, because <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) declares 'It is indeed their Self.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.71 //

children.text: jīvaś cet param ātmānaṃ svātmānaṃ devam añjasā /
children.translated_text: If the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) knows directly the supreme Self, its own Self, as God,

children.text: devopāsyaḥ sa devānāṃ paśutvāc ca nivartate // SamUpad_I,17.72 //
children.translated_text: he who is to be worshipped by the gods—he is freed from being a subject of the gods. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.72 //

children.text: aham eva sadātmajñaḥ śūnyas tv anyair yathāmbaram /
children.translated_text: I alone am the eternal knower of the Self, void of others like space,

children.text: ity evaṃ satyasaṃdhatvād asaddhātā na badhyate // SamUpad_I,17.73 //
children.translated_text: thus, being firmly established in truth, one who negates the unreal is not bound. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.73 //

children.text: kṛpaṇās te 'nyathaivāto vidur brahma paraṃ hi ye /
children.translated_text: Pitiable are those who understand the supreme <s>Brahman</s> otherwise than this;

children.text: svarāḍ yo 'nanyadṛk svasthas tasya devā asan vaśe // SamUpad_I,17.74 //
children.translated_text: he who is self-sovereign, seeing no other, established in himself—to him the gods were subject. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.74 //

children.text: hitvā jātyādisaṃbandhaṃ vāco 'nyāḥ saha karmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the connection with birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the like, and all other words together with actions,

children.text: om ity evaṃ svam ātmānaṃ sarvaṃ śuddhaṃ prapadyatha // SamUpad_I,17.75 //
children.translated_text: through '<s>Oṃ</s>' alone, take refuge in your own Self, all-pure. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.75 //

children.text: setuṃ sarvavyavasthānām ahorātrādivarjitam /
children.translated_text: The bridge of all ordinances, devoid of day and night and the like,

children.text: tiryag ūrdhvam adhaḥ sarvaṃ sakṛjjyotir anāmayam // SamUpad_I,17.76 //
children.translated_text: pervading all—sideways, above, below—the one light, free from affliction. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.76 //

children.text: dharmādharmavinirmuktaṃ bhūtabhavyāt kṛtākṛtāt /
children.translated_text: Free from <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), from past and future, from what is done and undone—

children.text: svam ātmānaṃ paraṃ vidyād vimuktaṃ sarvabandhanaiḥ // SamUpad_I,17.77 //
children.translated_text: one should know one's own Self as supreme, liberated from all bonds. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.77 //

children.text: akurvan sarvakṛc chuddhas tiṣṭhann atyeti dhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Doing nothing yet the doer of all, pure, remaining still yet surpassing those who run,

children.text: māyayā sarvaśaktitvād ajaḥ san bahudhā mataḥ // SamUpad_I,17.78 //
children.translated_text: through <s>māyā</s> (illusion), being all-powerful, though unborn, it is regarded as many. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.78 //

children.text: rājavat sākṣimātratvāt saṃnidhyād bhrāmako yathā /
children.translated_text: Like a king, by being merely a witness; like a magnet, by mere proximity,

children.text: bhrāmayañ jagad ātmāhaṃ niṣkriyo 'kārako 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.79 //
children.translated_text: causing the world to revolve—I, the Self, am actionless, non-agent, and non-dual. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.79 //

children.text: nirguṇaṃ niṣkriyaṃ nityaṃ nirdvandvaṃ yan nirāmayam /
children.translated_text: That which is without qualities, without action, eternal, free from dualities, free from affliction,

children.text: śuddhaṃ buddhaṃ tathā muktaṃ tad brahmāsmīti dhārayet // SamUpad_I,17.80 //
children.translated_text: pure, awakened, and liberated—'I am that <s>Brahman</s>'—thus should one hold firmly. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.80 //

children.text: bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca sarvaṃ yata idam ubhayaṃ heyam ekaṃ dvayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Bondage and liberation—since both of these are to be abandoned, being one yet appearing as two,

children.text: jñeyājñeyābhyatītaṃ paramam adhigataṃ tattvam ekaṃ viśuddham /
children.translated_text: transcending both the knowable and the unknowable, the supreme reality attained is one and perfectly pure,

children.text: vijñāyaitad yathāvac chrutimunigaditaṃ śokamohāv atītaḥ /
children.translated_text: knowing this exactly as declared by <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) and the sages, having transcended grief and delusion,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvakṛt syād bhavabhayarahito brāhmaṇo 'vāptakṛtyaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.81 //
children.translated_text: one becomes omniscient, the doer of all, free from the fear of existence—a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has accomplished all that is to be done. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.81 //

children.text: na svayaṃ svasya nānyaś ca nānyasyātmā ca heyagaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither oneself for oneself, nor another, nor the Self for another—nothing is to be rejected,

children.text: upādeyo na cāpy evam iti samyaṅmatiḥ smṛtā // SamUpad_I,17.82 //
children.translated_text: nor is anything to be appropriated—thus is right understanding (<s>samyaṅmati</s>) declared. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.82 //

children.text: ātmapratyāyikā hy eṣā sarvavedāntagocarā /
children.translated_text: This conviction regarding the Self is the subject of all <s>Vedānta</s>,

children.text: jñātvaitāṃ hi vimucyante sarvasaṃsārabandhanaiḥ // SamUpad_I,17.83 //
children.translated_text: knowing which, one is freed from all the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.83 //

children.text: rahasyaṃ sarvavedānāṃ devānāṃ cāpi yat param /
children.translated_text: The secret of all the <s>Vedas</s> and that which is supreme among the gods,

children.text: pavitraṃ paramaṃ hy etat tad etat saṃprakāśitam // SamUpad_I,17.84 //
children.translated_text: this most sacred and supreme teaching—that has been herein illuminated. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.84 //

children.text: naitad deyam aśāntāya rahasyaṃ jñānam uttamam /
children.translated_text: This secret, supreme knowledge should not be given to one who is not tranquil;

children.text: viraktāya pradātavyaṃ śiṣyāyānugatāya ca // SamUpad_I,17.85 //
children.translated_text: it should be imparted to one who is dispassionate, to a disciple who is devoted. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.85 //

children.text: dadataś cātmano jñānaṃ niṣkriyo 'nyo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For one who gives knowledge of the Self, no higher actionless means is found;

children.text: jñānam icchan bhavet tasmād yuktaḥ śiṣyaguṇaiḥ sadā // SamUpad_I,17.86 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one desiring knowledge should always be endowed with the qualities of a disciple. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.86 //

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ tathā jñātā yasmād anyan na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Since nothing other than knowledge, the knowable, and the knower exists,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktir yas tasmai jñānātmane namaḥ // SamUpad_I,17.87 //
children.translated_text: homage to that omniscient, all-powerful one whose nature is knowledge. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.87 //

children.text: vidyayā tāritāḥ smo yair janmamṛtyumahodadhim /
children.translated_text: By whom we have been carried across the great ocean of birth and death through knowledge—

children.text: sarvajñebhyo namas tebhyo gurubhyo 'jñānasaṃkulam // SamUpad_I,17.88 //
children.translated_text: to those omniscient teachers, we bow—who led us across the ocean dense with ignorance. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17.88 //

body.text: iti samyaṅmatiprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,17 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Samyaṅmati-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Right Understanding). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,17 //

children.text: yenātmanā vilīyanta udbhavanti ca vṛttayaḥ /
children.translated_text: By that Self in which mental modifications dissolve and from which they arise—

children.text: nityāvagataye tasmai namo dhīpratyayātmane // SamUpad_I,18.1 //
children.translated_text: to that eternally realized one, whose nature is the witness of all mental cognitions, homage! // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.1 //

children.text: pramathya vajropamayuktisaṃbhṛtaiḥ śruter arātiñ śataśo vaco 'sibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having destroyed the enemies of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) a hundredfold with word-swords sharpened by diamond-like reasoning,

children.text: rarakṣa vedārthanidhiṃ viśāladhīr namo yatīndrāya guror garīyase // SamUpad_I,18.2 //
children.translated_text: the broad-minded one protected the treasury of Vedic meaning—homage to that supreme among ascetics, the greatest of teachers! // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.2 //

children.text: nityamuktaḥ sad evāsmīty evaṃ cen na bhaven matiḥ /
children.translated_text: If the understanding 'I am eternally liberated, existence itself' does not arise,

children.text: kimarthaṃ śrāvayaty evaṃ mātṛvac chrutir ādṛtā // SamUpad_I,18.3 //
children.translated_text: then for what purpose does the revered <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) thus teach, like a mother? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.3 //

children.text: siddhād evāham ity asmād yuṣmaddharmo niṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: From the already established truth 'I am,' the property of being 'you' [i.e., objecthood] is negated,

children.text: rajjvām ivāhidhīr yuktyā tat tvam ityādiśāsanaiḥ // SamUpad_I,18.4 //
children.translated_text: like the notion of a snake in a rope, through reasoning and the teachings such as '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.4 //

children.text: śāstraprāmāṇyato jñeyā dharmāder astitā yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the existence of <s>dharma</s> and the like is to be known through the authority of scripture,

children.text: viṣāpoho yathā dhyānād dhnutiḥ syāt pāpmanas tathā // SamUpad_I,18.5 //
children.translated_text: just as poison is removed through meditation, so too is the shaking off of sin. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.5 //

children.text: sad brahmāhaṃ karomīti pratyayāv ātmasākṣikau /
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>, existence' and 'I act'—these two cognitions are witnessed by the Self;

children.text: tayor ajñānajasyaiva tyāgo yuktataro mataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.6 //
children.translated_text: of the two, the abandonment of that which is born of ignorance alone is considered more appropriate. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.6 //

children.text: sad asmīti pramāṇotthā dhīr anyā tannibhodbhavā /
children.translated_text: The cognition 'I exist' arises from valid means of knowledge; the other arises from its semblance—

children.text: pratyakṣādinibhā vāpi bādhyate digbhramādivat // SamUpad_I,18.7 //
children.translated_text: or even from what resembles perception and the like, and is sublated, like the illusion of direction. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.7 //

children.text: kartā bhokteti yac chāstraṃ lokabuddhyanuvādi tat /
children.translated_text: The scripture that says 'doer' and 'enjoyer' follows the understanding of the common world;

children.text: sad asmīti śruter jātā bādhyate 'nyaitayaiva dhīḥ // SamUpad_I,18.8 //
children.translated_text: the other cognition is sublated by this very understanding born from <s>Śruti</s>: 'I am existence.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.8 //

children.text: sad eva tvam asīty ukte nātmano muktatāṃ sthirām /
children.translated_text: When it is declared 'You are indeed existence,' if one does not firmly attain the liberation of the Self,

children.text: prapadyate prasaṃcakṣām ato yuktyānucintayet // SamUpad_I,18.9 //
children.translated_text: one should resort to <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (repeated contemplation), and therefore reflect through reasoning. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.9 //

children.text: sakṛd uktaṃ na gṛhṇāti vākyārthajño 'pi yo bhavet /
children.translated_text: Even one who understands the meaning of the sentence, if he does not grasp it when stated once,

children.text: apekṣate 'ta evānyad avocāma dvayaṃ hi tat // SamUpad_I,18.10 //
children.translated_text: requires something further—therefore we have spoken of a twofold means. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.10 //

children.text: niyogo 'pratipannatvāt karmaṇāṃ sa yathā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Just as injunction of actions would apply to one who has not yet attained,

children.text: aviruddho bhavet tāvad yāvat saṃvedyatādṛḍhā // SamUpad_I,18.11 //
children.translated_text: so it remains non-contradictory as long as the conviction of experiential reality is firm. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.11 //

children.text: ceṣṭitaṃ ca tathā mithyā svacchandaḥ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: And thus all activity is false—one who is independent understands this;

children.text: prasaṃkhyānam ataḥ kāryaṃ yāvad ātmānubhūyate // SamUpad_I,18.12 //
children.translated_text: therefore <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (repeated contemplation) is to be practiced until the Self is directly experienced. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.12 //

children.text: sad asmīti ca vijñānam akṣajo bādhate dhruvam /
children.translated_text: The knowledge 'I am existence' is certainly obstructed by sense-born cognition,

children.text: śabdotthaṃ dṛḍhasaṃskāro doṣaiś cākrṣyate bahiḥ // SamUpad_I,18.13 //
children.translated_text: for though born of the word of scripture, with firm impressions, it is dragged outward by the defects of the mind. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.13 //

children.text: śrutānumānajanmānau sāmānyaviṣayau yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since cognitions born of scripture and inference have a general object,

children.text: pratyayāv akṣajo 'vaśyaṃ viśeṣārtho nivārayet // SamUpad_I,18.14 //
children.translated_text: the sense-born cognition, having a particular object, necessarily obstructs them. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.14 //

children.text: vākyārthapratyayi kaścin nirduḥkho nopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: No one who merely believes in the meaning of the sentence is found to be free from suffering,

children.text: yadi vā dṛśyate kaścid vākyārthaśrutimātrataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.15 //
children.translated_text: or if someone is seen to be free, it is not from mere hearing of the sentence's meaning alone. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.15 //

children.text: nirduḥkho 'tītadeheṣu kṛtabhāvo 'numīyate /
children.translated_text: One who is free from suffering is inferred to have practiced contemplation in past lives;

children.text: caryā no 'śāstrasaṃvedyā syād aniṣṭaṃ tathā sati // SamUpad_I,18.16 //
children.translated_text: his conduct is not to be known merely through scripture—such would be undesirable if it were so. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.16 //

children.text: sad asīti phalaṃ coktvā vidheyaṃ sādhanaṃ yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since, having declared 'You are existence' as the result, a means is to be enjoined—

children.text: na tad anyat prasaṃkhyānāt prasiddhārtham iheṣyate // SamUpad_I,18.17 //
children.translated_text: that means is no other than <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (repeated contemplation)—this is the accepted meaning here. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.17 //

children.text: tasmād anubhavāyaiva prasaṃcakṣīta yatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the sake of direct experience alone, one should diligently contemplate,

children.text: tyajan sādhanatatsādhyaviruddhaṃ śamanādimān // SamUpad_I,18.18 //
children.translated_text: abandoning whatever is contrary to the means and its end, being endowed with <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and the like. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.18 //

children.text: naitad evaṃ rahasyānāṃ netinetyavasānataḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not so, for the esoteric teachings culminate in '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this)—

children.text: kriyāsādhyaṃ purā śrāvyaṃ na mokṣo nityasiddhataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.19 //
children.translated_text: liberation is not to be achieved through action, for it is to be taught first and is eternally established. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.19 //

children.text: putraduḥkhaṃ yathādhyastaṃ pitrāduḥkhe sva ātmani /
children.translated_text: Just as a father superimposes suffering for his son upon his own Self, which is free from suffering,

children.text: ahaṃkartrā tathādhyastaṃ nityāduḥkhe sva ātmani // SamUpad_I,18.20 //
children.translated_text: so too the ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) superimposes suffering upon the Self which is eternally free from suffering. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.20 //

children.text: so 'dhyāso neti netīti prāptavat pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: That superimposition is negated by '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), as though it had been actually attained,

children.text: bhūyo 'dhyāsavidhiḥ kaścit kutaścin nopapadyate // SamUpad_I,18.21 //
children.translated_text: and no further rule of superimposition arises from any source whatsoever. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.21 //

children.text: ātmanīha yathādhyāsaḥ pratiṣedhas tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Just as there is superimposition upon the Self here, so too there is its negation—

children.text: malādhyāsaniṣedhau khe kriyete ca yathābudhaiḥ // SamUpad_I,18.22 //
children.translated_text: just as the ignorant superimpose and negate impurity in space. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.22 //

children.text: prāptaś cet pratiṣidhyeta mokṣo 'nityo bhaved dhruvam /
children.translated_text: If what has actually been attained were to be negated, liberation would certainly be impermanent;

children.text: ato 'prāptaniṣedho 'yaṃ divy agnicayanādivat // SamUpad_I,18.23 //
children.translated_text: therefore this is the negation of what was never actually attained, like the celestial fire-altar and the like. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.23 //

children.text: saṃbhāvyo gocare śabdaḥ pratyayo vā na cānyathā /
children.translated_text: A word or cognition is possible only in the domain of objects, and not otherwise;

children.text: na saṃbhāvyau tadātmatvād ahaṃkartus tathaiva ca // SamUpad_I,18.24 //
children.translated_text: they are not possible in the Self, since the ego-sense is of that nature, being an object. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.24 //

children.text: ahaṃkartrātmani nyastaṃ caitanye kartṛtādi yat /
children.translated_text: Whatever doership and the like has been projected by the ego-sense upon the Self, upon pure consciousness—

children.text: neti netīti tat sarvaṃ sāhaṃkartrā niṣidhyate // SamUpad_I,18.25 //
children.translated_text: all of that is negated by '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), along with the ego-sense itself. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.25 //

children.text: upalabdhiḥ svayaṃjyotir dṛśiḥ pratyaksadakriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Apprehension, self-luminous, seeing, inward-facing, real, actionless,

children.text: sākṣāt sarvāntaraḥ sākṣī cetā nityo 'guṇo 'dvayaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.26 //
children.translated_text: directly present, innermost of all, the witness, the conscious one, eternal, without qualities, non-dual. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.26 //

children.text: saṃnidhau sarvadā tasya syāt tadābho 'bhimānakṛt /
children.translated_text: In its constant proximity, there arises its reflection, which creates the sense of self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>),

children.text: ātmātmīyaṃ dvayaṃ cātaḥ syād ahaṃmamagocaraḥ // SamUpad_I,18.27 //
children.translated_text: and from this arises the duality of 'self' and 'mine'—the domain of 'I' and 'my.' // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.27 //

children.text: jātikarmādimattvād dhi tasmiñ śabdās tv ahaṃkṛti /
children.translated_text: Since the ego-sense possesses birth, action, and the like, words apply to it;

children.text: na kaścid vartate śabdas tadabhāvāt sva ātmani // SamUpad_I,18.28 //
children.translated_text: but no word whatsoever applies to the Self itself, due to the absence of those attributes. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.28 //

children.text: ābhāso yatra tatraiva śabdāḥ pratyagdṛśiṃ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is a reflection, there alone words abide; though directed toward the inner seer,

children.text: lakṣayeyur na sākṣāt tam abhidadhyuḥ kathaṃcana // SamUpad_I,18.29 //
children.translated_text: they can only indicate it indirectly, never denote it directly in any way. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.29 //

children.text: nahy ajātyādimān kaścid arthaḥ śabdair nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: For no entity that is without birth and the like can be defined by words;

children.text: ātmābhāso yato 'haṃkṛd ātmaśabdais tathocyate // SamUpad_I,18.30 //
children.translated_text: since the ego-sense is a reflection of the Self, it is thus spoken of with Self-related words. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.30 //

children.text: ulmukādau yathāgnyarthāḥ parārthatvān na cāñjasā /
children.translated_text: Just as fire-related terms apply to a firebrand and the like not directly, since they serve another purpose,

children.text: mukhād anyo mukhābhāso yathādarśānukārataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.31 //
children.translated_text: so the reflection of a face is different from the face, being an imitation in a mirror. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.31 //

children.text: ābhāsān mukham apy evam ādarśānanuvartanāt /
children.translated_text: Just as the face is distinct from its reflection and does not follow the mirror,

children.text: ahaṃkṛty ātmanirbhāso mukhābhāsavad iṣyate // SamUpad_I,18.32 //
children.translated_text: so the reflection of the Self in the ego-sense is regarded as like the reflection of a face. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.32 //

children.text: mukhavat sthita ātmānyo 'viviktau tau tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Like the face, the Self abides unchanged; the other, the reflection—the two are undiscriminated, just so;

children.text: saṃsārī ca sa ity eka ābhāso yas tv ahaṃkṛti // SamUpad_I,18.33 //
children.translated_text: and the one called the transmigrating self is none other than the reflection in the ego-sense. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.33 //

children.text: vastu cchāyā smṛter anyan mādhuryādi ca kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Some say the reflection is a real entity different from memory, and the cause of sweetness and the like;

children.text: jñaikadeśo vikāro vā tadābhāsāśrayaḥ pare // SamUpad_I,18.34 //
children.translated_text: others say it is a part of cognition or a modification—the substratum of that reflection. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.34 //

children.text: ahaṃkartaiva saṃsārī svatantra iti kecana /
children.translated_text: Some say the ego-sense alone is the transmigrating self, being independent;

children.text: ahaṃkārādisaṃtānaḥ saṃsārī nānvayi pṛthak // SamUpad_I,18.35 //
children.translated_text: the continuum beginning with the ego-sense is the transmigrating self—not a persisting entity separate from it. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.35 //

children.text: ity evaṃ saugatā āhus tatra nyāyo vicāryatām /
children.translated_text: Thus the Buddhists (<s>Saugatā</s>) say; let the reasoning therein be examined.

children.text: saṃsāriṇāṃ kathā tv āstāṃ prakṛtaṃ tv adhunocyate // SamUpad_I,18.36 //
children.translated_text: But let the discussion of the transmigrating selves be set aside; the main topic is now stated. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.36 //

children.text: mukhābhāso ya ādarśe dharmo nānyatarasya saḥ /
children.translated_text: The reflection of a face in a mirror—that property belongs to neither one alone;

children.text: dvayor ekasya ced dharmo viyukte 'nyatare bhavet // SamUpad_I,18.37 //
children.translated_text: if it were the property of one of the two, it would exist when the other is removed. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.37 //

children.text: mukhena vyapadeśāt sa mukhasyaiveti cen matam /
children.translated_text: If one thinks that since it is designated by reference to the face, it belongs to the face alone—

children.text: nādarśānuvidhānāc ca mukhe saty avibhāvataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.38 //
children.translated_text: that is not so, since it follows the mirror and does not appear when only the face is present without a mirror. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.38 //

children.text: dvayor eveti cet tan na dvayor evāpy adarśanāt /
children.translated_text: If one says it belongs to both, that is not so either, since it is not seen belonging to both independently;

children.text: adṛṣṭasya sato dṛṣṭiḥ syād rāhoś candrasūryayoḥ // SamUpad_I,18.39 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, an unseen existing thing would become visible—like <s>Rāhu</s> appearing only during eclipses of the moon and sun. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.39 //

children.text: rāhoḥ prāg eva vastutvaṃ siddhaṃ śāstrapramāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: The reality of <s>Rāhu</s> is established beforehand on the authority of scripture;

children.text: chāyāpakṣe tv avastutvaṃ tasya syāt pūrvayuktitaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.40 //
children.translated_text: but on the view that the reflection is a shadow, its unreality would follow from the previous reasoning. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.40 //

children.text: chāyākrānter niṣedho 'yaṃ na tu vastutvasādhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is a negation of shadow-encroachment, not an establishment of reality;

children.text: na hy arthāntaraniṣṭhaṃ sad vākyam arthāntaraṃ vadet // SamUpad_I,18.41 //
children.translated_text: for a sentence established in one meaning cannot convey another meaning. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.41 //

children.text: mādhuryādi ca yat kāryam uṣṇadravyādyasevanāt /
children.translated_text: And the effect of sweetness and the like is produced through the non-employment of hot substances and the like,

children.text: chāyāyā na tv adṛṣṭatvād apām eva ca darśanāt // SamUpad_I,18.42 //
children.translated_text: not from the shadow, since it is not observed to produce such effects, while it is observed in water itself. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.42 //

children.text: ātmābhāsāśrayāś caivaṃ mukhābhāsāśrayā yathā /
children.translated_text: Thus, those who say the ego-sense is the substratum of the Self's reflection—just as the mirror is the substratum of the face's reflection—

children.text: gamyate śāstrayuktibhyām ābhāsāsattvam eva ca // SamUpad_I,18.43 //
children.translated_text: through scripture and reasoning, the unreality of the reflection itself is understood. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.43 //

children.text: na dṛśer avikāritvād ābhāsasyāpy avastutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the seer is changeless, and the reflection too is unreal,

children.text: nācititvād ahaṃkartuḥ kasya saṃsāritā bhavet // SamUpad_I,18.44 //
children.translated_text: and since the ego-sense is insentient—to whom then could transmigration belong? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.44 //

children.text: avidyāmātra evātaḥ saṃsāro 'stv avivekataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) exists only as mere <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), due to non-discrimination—

children.text: kūṭasthenātmanā nityam ātmavān ātmanīva saḥ // SamUpad_I,18.45 //
children.translated_text: while through the immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) Self, one ever possesses the Self, as if established in the Self alone. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.45 //

children.text: rajjusarpo yathā rajjvā sātmakaḥ prāg vivekataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the rope-snake, prior to discrimination, derives its being from the rope,

children.text: avastusann api hy eṣa kūṭasthenātmanā tathā // SamUpad_I,18.46 //
children.translated_text: so too this appearance, though unreal, derives its being from the immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.46 //

children.text: ātmābhāsāśrayaś cātmā pratyayaiḥ svair vikāravān /
children.translated_text: Some hold that the Self, as the substratum of its own reflection, undergoes modification through its own cognitions,

children.text: sukhī duḥkhī ca saṃsārī nitya eveti kecana // SamUpad_I,18.47 //
children.translated_text: experiencing happiness and suffering while transmigrating, yet being eternal. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.47 //

children.text: ātmābhāsāparijñānād yāthātmyena vimohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Not comprehending the reflection of the Self as it truly is, deluded,

children.text: ahaṃkartāram ātmeti manyante te nirāgamāḥ // SamUpad_I,18.48 //
children.translated_text: they consider the ego-sense to be the Self—they are without true scriptural understanding. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.48 //

children.text: saṃsāro vastusaṃs teṣāṃ kartṛbhoktṛtvalakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is real, characterized by being agents and experiencers;

children.text: ātmābhāsāśrayājñānāt saṃsaranty avivekataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.49 //
children.translated_text: due to ignorance dependent on the semblance of the Self, they transmigrate through non-discrimination. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.49 //

children.text: caitanyābhāsatā buddher ātmanas tatsvarūpatā /
children.translated_text: The semblance of consciousness belongs to the intellect, while its true nature belongs to the Self;

children.text: syāc cet taṃ jñānaśabdaiś ca vedaḥ śāstīti yujyate // SamUpad_I,18.50 //
children.translated_text: if so, then the <s>Veda</s> rightly instructs it with terms denoting knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.50 //

children.text: prakṛtipratyayārthau yau bhinnāv ekāśrayau yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the meanings of the verbal root and the affix, though distinct, share a single substrate,

children.text: karoti gacchatītyādau dṛṣṭau lokaprasiddhitaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.51 //
children.translated_text: as seen in [expressions like] 'makes' and 'goes' — from common worldly usage, // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.51 //

children.text: nānayor dvyāśrayatvaṃ tu loke dṛṣṭaṃ smṛtau tathā /
children.translated_text: their having two substrates is never seen in the world nor in <s>smṛti</s>;

children.text: jānātyartheṣu ko hetur dvyāśrayatve nigadyatām // SamUpad_I,18.52 //
children.translated_text: in 'knows objects' — what reason for two substrates? Let it be stated. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.52 //

children.text: ātmābhāsas tu tiṅvācyo dhātvarthaś ca dhiyaḥ kriyā /
children.translated_text: The semblance of the Self is denoted by the verbal ending (<s>tiṅ</s>), and the activity of the intellect is the meaning of the verbal root;

children.text: ubhayaṃ cāvivekena jānātīty ucyate mṛṣā // SamUpad_I,18.53 //
children.translated_text: both are falsely spoken of as 'knows' due to non-discrimination [of the two]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.53 //

children.text: na buddher avabodho 'sti nātmano vidyate kriyā /
children.translated_text: There is no cognition belonging to the intellect, nor does activity belong to the Self;

children.text: ato nānyatarasyāpi jānātīti ca yujyate // SamUpad_I,18.54 //
children.translated_text: therefore, 'knows' is not rightly applied to either one separately. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.54 //

children.text: nāpy ato bhāvaśabdena jñaptir ity api yujyate /
children.translated_text: Nor therefore is it proper that 'cognition' be expressed by an action-word (<s>bhāvaśabda</s>);

children.text: na hy ātmā vikriyāmātro nitya ātmetiśāsanāt // SamUpad_I,18.55 //
children.translated_text: for the Self is not mere modification, since the <s>śāstra</s> teaches that the Self is eternal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.55 //

children.text: na buddher buddhivācyatvaṃ karaṇaṃ na hy akartṛkam /
children.translated_text: Nor is the intellect denoted by a word for intellect [as agent], for an instrument is not without an agent;

children.text: nāpi jñāyata ity evaṃ karmaśabdair nirucyate // SamUpad_I,18.56 //
children.translated_text: nor is it expressed as 'is known' — that is, by words denoting objects of action. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.56 //

children.text: na yeṣām eka evātmā nirduḥkho 'vikriyaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: For those who do not hold that the Self is one, free from sorrow, and always changeless,

children.text: teṣāṃ syāc chabdavācyatvaṃ jñeyatvaṃ cātmanaḥ sadā // SamUpad_I,18.57 //
children.translated_text: the Self would always be expressible by words and always an object of knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.57 //

children.text: yadāhaṃkartur ātmatvaṃ tadā śabdārthamukhyatā /
children.translated_text: When selfhood belongs to the ego-agent, then the primary meaning of [such] words [applies];

children.text: nāśanāyādimattvāt tu śrutau tasyātmateṣyate // SamUpad_I,18.58 //
children.translated_text: but since it [the ego] has a beginning and destruction, the <s>śruti</s> does not accept it as the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.58 //

children.text: hanta tarhi na mukhyārtho nāpi gauṇaḥ kathaṃcana /
children.translated_text: Alas! Then neither the primary meaning nor any secondary meaning

children.text: jānātītyādiśabdasya gatir vācyā tathāpi tu // SamUpad_I,18.59 //
children.translated_text: of words like 'knows' [can apply] — the usage must still be explained. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.59 //

children.text: śabdānām ayathārthatve vedasyāpy apramāṇatā /
children.translated_text: If words are not true to their objects, then even the <s>Veda</s> would not be a valid means of knowledge;

children.text: sā ca neṣṭā tato grāhyā gatir asya prasiddhitaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.60 //
children.translated_text: and that is not desired — therefore the usage should be understood from common convention. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.60 //

children.text: prasiddhir mūḍhalokasya yadi grāhyā nirātmatā /
children.translated_text: If the convention of the deluded world is to be accepted, [then] the doctrine of no-self [would follow];

children.text: lokāyatikasiddhāntaḥ sa cāniṣṭaḥ prasajyate // SamUpad_I,18.61 //
children.translated_text: the doctrine of the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists) would thereby ensue — and that is undesirable. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.61 //

children.text: abhiyuktaprasiddhiś cet pūrvavad durvivekatā /
children.translated_text: If [you say] the convention of the learned [should apply] — [then the same] failure of discrimination [arises] as before;

children.text: gatiśūnyaṃ na vedo 'yaṃ pramāṇaṃ saṃvadaty uta // SamUpad_I,18.62 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Veda</s> is not devoid of meaning — it is authoritative and accords [with truth]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.62 //

children.text: ādarśamukhasāmānyaṃ mukhasyeṣṭaṃ hi mānavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The similarity between a mirror and a face is accepted by people;

children.text: mukhasya pratibimbo hi mukhākāreṇa dṛśyate // SamUpad_I,18.63 //
children.translated_text: for the reflection of the face is seen with the form of the face. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.63 //

children.text: yatra yasyāvabhāsas tu tayor evāvivekataḥ /
children.translated_text: Wherever there is a semblance of something — due to the non-discrimination of those two,

children.text: jānātīti kriyāṃ sarvo loko vakti svabhavataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.64 //
children.translated_text: everyone in the world naturally says the activity 'knows.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.64 //

children.text: buddheḥ kartṛtvam adhyasya jānātīti jña ucyate /
children.translated_text: By superimposing the agency of the intellect, the knower is said to 'know';

children.text: tathā caitanyam adhyasya jñatvaṃ buddher ihocyate // SamUpad_I,18.65 //
children.translated_text: likewise, by superimposing consciousness [on the intellect], the intellect is here said to have knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.65 //

children.text: svarūpaṃ cātmano jñānaṃ nityaṃ jyotiḥ śruter yataḥ /
children.translated_text: And the nature of the Self is knowledge — eternal light, as the <s>śruti</s> declares;

children.text: na buddhyā kriyate tasmān nātmanānyena vā sadā // SamUpad_I,18.66 //
children.translated_text: it is not produced by the intellect, nor by the Self, nor by anything else, ever. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.66 //

children.text: dehe 'haṃpratyayo yadvaj jānātīti ca laukikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as [there is] the I-notion in the body, so worldly people

children.text: vadanti jñānakartṛtvaṃ tadvad buddhes tathātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.67 //
children.translated_text: speak of knowledge as having an agent — and similarly of the intellect and the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.67 //

children.text: bauddhais tu pratyayair evaṃ kriyamāṇaiś ca cinnibhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Deluded by such cognitions which resemble consciousness,

children.text: mohitāḥ kriyate jñānam ity āhus tārkikā janāḥ // SamUpad_I,18.68 //
children.translated_text: the logicians say 'knowledge is produced.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.68 //

children.text: tasmāj jñābhāsabuddhīnām avivekāt pravartitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, arising from the non-discrimination of the knower, its semblance, and the cognitions,

children.text: jānātītyādiśabdaś ca pratyayo yā ca tatsmṛtiḥ // SamUpad_I,18.69 //
children.translated_text: are words like 'knows,' and the cognition and the memory thereof. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.69 //

children.text: ādarśānuvidhāyitvaṃ chāyāyā asyate mukhe /
children.translated_text: Just as the shadow [in a mirror] conforms to the mirror, so it is projected onto the face;

children.text: buddhidharmānukāritvaṃ jñābhāsasya tatheṣyate // SamUpad_I,18.70 //
children.translated_text: likewise, the semblance of the knower is accepted as conforming to the properties of the intellect. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.70 //

children.text: buddhes tu pratyayās tasmād ātmābhāsena dīpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The cognitions of the intellect, therefore, illuminated by the semblance of the Self,

children.text: grāhakā iva bhāsante dahantīvolmukādayaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.71 //
children.translated_text: appear as if they are perceivers, like whirling firebrands and the like [appear as circles]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.71 //

children.text: svayam evāvabhāsyante grāhakāḥ svayam eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'They illuminate themselves and are perceivers by themselves' —

children.text: ity evaṃ grāhakāstitvaṃ pratiṣedhanti saugatāḥ // SamUpad_I,18.72 //
children.translated_text: thus the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>) deny the existence of a [separate] perceiver. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.72 //

children.text: yady evaṃ nānyadṛśyās te kiṃ tadvāraṇam ucyatām /
children.translated_text: If so, they are not perceived by another — what then prevents [your view]? Let it be stated.

children.text: bhāvābhāvau hi teṣāṃ yau nānyagrāhyau sadā yadi // SamUpad_I,18.73 //
children.translated_text: For their existence and non-existence, if never grasped by another, // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.73 //

children.text: anvayī grāhakas teṣām ity etad api tatsamam /
children.translated_text: 'A continuous perceiver of them [exists]' — this [assertion] too has the same [problem],

children.text: acititvasya tulyatvād anyasmin grāhake sati // SamUpad_I,18.74 //
children.translated_text: since unconsciousness is equally [present], if another perceiver exists. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.74 //

children.text: adhyakṣasya samīpe tu siddhiḥ syād iti cen matam /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Establishment [of cognitions] would occur in the proximity of the witness (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) — if that is the view,

children.text: nādhyakṣe 'nupakāritvād anyatrāpi prasaṅgataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.75 //
children.translated_text: [Reply:] since the witness does not contribute, the same consequence would apply elsewhere too. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.75 //

children.text: arthī duḥkhī ca yaḥ śrotā sa tv adhyakṣo 'thavetaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The listener who is needy and suffering — is he the witness or the other?

children.text: adhyakṣasya ca duḥkhitvam arthitvaṃ ca na te matam // SamUpad_I,18.76 //
children.translated_text: You do not accept that the witness has suffering or neediness. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.76 //

children.text: kartādhyakṣaṃ sad asmīti naiva sadgraham arhati /
children.translated_text: The agent [who says] 'the witness is existent, I am' does not deserve such a true apprehension;

children.text: sad evāsīti mithyoktiḥ śruter api na yujyate // SamUpad_I,18.77 //
children.translated_text: even the <s>śruti</s> statement 'existence alone was' is not properly applicable [in that way], being a false assertion. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.77 //

children.text: avivicyobhayaṃ vakti śrutiś cet syād grahas tathā /
children.translated_text: If the <s>śruti</s> speaks without discriminating both, then the apprehension would be likewise [confused];

children.text: asmadas tu vivicyaiva tvam eveti vaded yadi // SamUpad_I,18.78 //
children.translated_text: but if, having discriminated from the 'I' [perspective], it says 'you are that,' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.78 //

children.text: pratyayānvayiniṣṭhatvam ukto doṣaḥ prasajyate /
children.translated_text: the stated fault of resting on the continuity of cognitions would follow;

children.text: tvam ity adhyakṣaniṣṭhaś ced ahamadhyakṣayoḥ katham // SamUpad_I,18.79 //
children.translated_text: if 'you' rests on the witness — how [is there a connection] between 'I' and the witness? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.79 //

children.text: saṃbandho vācya evātra yena tvam iti lakṣayet /
children.translated_text: The relation by which it would indicate 'you' must be stated here;

children.text: draṣṭṛdṛśyatvasaṃbandho yady adhyakṣe 'kriye katham // SamUpad_I,18.80 //
children.translated_text: if the relation of seer and seen [exists] in the witness, how [can it], since it is actionless? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.80 //

children.text: akriyatve 'pi tādātmyam adhyakṣasya bhaved yadi /
children.translated_text: Even if actionless, if the witness has identity [with the Self],

children.text: ātmādhyakṣo mamāstīti saṃbandhāgrahaṇe na dhīḥ // SamUpad_I,18.81 //
children.translated_text: without apprehending the relation, the cognition 'the witness is my Self' [would not arise]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.81 //

children.text: saṃbandhagrahaṇaṃ śāstrād iti cen manyase na hi /
children.translated_text: If you think the apprehension of the relation comes from scripture — no, indeed;

children.text: pūrvoktāḥ syus tridhā doṣā graho vā syān mameti ca // SamUpad_I,18.82 //
children.translated_text: the three previously stated faults would arise, or else [there would be] the apprehension 'mine.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.82 //

children.text: adṛśir dṛśirūpeṇa bhāti buddhir yadā sadā /
children.translated_text: When the intellect, which is not a seer, always appears in the form of a seer,

children.text: pratyayā api tasyāḥ syus taptāyovisphuliṅgavat // SamUpad_I,18.83 //
children.translated_text: its cognitions too would be like sparks from heated iron. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.83 //

children.text: ābhāsas tadabhāvaś ca dṛśeḥ sīmno na cānyathā /
children.translated_text: The semblance [of consciousness] and its absence are the limits of the seer, and not otherwise;

children.text: lokasya yuktitaḥ syātāṃ tadgrahaś ca tathā sati // SamUpad_I,18.84 //
children.translated_text: they would [be established] for the world through reasoning, and the apprehension of that [seer] would [follow] accordingly. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.84 //

children.text: nanv evaṃ dṛśisaṃkrāntir ayaḥpiṇḍe 'gnivad bhavet /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, the transference of seeing [to the intellect] would occur, like fire in an iron ball.

children.text: mukhābhāsavad ity etad ādarśe tan nirākṛtam // SamUpad_I,18.85 //
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Like the reflection of a face in a mirror — that [objection] has been refuted. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.85 //

children.text: kṛṣṇāyo rohitābhāsam ity etad dṛṣṭam ucyate /
children.translated_text: 'Black iron has a red appearance' — this is said from observation;

children.text: dṛṣṭadārṣṭāntatulyatvaṃ na tu sarvātmanā kvacit // SamUpad_I,18.86 //
children.translated_text: the equality of the observed and the illustration is never complete in all respects. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.86 //

children.text: tathaiva cetanābhāsaṃ cittaṃ caitanyavad bhavet /
children.translated_text: Just so, the mind, having the semblance of consciousness, would be as if conscious,

children.text: mukhābhāso yathādarśa ābhāsaś codito mṛṣā // SamUpad_I,18.87 //
children.translated_text: just as a mirror [has] the semblance of a face — and a semblance is declared to be unreal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.87 //

children.text: cittaṃ cetanam ity etac chāstrayuktivivarjitam /
children.translated_text: 'The mind is conscious' — this is devoid of scriptural and logical support;

children.text: dehasyāpi prasaṅgaḥ syāc cakṣurādes tathaiva ca // SamUpad_I,18.88 //
children.translated_text: the same consequence would apply to the body, and to the eye and the like as well. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.88 //

children.text: tad apy astv iti cet tan na lokāyatikasaṃgateḥ /
children.translated_text: If one says 'let that be so' — no, because that would accord with materialism (<s>Lokāyata</s>);

children.text: na ca dhīr dṛśir asmīti yady ābhāso na cetasi // SamUpad_I,18.89 //
children.translated_text: and the intellect would not [say] 'I am a seer,' if there were no semblance [of consciousness] in the mind. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.89 //

children.text: sad asmīti dhiyo 'bhāve vyarthaṃ syāt tat tvam asy api /
children.translated_text: In the absence of the cognition 'I am existent,' even '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (that thou art) would be meaningless;

children.text: yuṣmadasmadvivekajñe syād arthavad idaṃ vacaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.90 //
children.translated_text: for one who knows the distinction between 'you' and 'I,' this statement would be meaningful. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.90 //

children.text: mamedaṃpratyayau jñeyau yuṣmady eva na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Mine' and 'this' — these cognitions are to be known as belonging to 'you' (<s>yuṣmad</s>) alone, without doubt;

children.text: aham ity asmadīṣṭaḥ syād ayam asmīti cobhayoḥ // SamUpad_I,18.91 //
children.translated_text: 'I' is regarded as belonging to 'I' (<s>asmad</s>), while 'this I am' [partakes] of both. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.91 //

children.text: anyonyāpekṣayā teṣāṃ pradhānaguṇateṣyate /
children.translated_text: Their principal and subordinate status is accepted based on their mutual dependence;

children.text: viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatvaṃ tathā grāhyaṃ hi yuktitaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.92 //
children.translated_text: the relation of qualifier and qualified should be understood accordingly through reasoning. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.92 //

children.text: mamedaṃ dvayam apy etan madhyamasya viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Mine' and 'this' — both of these are qualifications of the middle [term, 'I'];

children.text: dhanī gomān yathā tadvad deho 'haṃkartur eva ca // SamUpad_I,18.93 //
children.translated_text: just as 'wealthy' or 'owning cows' [qualify a person], so too the body [qualifies] the ego-agent alone. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.93 //

children.text: buddhyārūḍhaṃ sadā sarvaṃ sāhaṃkartrā ca sākṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Everything always rests upon the intellect, together with the ego-agent and the witness;

children.text: tasmāt sarvāvabhāso jñaḥ kiṃcid apy aspṛśan sadā // SamUpad_I,18.94 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the knower is the illuminator of all, while never touching anything whatsoever. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.94 //

children.text: pratilomam idaṃ sarvaṃ yathoktaṃ lokabuddhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: All this is the reverse of what has been stated from the worldly standpoint;

children.text: avivekadhiyām asti nāsti sarvaṃ vivekinām // SamUpad_I,18.95 //
children.translated_text: it exists for those of undiscriminating minds — for the discriminating, none of it exists. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.95 //

children.text: anvayavyatirekau hi padārthasya padasya ca /
children.translated_text: The co-presence and co-absence of the referent and the word

children.text: syād etad aham ity atra yuktir evāvadhāraṇe // SamUpad_I,18.96 //
children.translated_text: in 'this is I' — reason alone is [the means of] ascertainment here. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.96 //

children.text: nādrākṣam aham iti asmin suṣupte 'nyan manāg api /
children.translated_text: 'I did not see' — in this [statement about] deep sleep, nothing else whatsoever [was perceived];

children.text: na vārayati dṛṣṭiṃ svāṃ pratyayaṃ tu niṣedhati // SamUpad_I,18.97 //
children.translated_text: it does not negate its own seeing, but negates the cognition [of objects]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.97 //

children.text: svayaṃjyotir na hi draṣṭur ity evaṃ saṃvido 'stitām /
children.translated_text: For the seer is self-luminous — thus, the existence of awareness,

children.text: kauṭasthyaṃ ca tathā tasyāḥ pratyayasya ca luptatām /
children.translated_text: and likewise its immutability, and the dissolution of [objective] cognition —

children.text: svayam evābravīc chāstraṃ pratyayāvagatī pṛthak // SamUpad_I,18.98 //
children.translated_text: scripture itself declared that awareness and cognition are distinct. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.98 //

children.text: evaṃ vijñātavākyārthe śrutilokaprasiddhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the meaning of the [Vedāntic] statement has been understood from scriptural and worldly convention,

children.text: śrutis tat tvam asīty āha śrotur mohāpanuttaye // SamUpad_I,18.99 //
children.translated_text: the <s>śruti</s> says '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (that thou art) for the removal of the listener's delusion. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.99 //

children.text: brahmā dāśarather yadvad uktyaivāpānudat tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Brahmā</s> dispelled the darkness of <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) by speech alone,

children.text: tasya viṣṇutvasaṃbodhe na yatnāntaram ūcivān // SamUpad_I,18.100 //
children.translated_text: when awakening him to his nature as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he did not prescribe any other effort. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.100 //

children.text: ahaṃśabdasya yā niṣṭhā jyotiṣi pratyagātmani /
children.translated_text: The ultimate referent of the word 'I' is the light that is the inner Self;

children.text: saivoktā sad asīty evaṃ phalaṃ tatra vimuktatā // SamUpad_I,18.101 //
children.translated_text: this is what is stated as 'you are existence' — and the fruit thereof is liberation. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.101 //

children.text: śrutamātre na cet tat syāt kāryaṃ tatra bhaved dhruvam /
children.translated_text: If that [liberation] does not [occur] upon mere hearing, then further practice would certainly be required;

children.text: vyavahārāt purāpīṣṭaḥ sadbhāvaḥ svayam ātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.102 //
children.translated_text: but the existence of the Self was already accepted even prior to worldly activity. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.102 //

children.text: aśanāyādinirmuktyai tatkālā jāyate pramā /
children.translated_text: For liberation from hunger and the like, valid knowledge arises at that very time;

children.text: tattvamasyādivākyārthe triṣu kāleṣv asaṃśayaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.103 //
children.translated_text: regarding the meaning of statements like '<s>tat tvam asi</s>,' [the knowledge is valid] in all three times, without doubt. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.103 //

children.text: pratibandhavihīnatvāt svayaṃ cānubhavātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since there is no obstruction, and since it is self-experienced in nature,

children.text: jāyetaiva pramā tatra svātmany eva na saṃśayaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.104 //
children.translated_text: valid knowledge would certainly arise there, regarding one's own Self — there is no doubt. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.104 //

children.text: kiṃ sad evāham asmīti kiṃ vānyat pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Does one realize 'I am existence indeed,' or something else?

children.text: sad eva ced ahaṃśabdaḥ satā mukhyārtha iṣyatām // SamUpad_I,18.105 //
children.translated_text: If it is 'existence' indeed, let the word 'I' be accepted in its primary meaning [as referring to] existence. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.105 //

children.text: anyac cet sadahaṃgrāhapratipattir mṛṣaiva sā /
children.translated_text: If it is something else, then the apprehension that 'existence' and 'I' [denote the same] is indeed false;

children.text: tasmān mukhyagrahe nāsti vāraṇāvagater iha // SamUpad_I,18.106 //
children.translated_text: therefore, when the primary meaning is grasped, there is no [further] obstacle to understanding here. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.106 //

children.text: pratyayī pratyayaś caiva yadābhāsau tadarthatā /
children.translated_text: When the cognizer and the cognition both appear as semblances, their purposefulness [arises];

children.text: tayor acitimattvāc ca caitanye kalpyate phalam // SamUpad_I,18.107 //
children.translated_text: since both lack consciousness, the fruit is attributed to consciousness [itself]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.107 //

children.text: kūṭasthe 'pi phalaṃ yogyaṃ rājanīva jayādikam /
children.translated_text: Even in the immutable [Self], the fruit is fitting, like victory and the like for a king;

children.text: tadanātmatvahetubhyāṃ kriyāyāḥ pratyayasya ca // SamUpad_I,18.108 //
children.translated_text: because both action and cognition are not the Self, [the fruit belongs to the Self]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.108 //

children.text: ādarśas tu yadābhāso mukhākāraḥ sa eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mirror has a semblance, that is the very form of the face — that itself is that;

children.text: yathaivaṃ pratyayādarśo yadābhāsas tadā hy aham // SamUpad_I,18.109 //
children.translated_text: just so, the mirror of cognition — when it has a semblance, then it is 'I.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.109 //

children.text: ity evaṃ pratipattiḥ syāt sad asmīti ca nānyathā /
children.translated_text: Thus the realization would be 'I am existent' and not otherwise;

children.text: tat tvam ity upadeśo 'pi dvārābhāvād anarthakaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.110 //
children.translated_text: [otherwise] the instruction '<s>tat tvam</s>' (that thou [art]) would also be purposeless, due to the absence of a [proper] gateway [of understanding]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.110 //

children.text: śrotuḥ syād upadeśaś ced arthavattvaṃ tathā bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the instruction is for the listener, then it would indeed have meaning;

children.text: adhyakṣasya na ced iṣṭaṃ śrotṛtvaṃ kasya tad bhavet // SamUpad_I,18.111 //
children.translated_text: if listenership is not accepted for the witness, to whom would that [instruction] belong? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.111 //

children.text: adhyakṣasya samīpe buddher eveti cen matam /
children.translated_text: If [you say] in the proximity of the witness, it belongs to the intellect alone — if that is the view,

children.text: na tatkṛtopakāro 'sti kāṣṭhād yadvan na kalpyate // SamUpad_I,18.112 //
children.translated_text: [then] there is no benefit produced by it [for the witness], just as none is conceived from a log of wood. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.112 //

children.text: buddhau cet tatkṛtaḥ kaścin nanv evaṃ pariṇāmitā /
children.translated_text: If some [benefit] produced by it exists in the intellect — then surely there is modification;

children.text: ābhāse 'pi ca ko doṣaḥ sati śrutyādyanugrahe // SamUpad_I,18.113 //
children.translated_text: and what fault is there in [accepting] the semblance, given the support of <s>śruti</s> and the like? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.113 //

children.text: ābhāse pariṇāmaś cen na rajjvādinibhatvavat /
children.translated_text: If there is modification in the semblance — no, because it is like a rope and the like [being mistaken for a snake];

children.text: sarpādeś ca tathāvocam ādarśe ca mukhatvavat // SamUpad_I,18.114 //
children.translated_text: as I stated regarding the snake and the like — and like the [appearance of a] face in a mirror. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.114 //

children.text: nātmābhāsatvasiddhiś ced ātmano grahaṇāt pṛthak /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The establishment of the Self as a semblance cannot be proven apart from the apprehension of the Self;

children.text: mukhādes tu pṛthaksiddhir iha tv anyonyasaṃśrayaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.115 //
children.translated_text: the face and the like are established independently — but here there is mutual dependence. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.115 //

children.text: adhyakṣasya pṛthaksiddhāv ābhāsasya tadīyatā /
children.translated_text: If the witness is independently established, then the semblance belongs to it;

children.text: ābhāsasya tadīyatve hy adhyakṣavyatiriktatā // SamUpad_I,18.116 //
children.translated_text: and if the semblance belongs to it, then the distinctness of the witness [from the semblance is established]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.116 //

children.text: naivaṃ svapne pṛthaksiddheḥ pratyayasya dṛśes tathā /
children.translated_text: Not so [is there mutual dependence] — since in dreams, the cognition and the seer are independently established,

children.text: rathādes tatra śūnyatvāt pratyayasyātmanā grahaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.117 //
children.translated_text: since there is the absence of a chariot and the like therein, the cognition is grasped by the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.117 //

children.text: avagatyā hi saṃvyāptaḥ pratyayo viṣayākṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: A cognition, pervaded by awareness, having the form of an object,

children.text: jāyate sa yadākāraḥ sa bāhyo viṣayo mataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.118 //
children.translated_text: arises; that form which it has is considered the external object. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.118 //

children.text: karmepsitatamatvāt sa tadvān kārye niyujyate /
children.translated_text: Being the most desired as an object of action, one possessed of it is engaged in activity;

children.text: ākāro yatra cārpyeta karaṇaṃ tad ihocyate // SamUpad_I,18.119 //
children.translated_text: that in which the form is deposited is called here the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.119 //

children.text: yadābhāsena saṃvyāptaḥ sa jñāteti nigadyate /
children.translated_text: That by whose reflection [the cognition] is pervaded, he is called the knower;

children.text: trayam etad vivicyātra yo jānāti sa ātmavit // SamUpad_I,18.120 //
children.translated_text: one who discriminates these three here—he is a knower of the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.120 //

children.text: samyaksaṃśayamithyoktāḥ pratyayā vyabhicāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Correct, doubtful, and erroneous—cognitions are variable;

children.text: ekaivāvagatis teṣu bhedas tu pratyayārpitaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.121 //
children.translated_text: but awareness in them is one alone; the difference is attributed to the cognition. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.121 //

children.text: ādhibhedād yathā bhedo maṇer avagates tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as there is differentiation of a gem due to difference in its base, so too of awareness;

children.text: aśuddhiḥ pariṇāmaś ca sarvaṃ pratyayasaṃśrayāt // SamUpad_I,18.122 //
children.translated_text: impurity and transformation—all are due to dependence on cognition. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.122 //

children.text: prathanaṃ grahaṇaṃ siddhiḥ pratyayānām ihānyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Manifestation, apprehension, and establishment of cognitions [come] here from another;

children.text: āparokṣyāt tad evoktam anumānaṃ pradīpavat // SamUpad_I,18.123 //
children.translated_text: due to its immediacy, that is called inference, like a lamp. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.123 //

children.text: kim ajñaṃ grāhayet kaścit pramāṇena tu kenacit /
children.translated_text: Would someone cause an unknown [entity] to be known by some means of valid knowledge?

children.text: vinaiva tu pramāṇena nivṛttyānyasya śeṣataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.124 //
children.translated_text: But without any means of knowledge, [it is established] by the cessation [of superimposition] upon the remainder of the other. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.124 //

children.text: śabdenaiva pramāṇena nivṛttiś ced ihocyate /
children.translated_text: If it is said that cessation [of superimposition] occurs here through scripture as the sole means of knowledge,

children.text: adhyakṣasyāprasiddhatvāc chūnyataiva prasajyate // SamUpad_I,18.125 //
children.translated_text: then since the witness (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) is not [independently] established, sheer voidness would result. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.125 //

children.text: cetanas tvaṃ kathaṃ deha iti cen nāprasiddhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] 'You are conscious, how can you be the body?'—if [you say this], it is not [valid] because of non-establishment;

children.text: cetanasyānyatāsiddhāv evaṃ syād anyahānataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.126 //
children.translated_text: if the otherness of the conscious [Self from the body] were already established, then it would be so, [but that means] loss of the other [position]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.126 //

children.text: adhyakṣaḥ svayam asty eva cetanasyāparokṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: The witness exists by itself, due to the immediacy of the conscious [Self];

children.text: tulya evaṃ prabodhaḥ syād ajñasyāsattvavādinā // SamUpad_I,18.127 //
children.translated_text: thus the awakening [of the ignorant] would be the same as that [proposed] by the advocate of non-existence. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.127 //

children.text: aham ajñāsiṣaṃ cedam iti lokasmṛter iha /
children.translated_text: From the common memory 'I did not know this,'

children.text: karaṇaṃ karma kartā ca siddhās tv ekakṣaṇe kila // SamUpad_I,18.128 //
children.translated_text: the instrument, action, and agent are indeed established here in a single moment, it is claimed. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.128 //

children.text: prāmāṇye 'pi smṛteḥ śaighryād yaugapadyaṃ vibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: Even if memory is valid, simultaneity is perceived [only] due to its swiftness;

children.text: krameṇa grahaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ smṛteḥ paścāt tathaiva ca // SamUpad_I,18.129 //
children.translated_text: apprehension comes first in sequence, and then memory [comes] later, likewise. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.129 //

children.text: ajñāsiṣam idaṃ māṃ cety apekṣā jāyate dhruvam /
children.translated_text: The expectation 'I did not know this, and [did not know] me' certainly arises;

children.text: viśeṣo 'pekṣyate yatra tatra naivaikakālatā // SamUpad_I,18.130 //
children.translated_text: where a distinction is expected, there is certainly no simultaneity. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.130 //

children.text: ātmano grahaṇe cāpi trayāṇām iha saṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: And in the apprehension of the Self too, since the three [agent, action, object] are possible here,

children.text: ātmany āsaktakartṛtvaṃ na syāt karaṇakarmaṇoḥ // SamUpad_I,18.131 //
children.translated_text: doership cannot be inherently attached to the Self, [which is distinct] from the instrument and the object. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.131 //

children.text: vyāptum iṣṭaṃ ca yat kartuḥ kriyayā karma tat smṛtam /
children.translated_text: What the agent desires to pervade through action—that is remembered as the object;

children.text: ato hi kartṛtantratvaṃ tasyeṣṭaṃ nānyatantratā // SamUpad_I,18.132 //
children.translated_text: therefore its dependence on the agent is accepted, not dependence on another. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.132 //

children.text: śabdād vānumiter vāpi pramāṇād vā tato 'nyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether from scripture, inference, or from some other means of valid knowledge,

children.text: siddhiḥ sarvapadārthānāṃ syād ajñaṃ prati nānyathā // SamUpad_I,18.133 //
children.translated_text: the establishment of all entities can occur for the ignorant—not otherwise. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.133 //

children.text: adhyakṣasyāpi siddhiḥ syāt pramāṇena vinaiva vā /
children.translated_text: Even the establishment of the witness may be with or without a means of valid knowledge;

children.text: vinā svasya prasiddhis tu nājñaṃ praty upayujyate // SamUpad_I,18.134 //
children.translated_text: but establishment [of the Self] by itself, without [external means], is not useful for the ignorant. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.134 //

children.text: tasyaivājñatvam iṣṭaṃ cej jñātatve 'nyā mitir bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the ignorance of that very [Self] is maintained, then for its being known, another cognition would be needed;

children.text: anyasyaivājñatāyāṃ ca tadvijñāne dhruvā bhavet // SamUpad_I,18.135 //
children.translated_text: and if that other too is unknown, then certainly [yet another cognition] would be needed for its knowledge. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.135 //

children.text: jñātatā svātmalābho vā siddhiḥ syād anyad eva vā /
children.translated_text: Being known, or the attainment of one's own Self—which would be the establishment, or something else?

children.text: jñātatve 'nantaroktau tvaṃ pakṣau saṃsmartum arhasi // SamUpad_I,18.136 //
children.translated_text: If it is being known, you should remember the two positions stated just before. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.136 //

children.text: siddhiḥ syāt svātmalābhaś ced yatnas tatra nirarthakaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the establishment is the attainment of one's own Self, effort in that regard is purposeless,

children.text: sarvalokaprasiddhatvāt svahetubhyas tu vastunaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.137 //
children.translated_text: since the thing is already established for the whole world, arising from its own causes. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.137 //

children.text: jñānajñeyādivāde 'taḥ siddhir jñātatvam ucyate /
children.translated_text: In the doctrine of knowledge and knowable, therefore, establishment is called 'being known';

children.text: adhyakṣādhyakṣyayoḥ siddhir jñeyatvaṃ nātmalābhatā // SamUpad_I,18.138 //
children.translated_text: the establishment of the witness and what it witnesses is knowability, not self-attainment. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.138 //

children.text: spaṣṭatvaṃ karmakartrādeḥ siddhatā yadi kalpyate /
children.translated_text: If establishment is conceived as the clarity of action, agent, and the like,

children.text: spaṣṭatāspaṣṭate syātām anyasyaiva na cātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.139 //
children.translated_text: the states of clarity and obscurity would belong to the other alone, not to the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.139 //

children.text: adraṣṭur naiva cāndhasya spaṣṭībhāvo ghaṭasya tu /
children.translated_text: Just as there is no becoming-clear for a blind person who cannot see, but [only] for the pot;

children.text: kartrādeḥ spaṣṭateṣṭā ced draṣṭṛtādhyakṣakartṛkā // SamUpad_I,18.140 //
children.translated_text: if clarity of the agent and the like is desired, the seer-ship belongs to the witness. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.140 //

children.text: anubhūteḥ kim antasmin syāt tavāpekṣayā vada /
children.translated_text: What would be beyond experience in this regard? Tell me, according to your view.

children.text: anubhavitarīṣṭā syāt so 'py anubhūtir eva naḥ // SamUpad_I,18.141 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] it is desired in the experiencer—he too is nothing but experience for us. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.141 //

children.text: "abhinno 'pi hi buddhyātmā viparyāsitadarśanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Though the intellect-self (<s>buddhyātman</s>) is non-different, by those of perverted vision,

children.text: grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittibhedavān iva lakṣyate" // SamUpad_I,18.142 //
children.translated_text: it is perceived as if possessing the distinction of grasped, grasper, and awareness." // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.142 //

body.text: bhūtir yeṣāṃ kriyā saiva kārakaṃ saiva cocyate /
body.translated_text: For those whose existence is action itself, and that alone is called the instrument;

children.text: sattvaṃ nāśitvam asyāś cet sakartṛtvaṃ tatheṣyatām /
children.translated_text: if its existence implies its destructibility, then let it also be admitted as having agency;

children.text: na kaścic ceṣyate dharma iti cet pakṣahānatā // SamUpad_I,18.143 //
children.translated_text: if [you say] no property whatsoever is accepted, then that is abandonment of your own position. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.143 //

children.text: nanv astitvādayo dharmā nāstitvādinivṛttayaḥ /
