children.translated_text: [Objection:] But surely existence and the like are properties, being the negation of non-existence and the like.

children.text: na bhūtes tarhi nāśitvaṃ svālakṣaṇyaṃ hi te // SamUpad_I,18.144 //
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Then destructibility does not belong to the entity; for those [properties] are your own particular characteristics. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.144 //

children.text: svalakṣaṇāvadhir nāśo nāśo 'nāśanivṛttitā /
children.translated_text: Destruction is the limit of one's own particular characteristic; destruction is the cessation of non-destruction;

children.text: agor asattvaṃ gotvaṃ te na tu tad goḥ svalakṣaṇam // SamUpad_I,18.145 //
children.translated_text: the non-existence of a non-cow is cow-ness for you, but that is not the particular characteristic of a cow. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.145 //

children.text: kṣaṇavācyo 'pi yo 'rthaḥ syāt so 'py anyābhāva eva te /
children.translated_text: Whatever entity might be denoted by 'momentary,' that too is merely the absence of another for you;

children.text: bhedābhāve 'py abhāvasya bhedo nāmabhir iṣyate // SamUpad_I,18.146 //
children.translated_text: even in the absence of difference, difference of non-existence is accepted through names. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.146 //

children.text: nāmabhedair anekatvam ekasya syāt kathaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: How could there be multiplicity of a single thing through differences of names for you?

children.text: apoho yadi bhinnānāṃ vṛttis tasya kathaṃ gavi // SamUpad_I,18.147 //
children.translated_text: If [the meaning is] exclusion (<s>apoha</s>), how could the application of that operate in [the case of] a cow? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.147 //

children.text: nābhāvā bhedakāḥ sarve viśeṣā vā kadācana /
children.translated_text: Absences are never differentiators, nor particulars at any time;

children.text: nāmajātyādayo yadvat saṃvidas te 'viśeṣataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.148 //
children.translated_text: name, universals, and the like are cognitions for you, due to non-distinction. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.148 //

children.text: pratyakṣam anumānaṃ vā vyavahāre yadīcchasi /
children.translated_text: If you accept perception or inference in practical usage,

children.text: kriyākārakabhedais tad abhyupeyaṃ dhruvaṃ bhavet // SamUpad_I,18.149 //
children.translated_text: then the distinctions of action and instruments must certainly be conceded. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.149 //

children.text: tasmān nīlaṃ tathā pītaṃ ghaṭādir vā viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, blue, yellow, pot, and the like are qualifiers

children.text: saṃvidas tad upetyaṃ syād yena cāpy anubhūyate // SamUpad_I,18.150 //
children.translated_text: of awareness; that must be accepted, and also that by which [awareness] is experienced. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.150 //

children.text: rūpādīnāṃ yathānyaḥ syād grāhyatvād grāhakas tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as there is something other than forms and the like, since they are objects of apprehension, so too the apprehender;

children.text: pratyayasya tathānyaṃ syād vyañjakatvāc ca dīpavat // SamUpad_I,18.151 //
children.translated_text: likewise there is something other than cognition, since it illumines, like a lamp. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.151 //

children.text: adhyakṣasya dṛśeḥ kīdṛk saṃbandhaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: What kind of connection of the witness (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) with seeing will be possible?

children.text: adhyakṣyeṇa tu dṛśyena muktvānyo draṣṭṛdṛśyatām // SamUpad_I,18.152 //
children.translated_text: Setting aside the seer-and-seen relation, [what connection is there] with the witnessed object? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.152 //

children.text: adhyakṣeṇa kṛtā dṛṣṭir dṛśyaṃ vyāpnoty athāpi vā /
children.translated_text: Is seeing created by the witness such that it pervades the seen, or rather

children.text: nityādhyakṣakṛtaḥ kaścid upakāro bhaved dhiyām // SamUpad_I,18.153 //
children.translated_text: does the eternal witness render some assistance to the intellects? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.153 //

children.text: sa coktas tannibhatvaṃ prāk saṃvyāptiś ca ghaṭādiṣu /
children.translated_text: That has been stated earlier: [the intellect's] resemblance to it, and the pervading of pots and the like;

children.text: yathālokādisaṃvyāptir vyañjakatvād dhiyas tathā // SamUpad_I,18.154 //
children.translated_text: just as there is pervading by light and the like, so too through the illuminating nature of the intellect. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.154 //

children.text: ālokastho ghaṭo yadvad buddhyārūḍho bhavet tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a pot standing in light [becomes visible], so too [an object] mounted on the intellect;

children.text: dhīvyāptiḥ syād ghaṭāroho dhiyo vyāptau kramo bhavet // SamUpad_I,18.155 //
children.translated_text: the pervading by the intellect would be the pot's mounting on the intellect; in the pervading of the intellect, there would be a sequence. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.155 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ syāt pratyayavyāptis tato 'nugraha ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: First there would be the pervading of the cognition, then the favor of the Self;

children.text: kṛtsnādhyakṣasya so 'yuktaḥ kālākāśādivat kramaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.156 //
children.translated_text: [but] that sequence is improper for the all-witnessing [Self], like time, space, and the like. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.156 //

children.text: viṣayagrahaṇaṃ yasya kāraṇāpekṣayā bhavet /
children.translated_text: One whose apprehension of objects depends on causes,

children.text: saty eva grāhyaśeṣe ca pariṇāmī sa cittavat // SamUpad_I,18.157 //
children.translated_text: and who, even when the remainder of the apprehensible exists, [undergoes change]—he is mutable, like the mind. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.157 //

children.text: adhyakṣo 'ham iti jñānaṃ buddher eva viniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The knowledge 'I am the witness' is a determination of the intellect alone;

children.text: nādhyakṣasyāviśeṣatvān na tasyāsti paro yataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.158 //
children.translated_text: it does not belong to the witness, since it is undifferentiated, and since nothing higher than it exists. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.158 //

children.text: kartrā ced aham ity evam anubhūyeta muktatā /
children.translated_text: If liberation were to be experienced as 'I am the agent' [of liberation],

children.text: sukhaduḥkhavinirmoko nāhaṃkartari yujyate // SamUpad_I,18.159 //
children.translated_text: then freedom from pleasure and pain would not be possible for one who is the ego-agent. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.159 //

children.text: dehādāv abhimānottho duḥkhīti pratyayo dhruvam /
children.translated_text: The cognition 'I am suffering' certainly arises from false identification with the body and the like;

children.text: kuṇḍalipratyayo yadvat pratyagātmābhimāninā // SamUpad_I,18.160 //
children.translated_text: just as the cognition of an earring [arises] for one who falsely identifies with the inner Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.160 //

children.text: bādhyate pratyayeneha vivekenāvivekavān /
children.translated_text: One who lacks discrimination is here sublated by the cognition born of discrimination;

children.text: viparyaye 'sadantaṃ syāt pramāṇasyāpramāṇataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.161 //
children.translated_text: in the opposite case, it would end in unreality, due to the invalidity of the [sublating] means of knowledge. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.161 //

children.text: dāhacchedavināśeṣu duḥkhitvaṃ nānyathātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: In burning, cutting, and destruction, the suffering does not otherwise belong to the Self;

children.text: naiva hy anyasya dāhādāv anyo duḥkhī bhavet kvacit // SamUpad_I,18.162 //
children.translated_text: for indeed, in the burning and the like of another, no other person ever becomes the sufferer anywhere. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.162 //

children.text: asparśatvād adehatvān nāhaṃ dāhyo yataḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Since I am intangible and bodiless, I am never to be burned;

children.text: tasmān mithyābhimānotthaṃ mṛte putre mṛtir yathā // SamUpad_I,18.163 //
children.translated_text: therefore [the suffering] arises from false identification, like [the sorrow of] death when [hearing of] the death of a son. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.163 //

children.text: kuṇḍaly aham iti hy etad bādhyetaiva vivekinā /
children.translated_text: The [cognition] 'I am wearing an earring' is indeed sublated by the discriminating person;

children.text: duḥkhīti pratyayas tadvat kevalāhaṃdhiyā sadā // SamUpad_I,18.164 //
children.translated_text: likewise the cognition 'I am suffering' [is sublated] always by the pure I-consciousness alone. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.164 //

children.text: siddhe suḥkhitva iṣṭaṃ syāt taccaktitvaṃ sadātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the happiness-nature [of the Self] is established, its capacity [for happiness] is the eternal nature of the Self;

children.text: mithyābhimānato duḥkhī tenārthāpādanakṣayaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.165 //
children.translated_text: one suffers from false identification; thereby the inference by implication is destroyed. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.165 //

children.text: asparśo 'pi yathā sparśam acalaś calanādi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as the intangible [Self appears to have] touch, and the immovable [appears to have] movement and the like,

children.text: avivekāt tathā duḥkhaṃ mānasaṃ cātmanīkṣate // SamUpad_I,18.166 //
children.translated_text: so too through non-discrimination, mental suffering is seen as [belonging to] the Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.166 //

children.text: vivekātmadhiyā duḥkhaṃ nudyate calanādivat /
children.translated_text: Through the discriminating awareness of the Self, suffering is repelled, like movement and the like;

children.text: avivekasvabhāvena mano gacchaty anicchataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.167 //
children.translated_text: through the non-discriminating nature of the mind, [it] proceeds involuntarily. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.167 //

children.text: tadānudṛśyate duḥkhaṃ naiścalye naiva tasya tat /
children.translated_text: Suffering is seen following that [mind]; in [the Self's] immobility, that [suffering] does not belong to it;

children.text: pratyagātmani tasmāt tad duḥkhaṃ naivopapadyate // SamUpad_I,18.168 //
children.translated_text: therefore, suffering does not at all belong to the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.168 //

children.text: tvaṃsatos tulyanīḍatvān nīlāśvavad idaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Since 'you' (<s>tvam</s>) and 'that' (<s>tat</s>) share the same locus, this would be like [saying] 'a blue horse';

children.text: nirduḥkhavācinā yogāt tvaṃśabdasya tadarthatā // SamUpad_I,18.169 //
children.translated_text: through the connection of the word 'you' with [the word] denoting the suffering-free [<s>Brahman</s>], that meaning [of freedom from suffering attaches to 'you']. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.169 //

children.text: pratyagātmābhidhānena tacchabdasya yutes tathā /
children.translated_text: Through the connection of that word (<s>tat</s>) with the designation of the inner Self,

children.text: daśamas tvam asīty evaṃ vākyaṃ syāt pratyagātmani // SamUpad_I,18.170 //
children.translated_text: the sentence 'You are the tenth' (<s>daśamas tvam asi</s>) would be [analogous] to [the sentence about] the inner Self. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.170 //

children.text: svārthasya hy aprahāṇena viśiṣṭārthasamarpakau /
children.translated_text: Without abandoning their own meanings, [the two words] convey a qualified meaning;

children.text: pratyagātmāvagatyantau nānyo 'rtho 'rthād virodhy ataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.171 //
children.translated_text: [the sentence] terminates in the awareness of the inner Self; no other meaning is contradictory to this meaning. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.171 //

children.text: navabuddhyapahārād dhi svātmānaṃ daśapūraṇam /
children.translated_text: Due to the removal [of Self-knowledge] by the nine cognitions [of the body, etc.], one who does not see one's own Self as the completion of the ten

children.text: apaśyañ jñātum evecchet svam ātmānaṃ janas tathā // SamUpad_I,18.172 //
children.translated_text: yet desires to know one's own Self—so too is the case with people. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.172 //

children.text: avidyābaddhacakṣuṣṭvāt kāmāpahṛtadhīḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: With eyes bound by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), with understanding always stolen by desires,

children.text: viviktaṃ dṛśim ātmānaṃ nekṣate daśamaṃ yathā // SamUpad_I,18.173 //
children.translated_text: one does not see the Self, which is isolated seeing, just as [one does not see] the tenth man. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.173 //

children.text: daśamas tvam asīty evaṃ tattvamasyādivākyataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are the tenth' (<s>daśamas tvam asi</s>)—thus, from sentences like '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That you are),

children.text: svam ātmānaṃ vijānāti kṛtsnāntaḥkaraṇekṣaṇam // SamUpad_I,18.174 //
children.translated_text: one knows one's own Self as the seer of the entire inner organ. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.174 //

children.text: idaṃ pūrvam idaṃ paścāt padaṃ vākye bhaved iti /
children.translated_text: 'This word comes first, this comes after in the sentence'—

children.text: niyamo naiva vede 'sti padasāṃgatyam arthataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.175 //
children.translated_text: there is no such fixed rule in the <s>Veda</s>; the connection of words is [determined] by meaning. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.175 //

children.text: vākye hi śrūyamāṇānāṃ padānām arthasaṃsmṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the words of a sentence are being heard, the meanings of the individual words are recalled;

children.text: anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tato vākyārthabodhanam // SamUpad_I,18.176 //
children.translated_text: from the methods of <s>anvaya</s> (agreement) and <s>vyatireka</s> (difference), the understanding of the sentence-meaning [arises]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.176 //

children.text: yadā nityeṣu vākyeṣu padārthas tu vivicyate /
children.translated_text: When the meaning of words in eternal [Vedic] sentences is analyzed for the purpose of conveying sentence-meaning,

children.text: vākyārthajñānasaṃkrāntyai tadā praśno na yujyate // SamUpad_I,18.177 //
children.translated_text: then questioning is not appropriate. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.177 //

children.text: anvayavyatirekoktiḥ padārthasmaraṇāya tu /
children.translated_text: The statement of <s>anvaya</s> (agreement) and <s>vyatireka</s> (difference) is for the purpose of recalling the word-meanings;

children.text: smṛtyabhāve na vākyārtho jñātuṃ śakyo bi kenacit // SamUpad_I,18.178 //
children.translated_text: without memory, the sentence-meaning cannot be known by anyone. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.178 //

children.text: tattvamasyādivākyeṣu tvaṃpadārthāvivekataḥ /
children.translated_text: In sentences like '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That you are), due to the non-discrimination of the meaning of the word 'you' (<s>tvam</s>),

children.text: vyajyate naiva vākyārtho nityamukto 'ham ity ataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.179 //
children.translated_text: the sentence-meaning—'I am eternally liberated'—is not revealed. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.179 //

children.text: anvayavyatirekoktis tadvivekāya nānyathā /
children.translated_text: The statement of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> is for the discrimination of that [word 'you'], not otherwise;

children.text: tvaṃpadārthaviveke hi pāṇāv arpitavilvavat // SamUpad_I,18.180 //
children.translated_text: for when the meaning of the word 'you' is discriminated, [the sentence-meaning is] like a <s>bilva</s> fruit placed in the hand. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.180 //

children.text: vākyārtho vyajyate caivaṃ kevalo 'haṃpadārthataḥ /
children.translated_text: The sentence-meaning is thus revealed solely from the meaning of the word 'I' (<s>aham</s>),

children.text: duḥkhīty etadapohena pratyagātmaviniścayāt // SamUpad_I,18.181 //
children.translated_text: by the removal of [the notion] 'I am suffering,' through the ascertainment of the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>). // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.181 //

children.text: tatraivaṃ saṃbhavaty arthe śrutahānāśrutārthadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: If in this interpretation, [there arises] the understanding of an unheard meaning while abandoning the heard meaning,

children.text: naivaṃ kalpayituṃ yuktā padavākyārthakovidaiḥ // SamUpad_I,18.182 //
children.translated_text: such an interpretation should never be made by those skilled in word and sentence meanings. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.182 //

children.text: pratyakṣādīni bādheran kṛṣṇalādiṣu pākavat /
children.translated_text: Perception and the like would sublate [such interpretations], like cooking <s>kṛṣṇala</s> seeds and the like;

children.text: akṣajādinibhair etaiḥ kathaṃ syād vākyabādhanam // SamUpad_I,18.183 //
children.translated_text: how could there be sublation of the sentence by these [cognitions] which are comparable to sense-perception and the like? // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.183 //

children.text: duḥkhy asmīti sati jñāne nirduḥkhīti na jāyate /
children.translated_text: When there is the knowledge 'I am suffering,' the [knowledge] 'I am free from suffering' does not arise;

children.text: pratyakṣādinibhatve 'pi vākyān na vyabhicārataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.184 //
children.translated_text: yet even though [the former is] comparable to sense-perception and the like, [it is not ultimately valid] because the sentence does not deviate [from truth]. // <s>SamUpad</s> I,18.184 //

children.text: svapne duḥkhy aham adyāsaṃ dāhacchedādihetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: In a dream, 'I was suffering today, due to burning, cutting, and other causes'—

children.text: tatkālabhāvibhir vākyair na bādhaḥ kriyate yadi // SamUpad_I,18.185 //
children.translated_text: if the statements referring to that time do not sublate [the suffering]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.185 //

children.text: samāptes tarhi duḥkhasya prāk ca tadbādha iṣyatām /
children.translated_text: Then let the sublation of suffering be accepted even before its cessation;

children.text: na hi duḥkhasya saṃtāno bhrānter vā dṛśyate kvacit // SamUpad_I,18.186 //
children.translated_text: for a continuity of suffering or of delusion is never observed anywhere. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.186 //

children.text: pratyagātmana ātmatvaṃ duḥkhy asmīty asya bādhayā /
children.translated_text: The selfhood of the inner Self [is established] by the sublation of 'I am a sufferer';

children.text: daśamaṃ navam asyeva veda ced aviruddhatā // SamUpad_I,18.187 //
children.translated_text: just as [counting] the tenth [person who was] the ninth — if this is known, there is no contradiction. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.187 //

children.text: nityamuktatvavijñānaṃ vākyād bhavati nānyataḥ /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of being eternally liberated arises from the [Vedāntic] statement alone, not from anything else;

children.text: vākyārthasyāpi vijñānaṃ padārthasmṛtipūrvakam // SamUpad_I,18.188 //
children.translated_text: and the knowledge of the meaning of the statement is preceded by the recollection of the meaning of the words. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.188 //

children.text: anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ padārthaḥ smaryate dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Through co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), the meaning of a word is certainly recalled;

children.text: evaṃ nirduḥkham ātmānam akriyaṃ pratipadyate // SamUpad_I,18.189 //
children.translated_text: thus one realizes the Self as free from suffering and actionless. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.189 //

children.text: sad evetyādivākyebhyaḥ pramā sphuṭatarā bhavet /
children.translated_text: From statements like 'existence alone [was in the beginning],' a clearer valid knowledge would arise,

children.text: daśamas tvam asīty asmād yathaivaṃ pratyagātmani // SamUpad_I,18.190 //
children.translated_text: just as [from] 'you are the tenth' — so too regarding the inner Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.190 //

children.text: prabodhena yathā svāpnaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ nivartate /
children.translated_text: Just as upon awakening, all the suffering of a dream ceases,

children.text: pratyagātmadhiyā tadvad duḥkhitvaṃ sarvadātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.191 //
children.translated_text: so too, through the knowledge of the inner Self, the suffering of the Self at all times [ceases]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.191 //

children.text: kṛṣṇalādau pramājanma tadanyārthāmṛdutvataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the case of a [weighing] stone and the like, knowledge arises because the object to be known is not [already] intimately familiar;

children.text: tattvamasyādivākyeṣu na tv evam avirodhataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.192 //
children.translated_text: but in statements like '<s>tat tvam asi</s>,' it is not so, since there is no contradiction [with prior self-awareness]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.192 //

children.text: vākye tat tvam asīty asmiñ jñātārthaṃ tadasidvayam /
children.translated_text: In the statement '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (that thou art), the meaning of 'that' and 'existence' are [already] known;

children.text: tvamarthasmṛtyasāhāyyād vākyaṃ notpādayet pramām // SamUpad_I,18.193 //
children.translated_text: without the aid of the recollection of the meaning of 'thou,' the statement would not produce valid knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.193 //

children.text: tattvamos tulyanīḍārtham asīty etat padaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'That' and 'thou' would have a shared referent; 'art' (<s>asi</s>) would be the [linking] word;

children.text: tacchabdaḥ pratyagātmārthas tacchabdārthas tvamas tathā // SamUpad_I,18.194 //
children.translated_text: the word 'that' refers to the inner Self, and the meaning of 'that' is also [the meaning of] 'thou.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.194 //

children.text: duḥkhitvāpratyagātmatvaṃ vārayetām ubhāv api /
children.translated_text: Both would exclude suffering and non-selfhood [of the inner Self];

children.text: evaṃ ca netinetyarthaṃ gamayetāṃ parasparam // SamUpad_I,18.195 //
children.translated_text: and thus they would mutually convey the meaning of '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.195 //

children.text: evaṃ tat tvam asīty asya gamyamāne phale katham /
children.translated_text: When the fruit of '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' is thus understood, how

children.text: apramāṇatvam asyoktvā kriyāpekṣatvam ucyate // SamUpad_I,18.196 //
children.translated_text: can one, having declared it to lack authority, then say it requires action? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.196 //

children.text: tasmād ādyantamadhyeṣu kurv ity etad virodhy ataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the injunction 'do!' at the beginning, middle, and end is contradictory [to knowledge];

children.text: na kalpyam aśrutatvāc ca śrutatyāgo 'py anarthakaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.197 //
children.translated_text: it should not be imagined, since it is unheard [in scripture], and the abandonment of what is heard would be purposeless. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.197 //

children.text: yathānubhūyate tṛptir bhujer vākyān na gamyate /
children.translated_text: Just as satisfaction is experienced from eating, not known from a statement [about eating],

children.text: vākyasya vidhṛtis tadvad gośakṛtpāyasīkriyā // SamUpad_I,18.198 //
children.translated_text: so too is the holding back of the [Vedāntic] statement — like [expecting] milk from cow dung. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.198 //

children.text: satyam evam anātmārthe vākyāt pārokṣyabodhanam /
children.translated_text: It is true that regarding what is not the Self, the statement gives only indirect knowledge;

children.text: pratyagātmani na tv evaṃ saṃkhyāprāptivad adhruvam // SamUpad_I,18.199 //
children.translated_text: but regarding the inner Self, it is not so — [the knowledge is] not uncertain, like the knowledge of a number or an attainment. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.199 //

children.text: svasaṃvedyatvaparyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Self-awareness as a synonym [for self-luminosity] —

children.text: svapramāṇaka iṣyatām /
children.translated_text: let it be accepted as self-validating;

children.text: nivṛttāv ahamaḥ siddhaḥ svātmano 'nubhavaś ca naḥ // SamUpad_I,18.200 //
children.translated_text: upon the cessation of the ego, the Self is established, and our experience of one's own Self [is established]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.200 //

children.text: buddhīnāṃ viṣayo duḥkhaṃ tā yasya viṣayā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Suffering is the object of cognitions; those [cognitions] are regarded as objects of which [Self]?

children.text: kuto 'sya duḥkhasaṃbandho dṛśeḥ syāt pratyagātmanaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.201 //
children.translated_text: How could there be a connection of suffering with the seer, the inner Self? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.201 //

children.text: dṛśir evānubhūyeta svenaivānubhavātmanā /
children.translated_text: Seeing alone would be experienced, by its own nature which is experience itself;

children.text: tadābhāsatayā janma dhiyo 'syānubhavaḥ smṛtaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.202 //
children.translated_text: through its semblance, the arising of cognition is called its experience. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.202 //

children.text: aśanāyādinirmuktaḥ siddho mokṣas tvam eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from hunger and the like — liberation is already accomplished; you are that very [Self];

children.text: śrotavyādi tavety etad viruddhaṃ katham ucyate // SamUpad_I,18.203 //
children.translated_text: 'You should hear,' and so on — how is this contradictory [instruction] spoken [to you]? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.203 //

children.text: setsyatīty eva cet tat syāc chravaṇādi tadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'it will be accomplished [in the future],' then hearing and the like would be [required];

children.text: mokṣasyānityataivaṃ syād virodhy evānyathā vacaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.204 //
children.translated_text: liberation would thus be impermanent — any other statement is contradictory. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.204 //

children.text: śrotṛśrotavyayor bhedo yadīṣṭaḥ syād bhaved idam /
children.translated_text: If a difference between the listener and what is to be heard is desired, this [objection] would arise;

children.text: iṣṭārthakopa evaṃ syān na yuktaṃ sarvathā vacaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.205 //
children.translated_text: [but] this would undermine the desired conclusion — the statement is not proper in any way. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.205 //

children.text: siddho mokṣo 'ham ity evaṃ jñātvātmānaṃ bhaved yadi /
children.translated_text: If, having known the Self as 'liberation is already accomplished, I am [that],' [one still seeks to act],

children.text: cikīrṣur yaḥ sa mūḍhātmā śāstraṃ codghāṭayaty api // SamUpad_I,18.206 //
children.translated_text: such a deluded person even opens the scripture [looking for injunctions to act]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.206 //

children.text: na hi siddhasya kartavyaṃ sakāryasya na siddhatā /
children.translated_text: For what is already accomplished has nothing to be done; what has something to be done is not accomplished;

children.text: ubhayālambanaṃ kurvann ātmānaṃ vañcayaty asau // SamUpad_I,18.207 //
children.translated_text: one who grasps both [simultaneously] deceives oneself. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.207 //

children.text: siddho mokṣas tvam ity etad vastumātraṃ pradarśyate /
children.translated_text: 'Liberation is accomplished, you are that' — this merely shows the reality as it is;

children.text: śrotus tathātvavijñāne pravṛttiḥ syāt kathaṃ tv iti // SamUpad_I,18.208 //
children.translated_text: when the listener knows its true nature, how could there be any impulse to act? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.208 //

children.text: kartā duḥkhy aham asmīti pratyakṣeṇānubhūyate /
children.translated_text: 'I am an agent, I am a sufferer' — this is experienced as if by direct perception;

children.text: kartā duḥkhī ca mā bhūvam iti yatno bhavet tataḥ // SamUpad_I,18.209 //
children.translated_text: 'May I not be an agent or a sufferer' — from that, effort would arise. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.209 //

children.text: tadvijñānāya yuktyādi kartavyaṃ śrutir abravīt /
children.translated_text: For the realization of that, the <s>śruti</s> has prescribed reasoning and the like as things to be done;

children.text: kartṛtvādyanuvādena siddhatvānubhavāya tu // SamUpad_I,18.210 //
children.translated_text: but only by [first] reiterating the [apparent] agency, [does it lead] to the experience of one's accomplished [nature]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.210 //

children.text: nirduḥkho niṣkriyo 'kāmaḥ siddho mokṣo 'ham ity api /
children.translated_text: Free from suffering, actionless, desireless — 'liberation is accomplished, I am [that]';

children.text: gṛhītvaiva viruddhārtham ādadhyāt katham eva saḥ // SamUpad_I,18.211 //
children.translated_text: having grasped this, how could one take up a contradictory purpose? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.211 //

children.text: sakāmaḥ sakriyo 'siddha iti me 'nubhavaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: 'I have desires, I have activities, I am unaccomplished' — how can this be my experience?

children.text: ato me viparītasya tad bhavān vaktum arhati // SamUpad_I,18.212 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the reversal of this — may you be pleased to teach me that. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.212 //

children.text: ihaiva ghaṭate praśno na muktatvānubhūtaye /
children.translated_text: Here indeed the question is relevant, not for the experience of being liberated;

children.text: pramāṇena virodhī yaḥ so 'trārthaḥ praśnam arhati // SamUpad_I,18.213 //
children.translated_text: that meaning which contradicts a means of valid knowledge deserves questioning. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.213 //

children.text: ahaṃ nirmukta ity eṣa sad asīty anyamānajaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am liberated' — this, born from a different means of knowledge [i.e., scripture] like 'you are existence';

children.text: pratyakṣābhāsajanyatvād duḥkhitvaṃ praśnam arhati // SamUpad_I,18.214 //
children.translated_text: but being a sufferer, born from apparent direct perception, deserves questioning. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.214 //

children.text: pṛṣṭam ākāṅkṣitaṃ vācyaṃ duḥkhābhāvam abhīpsitam /
children.translated_text: What is asked, what is desired to be stated, is the absence of suffering that is wished for:

children.text: kathaṃ hīdaṃ nivarteta duḥkhaṃ sarvātmanā mama // SamUpad_I,18.215 //
children.translated_text: 'How indeed can this suffering of mine be completely removed?' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.215 //

children.text: iti praśnānurūpaṃ yad vācyaṃ duḥkhanivartakam /
children.translated_text: That which is to be stated in accordance with the question, as the remover of suffering —

children.text: śruteḥ svātmani nāśaṅkā prāmāṇye sati vidyate // SamUpad_I,18.216 //
children.translated_text: from the <s>śruti</s>, there is no doubt regarding one's own Self, when its validity is [established]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.216 //

children.text: tasmād ātmavimuktatvaṃ pratyāyayati tadvacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that statement conveys the liberatedness of the Self;

children.text: vaktavyaṃ tu tathārthaṃ syād virodhe 'sati kenacit // SamUpad_I,18.217 //
children.translated_text: and it should be stated to have that meaning, when there is no contradiction with anything. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.217 //

children.text: ito 'nyo 'nubhavaḥ kaścid ātmano nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: No other experience of the Self apart from this is logically possible;

children.text: avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ vijñātāram iti śruteḥ // SamUpad_I,18.218 //
children.translated_text: [as the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'The unknown of the knowers,' and 'the knower.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.218 //

children.text: tvaṃpadārthavivekāya saṃnyāsaḥ sarvakarmaṇām /
children.translated_text: For the discrimination of the meaning of 'thou,' the renunciation of all actions

children.text: sādhanatvaṃ vrajaty eva śānto dāntādiśāsanāt // SamUpad_I,18.219 //
children.translated_text: becomes a means — from the scriptural instruction of being tranquil, self-controlled, and the like. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.219 //

children.text: tvamarthaṃ pratyagātmānaṃ paśyed ātmānam ātmani /
children.translated_text: One should see the inner Self, the meaning of 'thou,' as the Self within the Self;

children.text: vākyārthaṃ tata ātmānaṃ sarvaṃ paśyati kevalam // SamUpad_I,18.220 //
children.translated_text: then one sees the Self alone as everything — that is the meaning of the statement. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.220 //

children.text: sarvam ātmeti vākyārthe vijñāte 'sya pramāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: When the meaning of the statement 'everything is the Self' is known through valid means,

children.text: asattve hy anyamānasya vidhis taṃ yojayet katham // SamUpad_I,18.221 //
children.translated_text: since any other cognition is non-existent, how could an injunction connect one [to action]? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.221 //

children.text: tasmād vākyārthavijñānān nordhvaṃ karmavidhir bhavet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, after the knowledge of the meaning of the statement, no injunction to act remains;

children.text: na hi brahmāsmi karteti viruddhe bhavato dhiyau // SamUpad_I,18.222 //
children.translated_text: for 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' and 'I am an agent' are contradictory cognitions. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.222 //

children.text: brahmāsmīti hi vidyeyaṃ naiva karteti bādhyate /
children.translated_text: This knowledge 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' is never sublated by 'I am not an agent';

children.text: sakāmo baddha ity evaṃ pramāṇābhāsajātayā // SamUpad_I,18.223 //
children.translated_text: 'I have desires, I am bound' — [these arise] from mere semblances of valid means of knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.223 //

children.text: śāstrād brahmāsmi nānyo 'ham iti buddhir bhaved dṛḍhā /
children.translated_text: From scripture, the firm conviction 'I am <s>Brahman</s>, I am not other' would arise;

children.text: yadāyuktā tadaivaṃ dhīr yathā dehātmadhīr iti // SamUpad_I,18.224 //
children.translated_text: when established, this cognition [is as natural] as the [false but habitual] cognition 'the body is the Self.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.224 //

children.text: sabhayād abhayaṃ prāptas tadarthaṃ yatate ca yaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who has reached fearlessness from a state of fear, and strives for that [fearlessness],

children.text: sa punaḥ sabhayaṃ gantuṃ svatantraś cen na hīcchati // SamUpad_I,18.225 //
children.translated_text: if free, does not desire to go back to a state of fear. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.225 //

children.text: yatheṣṭācaraṇaprāptiḥ saṃnyāsādividhau kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where is the attainment of acting as one pleases in the injunction of renunciation and the like,

children.text: padārthājñānabuddhasya vākyārthānubhavārthinaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.226 //
children.translated_text: for one who is awakened to the meaning of the words and seeks the experience of the meaning of the statement? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.226 //

body.text: ataḥ sarvam idaṃ siddhaṃ yat prāg asmābhir īritam // SamUpad_I,18.227 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, all that we have previously stated is established. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.227 //

children.text: yo hi yasmād viraktaḥ syān nāsau tasmai pravartate /
children.translated_text: One who is dispassionate toward something does not engage in it;

children.text: lokatrayād viraktatvān mumukṣuḥ kim itīhate // SamUpad_I,18.228 //
children.translated_text: being dispassionate toward the three worlds, why should the seeker of liberation strive [for them]? // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.228 //

children.text: kṣudhayā pīḍyamāno 'pi na viṣaṃ hy attum icchati /
children.translated_text: Even when afflicted by hunger, one does not wish to eat poison;

children.text: miṣṭānnadhvastatṛḍ jānan nāmūḍhas taj jighatsati // SamUpad_I,18.229 //
children.translated_text: one whose thirst has been quenched by delicious food, if not deluded, does not crave it [again]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.229 //

children.text: vedāntavākyapuṣpebhyo jñānāmṛtamadhūttamam /
children.translated_text: Salutation to that true teacher (<s>sadguru</s>) who, like a bee from the flowers of Vedāntic statements,

children.text: ujjahārālivad yo nas tasmai sadgurave namaḥ // SamUpad_I,18.230 //
children.translated_text: extracted for us the supreme nectar of knowledge! // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18.230 //

body.text: iti tattvamasiprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,18 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on '<s>Tat Tvam Asi</s>' (That Thou Art) (<s>Tattvamasiprakaraṇa</s>). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.18 //

children.text: prayujya tṛṣṇājvaranāśakāraṇaṃ cikitsitaṃ jñānavirāgabheṣajam /
children.translated_text: Having applied the treatment that is the cause of the destruction of the fever of craving — the medicine of knowledge and dispassion —

children.text: na yāti kāmajvarasannipātajāṃ śarīramālāśatayogaduḥkhitām // SamUpad_I,19.1 //
children.translated_text: [the Self] does not undergo the suffering of hundreds of garlands of bodies born from the affliction of the fever of desire. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.1 //

children.text: ahaṃ mameti tvam anartham īhase parārtham icchanti tavānya īhitam /
children.translated_text: 'I' and 'mine' — you strive for what is purposeless; your others desire what is for another's benefit.

children.text: na te 'rthabodho na hi me 'sti cārthitā tataś ca yuktaḥ śama eva te manaḥ // SamUpad_I,19.2 //
children.translated_text: You have no understanding of the goal, nor do I have any need — therefore, O mind, tranquility alone is fitting for you. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.2 //

children.text: yato na cānyaḥ paramāt sanātanāt sadaiva tṛpto 'ham ato na me 'rthitā /
children.translated_text: Since there is nothing other than the supreme eternal [Self], I am always satisfied — therefore I have no need;

children.text: sadaiva muktaś ca na kāmaye hitaṃ yatasva cetaḥ praśamāya te 'dhikam // SamUpad_I,19.3 //
children.translated_text: I am always liberated and do not desire what is beneficial — O mind, strive all the more for your pacification. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.3 //

children.text: ṣaḍūrmimālābhyativṛtta eva yaḥ sa eva cātmā jagataś ca naḥ śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: That which has completely transcended the garland of the six waves [of existence] — that alone is the Self of the world and of us, according to <s>śruti</s>;

children.text: pramāṇataś cāpi mayā pravedyate mudhaiva tasmāc ca manas tavehitam // SamUpad_I,19.4 //
children.translated_text: and it is made known by me through valid means of knowledge — therefore, O mind, your striving is in vain. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.4 //

children.text: tvayi praśānte na hi sāsti bhedadhīr yato jagan moham upaiti māyayā /
children.translated_text: When you are at peace, there is no cognition of difference; for the world falls into delusion through <s>māyā</s>;

children.text: graho hi māyāprabhavasya kāraṇaṃ grahād vimoke na hi sāsti kasyacit // SamUpad_I,19.5 //
children.translated_text: grasping is indeed the cause of what arises from <s>māyā</s>; upon release from grasping, it does not exist for anyone. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.5 //

children.text: na me 'sti mohas tava ceṣṭitena hi prabuddhatattvas tv asito hy avikriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: I have no delusion from your activity; for I am one whose true nature is awakened, taintless, and changeless;

children.text: na pūrvatattvottarabhedatā hi no vṛthaiva tasmāc ca manas tavehitam // SamUpad_I,19.6 //
children.translated_text: there is no distinction between the prior reality and the subsequent — therefore, O mind, your striving is in vain. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.6 //

children.text: yataś ca nityo 'ham ato na cānyathā vikārayoge hi bhaved anityatā /
children.translated_text: Since I am eternal, there is no otherwise; for with the occurrence of modification, there would be impermanence.

children.text: sadā prabhāto 'ham ato hi cādvayo vikalpitaṃ cāpy asad ity avasthitam // SamUpad_I,19.7 //
children.translated_text: I am always luminous, and therefore non-dual — and what is conceptualized is established as unreal. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.7 //

children.text: abhāvarūpaṃ tvam asīha he mano nirīkṣyamāṇe na hi yuktito 'stitā /
children.translated_text: You are of the nature of non-existence, O mind — when examined, your existence is not [established] by reasoning;

children.text: sato hy anāśād asato 'py ajanmato dvayaṃ ca te 'tas tava nāstiteṣyate // SamUpad_I,19.8 //
children.translated_text: since the existent cannot be destroyed and the non-existent cannot be born, both [qualities apply to] you — therefore your existence is not accepted. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.8 //

children.text: draṣṭā ca dṛśyaṃ ca tathā ca darśanaṃ bhramaḥ sa sarvas tava kalpito hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: The seer, the seen, and seeing — all that delusion is fabricated by you;

children.text: dṛśeś ca bhinnaṃ na hi dṛśyam īkṣyate svapan vibodhe ca tathā na bhidyate // SamUpad_I,19.9 //
children.translated_text: for nothing seen is perceived as different from seeing — in dreaming and waking alike, there is no real distinction. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.9 //

children.text: vikalpanā cāpi tathādvayā bhaved avastuyogāt tad alātacakravat /
children.translated_text: And conceptual construction too would be non-dual, due to the absence of a real object — like the circle of a whirling firebrand;

children.text: na śaktibhedo 'sti yato na cātmanāṃ tato 'dvayatvaṃ śrutito 'vasīyate // SamUpad_I,19.10 //
children.translated_text: since there is no difference of powers, nor among selves — therefore non-duality is ascertained from <s>śruti</s>. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.10 //

children.text: mithaś ca bhinnā yadi te hi cetanāḥ kṣayas tu teṣāṃ parimāṇayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: If those conscious beings are mutually different, then their destruction due to having measure [i.e., limitation]

children.text: dhruvo bhaved bhedavatāṃ hi dṛṣṭato jagatkṣayaś cāpi samastamokṣataḥ // SamUpad_I,19.11 //
children.translated_text: would certainly follow, as observed among things with parts — and the destruction of the world [would follow] from universal liberation. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.11 //

children.text: na me 'sti kaścin na ca so 'smi kasyacid yato 'dvayo 'haṃ na hi cāsti kalpitam /
children.translated_text: I have no one, nor do I belong to anyone, since I am non-dual; nor does anything fabricated exist;

children.text: akalpitaś cāsmi purā prasiddhito vikalpanāyā dvayam eva kalpitam // SamUpad_I,19.12 //
children.translated_text: and I am unfabricated, as known from the beginning — duality itself is merely the fabrication of conceptual construction. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.12 //

children.text: vikalpanā cāpy abhave na vidyate sad anyad ity evam ato na nāstitā /
children.translated_text: And conceptual construction does not exist in non-existence; [nor does the claim] 'there exists something else' — therefore there is no non-existence;

children.text: yataḥ pravṛttā tava cāpi kalpanā purā prasiddher na ca tad vikalpitam // SamUpad_I,19.13 //
children.translated_text: since your conceptualization too proceeds from what is known from the beginning, and that is not conceptually constructed. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.13 //

children.text: asad dvayaṃ te 'pi hi yad yad īkṣyate na dṛṣṭam ity eva na caiva nāstitā /
children.translated_text: Whatever duality of yours is seen is indeed unreal — but 'it is not seen' does not amount to non-existence;

children.text: yataḥ pravṛttā sadasadvikalpanā vicāravac cāpi tathādvayaṃ ca sat // SamUpad_I,19.14 //
children.translated_text: since the conceptualization of existence and non-existence proceeds from [the real] — and upon investigation, existence is non-dual. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.14 //

children.text: sad abhyupetaṃ bhavatopakalpitaṃ vicārahetor yadi tasya nāstitā /
children.translated_text: If the existence accepted by you is [merely] fabricated for the sake of investigation, then it would be non-existent;

children.text: vicārahānāc ca tathaiva saṃsthitaṃ na cet tad iṣṭaṃ nitarāṃ sad iṣyate // SamUpad_I,19.15 //
children.translated_text: and if, upon the cessation of investigation, it remains the same — if that is not accepted, then it must be accepted as supremely real. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.15 //

children.text: asatsamaṃ caiva sad ity apīti ced anarthavattvāt kharaśṛṅgatulyataḥ /
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'existence is the same as non-existence' — [that is rejected] because it would be purposeless, like a hare's horn;

children.text: anarthavattvaṃ tv asati hy akāraṇaṃ na caiva tasmān na viparyaye 'nyathā // SamUpad_I,19.16 //
children.translated_text: purposelessness, however, is groundless in what is non-existent — and therefore there is no reversal [of the established truth]. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.16 //

children.text: asiddhataś cāpi vicārakāraṇād dvayaṃ ca tasmāt prasṛtaṃ hi māyayā /
children.translated_text: And since unestablished, [duality arises only] from the cause of investigation; and duality has therefore sprung forth through <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: śruteḥ smṛteś cāpi tathā hi yuktitaḥ prasiddhyatītthaṃ na tu yujyate 'nyathā // SamUpad_I,19.17 //
children.translated_text: From <s>Śruti</s>, from <s>Smṛti</s>, and likewise from reasoning, this is established thus; it is not fitting otherwise. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.17 //

children.text: vikalpanāc cāpi vidharmakaṃ śruteḥ purā prasiddheś ca vikalpato 'dvayam /
children.translated_text: And also from the attribution of contrary properties in scripture, and from the prior establishment through attribution of the non-dual—

children.text: na ceti netīti tathā vikalpitaṃ niṣidhyate 'trāpy avaśeṣasiddhaye // SamUpad_I,19.18 //
children.translated_text: and what is attributed through '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) is negated here too, for the establishment of the remainder. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.18 //

children.text: akalpite 'py evam ajādvayākṣare vikalpayantaḥ sad asac ca janmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though in the unattributed, unborn, non-dual, Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), those who superimpose existence and non-existence through births,

children.text: svacittamāyāprabhavaṃ ca te bhavaṃ jarāṃ ca mṛtyuṃ ca niyānti saṃtatam // SamUpad_I,19.19 //
children.translated_text: and whose existence arises from the delusion of their own mind—they continually undergo birth, old age, and death. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.19 //

children.text: bhavābhavatvaṃ tu na ced avasthitir na tasya cānyas tv iti janma nānyathā /
children.translated_text: But if the Self's state is neither being nor non-being, and there is no other entity from it—then birth is not otherwise possible.

children.text: sato hy asattvād asataś ca sattvato na ca kriyā kārakam ity ato 'py ajam // SamUpad_I,19.20 //
children.translated_text: For the existent cannot become non-existent, nor the non-existent become existent; and since there is no action or agent, therefore it is unborn. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.20 //

children.text: akurvad iṣṭaṃ yadi vāsya kārakaṃ na kiṃcid anyan nanu nāsty akārakam /
children.translated_text: If, not acting, it is desired as a cause, or if its agent is nothing else—surely there is no non-agent.

children.text: sato 'viśeṣād asataś ca saccyutau tulāntayor yadvad aniścayān na hi // SamUpad_I,19.21 //
children.translated_text: Since there is no distinction from the existent, and since the non-existent falls away from existence—like the two pans of a balance, there is indeed no certainty. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.21 //

children.text: na cet sa iṣṭaḥ sadasadviparyayaḥ kathaṃ bhavaḥ syāt sadasadvyavasthitau /
children.translated_text: If the reversal of existence and non-existence is not accepted, how could birth occur when existence and non-existence are firmly established in their own natures?

children.text: vibhaktam etad dvayam apy avasthitaṃ na janma tasmāc ca mano hi kasyacit // SamUpad_I,19.22 //
children.translated_text: This duality is distinct and firmly established; therefore there is no birth, nor indeed a mind, of anyone. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.22 //

children.text: athābhyupetyāpi bhavaṃ tavecchato bravīmi nārthas tava ceṣṭitena me /
children.translated_text: Now, even conceding birth according to your wish, I say there is no purpose for you in my activity.

children.text: na hānavṛddhī na yataḥ svato 'sato bhavo 'nyato vā yadi vāstitā tayoḥ // SamUpad_I,19.23 //
children.translated_text: For there is neither diminution nor increase, since there is no coming into being of the non-existent by itself or from another, if the existence of both is established. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.23 //

children.text: dhruvā hy anityāś ca na cānyayogino mithaś ca kāryaṃ na ca teṣu yujyate /
children.translated_text: For the permanent and the impermanent are not connected with each other, and mutual causation is not fitting among them.

children.text: ato na kasyāpi hi kiṃcid iṣyate svayaṃ hi tattvaṃ na niruktigocaram // SamUpad_I,19.24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, nothing whatsoever is accepted for anyone; for reality itself is not within the reach of definition. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.24 //

children.text: samaṃ tu tasmāt satataṃ vibhātavad dvayād vimuktaṃ sadasadvikalpitāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, seeing through reasoning and scripture that it is equal, ever-shining, free from the duality of imagined existence and non-existence—

children.text: nirīkṣya yuktyā śrutitaś ca buddhimān aśeṣanirvāṇam upaiti dīpavat // SamUpad_I,19.25 //
children.translated_text: the wise one attains complete <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction of suffering), like a lamp that is extinguished. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.25 //

children.text: avedyam ekaṃ yad ananyavedināṃ kutārkikāṇāṃ ca suvedyam anyathā /
children.translated_text: That which is unknowable and one for those who know no other, and easily known otherwise by sophists—

children.text: nirīkṣya cetthaṃ tv aguṇagraho 'guṇaṃ na yāti mohaṃ grahadoṣamuktitaḥ // SamUpad_I,19.26 //
children.translated_text: seeing thus, one who grasps the qualityless as without qualities does not fall into delusion, being freed from the fault of wrong grasping. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.26 //

children.text: ato 'nyathā na grahanāśa iṣyate vimohabuddher graha eva kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the destruction of grasping is not accepted; grasping itself is the cause of the deluded intellect.

children.text: graho 'py ahetur hy analas tv anindhano yathā praśāntiṃ paramāṃ tathā vrajet // SamUpad_I,19.27 //
children.translated_text: But grasping too is without cause; just as fire without fuel reaches supreme extinction, so too does grasping. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.27 //

children.text: vimathya vedodadhitaḥ samuddhṛtaṃ surair mahābdhes tu yathā mahātmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as nectar was churned and extracted from the great ocean by the great-souled gods,

children.text: tathāmṛtaṃ jñānam idaṃ hi yaiḥ purā namo gurubhyaḥ param īkṣitaṃ ca yaiḥ // SamUpad_I,19.28 //
children.translated_text: so too this immortal knowledge was first perceived from the ocean of the <s>Vedas</s>—salutations to those <s>gurus</s> by whom the Supreme was seen! // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19.28 //

body.text: iti jvaranāśaprakaraṇam // SamUpad_I,19 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Jvaranāśa-prakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on the Destruction of Affliction). // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> I.19 //

body.text: II. GADYABANDHA
body.translated_text: II. <s>Gadyabandha</s> (Prose Section)

body.text: atha mokṣasādhanopadeśavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmo mumukṣūṇāṃ śraddadhānānām arthinām arthāya // SamUpad_II,1.1 //
body.translated_text: Now we shall explain the method of instruction in the means of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), for the benefit of seekers who desire liberation and who are endowed with faith. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.1 //

body.text: tad idaṃ mokṣasādhanaṃ jñānaṃ sādhanasādhyād anityāt sarvasmād viraktāya tyaktaputravittalokaiṣaṇāya pratipannaparamahaṃsapārivrājyāya śamadamadayādiyuktāya śāstraprasiddhaśiṣyaguṇasampannāya śucaye brāhmaṇāya vidhivad upasannāya śiṣyāya jātikarmavṛttavidyābhijanaiḥ parīkṣitāya brūyat punaḥ punar yāvad grahaṇaṃ dṛḍhībhavati // SamUpad_II,1.2 //
body.translated_text: This knowledge, which is the means to liberation, should be imparted to a student who has become dispassionate toward everything impermanent—whether the means or the end to be achieved—who has renounced the desires for sons, wealth, and worldly reputation, who has entered the order of the supreme wandering renunciant (<s>paramahaṃsa parivrājaka</s>), who is endowed with tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-control (<s>dama</s>), compassion (<s>dayā</s>) and the rest, who possesses the qualities of a student as established in the scriptures, who is a pure <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has properly approached the teacher, a student examined with respect to birth, conduct, behavior, knowledge, and lineage—and it should be repeated again and again until the understanding becomes firm. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.2 //

body.text: śrutiś ca -- "parīkṣya ... tattvato brahmavidyām" iti / dṛḍhagṛhītā hi vidyātmanaḥ śreyase santatyai ca bhavati / vidyāsantatiś ca prāṇyanugrahāya bhavati naur iva nadīṃ titīrṣoḥ / śāstraṃ ca -- "yady apy asmā imām adbhiḥ parigṛhītāṃ dhanasya pūrṇāṃ dadyād etad eva tato bhūyaḥ" iti / anyathā ca jñānaprāptyabhāvāt -- "ācāryavān puruṣo veda", "ācāryād dhaiva vidyā viditā [sādhiṣṭhaṃ prāpat]", "ācāryaḥ plāvayitā tasya [samyag]jñānaṃ plava ihocyate" ityādiśrutibhyaḥ smṛtibhyaś ca // SamUpad_II,1.3 //
body.translated_text: And <s>Śruti</s> says: 'Having examined... [one should teach] the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> in truth.' For knowledge firmly grasped leads to the welfare and continuity of the Self. And the continuity of knowledge serves to benefit living beings, like a boat for one who wishes to cross a river. And the scripture says: 'Even if one were to give him this earth surrounded by waters, full of wealth—this knowledge alone would be greater than that.' And because knowledge cannot be obtained otherwise: 'A person who has a teacher knows,' 'Knowledge learned from a teacher alone reaches its best goal,' 'The teacher is the ferryman; right knowledge is said to be the boat here'—from these and other <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> passages. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.3 //

body.text: śiṣyasya jñānāgrahaṇaṃ ca liṅgair buddhvā tadagrahaṇahetūn adharmalaukikapramādanityānitya[vastu]vivekaviṣayāsaṃjātadṛḍhapūrvaśrutatvalokacintāvekṣaṇajātyādyabhimānādīṃs tatpratipakṣaiḥ śrutismṛtivihitair apanayed akrodhādibhir ahiṃsādibhiś ca yamair jñānāviruddhaiś ca niyamaiḥ // SamUpad_II,1.4 //
body.translated_text: And discerning through signs that the student has not grasped the knowledge, the teacher should remove the causes of that non-comprehension—such as attachment to <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), worldly pursuits, negligence, absence of firm prior discrimination between the eternal and non-eternal, worldly reasoning, examination, pride of birth and the like—through their respective antidotes: the restraints (<s>yama</s>) such as non-anger and non-violence prescribed by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, and the observances (<s>niyama</s>) that are not opposed to knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.4 //

body.text: amānitvādiguṇaṃ ca jñānopāyaṃ samyag grāhayet // SamUpad_II,1.5 //
body.translated_text: And he should cause the student to properly grasp the qualities beginning with humility (<s>amānitva</s>) and the rest, which are the means to knowledge. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.5 //

body.text: ācāryaś cohāpohagrahaṇadhāraṇaśamadamadayānugrahādisampanno labdhāgamo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭabhogeṣv anāsaktas tyaktasarvakarmasādhano brahmavid brahmaṇi sthito 'bhinnavṛtto dambhadarpakuhakaśāṭhyamāyāmātsaryānṛtāhaṃkāramamatvādidoṣavarjitaḥ kevalaparānugrahaprayojano vidyopayogārthī pūrvam upadiśet -- "sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam", "yatra nānyat paśyati", "ātmaivedaṃ sarvam", brahmaivedaṃ sarvam", "ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīt", "sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma" ity[ādyāḥ] ātmaikatvapratipādanaparāḥ śrutiḥ // SamUpad_II,1.6 //
body.translated_text: And the teacher, endowed with the abilities of reasoning, refutation, comprehension, retention, tranquility, self-control, compassion, graciousness and the rest, having mastered the scriptures, unattached to the enjoyments of things seen and unseen, having renounced all the means of ritualistic action, a knower of <s>Brahman</s> established in <s>Brahman</s>, of blameless conduct, free from the faults of hypocrisy, pride, deceit, cunning, illusion, jealousy, falsehood, ego, possessiveness and the like, whose sole purpose is the welfare of others, who desires to employ knowledge—should first teach the <s>Śruti</s> passages that establish the oneness of the Self: '<s>Sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam</s>' (Existence alone, O dear one, was this in the beginning, one only without a second), 'Where one sees nothing else,' 'All this is indeed the Self,' 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>,' 'The Self alone was this in the beginning, one only,' '<s>Sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma</s>' (All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>)—and other such passages establishing the oneness of the Self. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.6 //

body.text: upadiśya ca grāhayed brahmaṇo lakṣaṇam -- "ya ātmāpahatapāpmā", "yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma", "yo 'śanāyāpipāse", "neti neti", "asthūlam anaṇu", "sa eṣa neti neti", "adṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭṛ", "vijñānam ānandam", "satyaṃ jñānam anantam", "adṛśye 'nātmye", "sa vā eṣaḥ", "aprāṇo hy amanāḥ", "sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ", "vijñānaghana eva", "anantaram abāhyam", "anyad eva tad viditād atho aviditāt", "ākāśo vai nāma" ityādiśrutibhiḥ // SamUpad_II,1.7 //
body.translated_text: And having taught, he should make the student grasp the defining characteristics of <s>Brahman</s> through <s>Śruti</s> passages: 'The Self that is free from evil,' 'That which is directly and immediately <s>Brahman</s>,' 'That which is beyond hunger and thirst,' '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this), 'Not gross, not subtle,' 'This Self is described as "not this, not this,"' 'The unseen seer,' 'Consciousness and bliss,' '<s>Satyaṃ jñānam anantam</s>' (Truth, knowledge, infinite), 'In the invisible, the non-Self,' 'That one indeed,' 'Without breath, without mind,' 'Both external and internal, unborn,' 'A mass of consciousness alone,' 'Without interior, without exterior,' 'It is different from the known and also from the unknown,' 'Space by name'—and other such <s>Śruti</s> passages. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.7 //

body.text: smṛtibhiś ca -- "na jāyate mriyate vā", "nādatte kasyacit pāpam", "yathākāśasthito nityam", "kṣetrajñāṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi", "na sat tan nāsad ucyate", "anāditvān nirguṇatvat", "samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu", "uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ" ityādibhiḥ śrutyuktalakṣaṇāviruddhābhiḥ paramātmāsaṃsāritvapratipādanaparābhis tasya sarveṇānanyatvapratipādanaparābhiś ca // SamUpad_II,1.8 //
body.translated_text: And through <s>Smṛti</s> passages: 'It is neither born nor does it die,' 'It takes on the sin of none,' 'Just as space ever abides,' 'Know me also as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field),' 'It is called neither existent nor non-existent,' 'Because it is beginningless and without qualities,' 'Equal in all beings,' 'The supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>'—through these and other passages that do not contradict the characteristics stated in <s>Śruti</s>, which establish the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) as free from the cycle of rebirth (<s>saṃsāra</s>), and which establish its non-difference from everything. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.8 //

body.text: evaṃ śrutismṛtibhir gṛhītaparamātmalakṣaṇaṃ śiṣyaṃ saṃsārasāgarād uttitīrṣuṃ pṛcchet -- kas tvam asi somyeti // SamUpad_II,1.9 //
body.translated_text: Having thus taught the student who has grasped the characteristics of the supreme Self through <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, wishing to carry him across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the teacher should ask: 'Who are you, O dear one?' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.9 //

body.text: sa yadi brūyāt -- brāhmaṇaputro 'donvayo brahmacāry āsaṃ gṛhastho vedānīm asmi paramahaṃsaparivrāṭ saṃsārasāgarāj janmamṛtyumahāgrāhād uttitīrṣur iti // SamUpad_II,1.10 //
body.translated_text: If he should reply: 'I am the son of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, of such-and-such lineage; I was formerly a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), then a householder; now I am a <s>paramahaṃsa parivrāṭ</s> (supreme wandering renunciant), wishing to cross over from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, from the great crocodile of birth and death.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.10 //

body.text: ācāryo brūyad -- ihaiva te somya mṛtasya śarīraṃ vayobhir adyate mṛdbhāvaṃ vāpadyate, tatra kathaṃ saṃsārasāgarād uttartum icchasīti / nahi nadyā avare kūle bhasmībhūto nadyāḥ pāraṃ tariṣyasīti // SamUpad_II,1.11 //
body.translated_text: The teacher should say: 'Here, O dear one, when you are dead, your body will be eaten by vultures or reduced to the state of earth. In that case, how do you wish to cross over the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>? For one who has been reduced to ashes on the near bank of a river will not cross to the far shore of the river.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.11 //

body.text: sa yadi brūyāt -- anyo 'haṃ śarīrāt / śarīraṃ tu jāyate mriyate, vayobhir adyate mṛdbhāvam āpadyate, śastrāgnyādibhiś ca vināśyate, vyādhyādibhiś ca yujyate / tasminn ahaṃ svakṛtadharmādharmavaśāt pakṣī nīḍam iva praviṣṭaḥ punaḥ punaḥ śarīravināśe dharmādharmavaśāc charīrāntaraṃ yāsyāmi, pūrvanīḍavināśe pakṣīva nīḍāntaram / evam evāham anādau saṃsāre devatiryaṅmanuṣyanirayasthāneṣu svakarmavaśād upāttam upāttaṃ śarīraṃ tyajan, navaṃ navaṃ cānyad upādadāno, janmamaraṇaprabandhacakre ghaṭīyantravat svakarmaṇā bhrāmyamāṇaḥ krameṇedaṃ śarīram āsādya saṃsāracakrabhramaṇād asmān nirviṇṇo bhagavantam upasanno 'smi saṃsāracakrabhramaṇapraśamāyeti / tasmān nitya evāhaṃ śarīrād anyaḥ / śarīrāṇy āgacchanty apagacchanti ca vāsāṃṣīva puruṣasyeti // SamUpad_II,1.12 //
body.translated_text: If he should reply: 'I am other than the body. The body is born and dies, is eaten by vultures, is reduced to the state of earth, and is destroyed by weapons, fire and the like, and is afflicted by diseases and the rest. Into it I have entered, driven by my own merit and demerit, like a bird into a nest. And again, upon the destruction of the body, driven by merit and demerit, I will go to another body, just as a bird to another nest when the previous nest is destroyed. Thus, in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, in the stations of gods, animals, humans, and hell-beings, driven by my own actions, abandoning each body that I have assumed and taking on yet another new one, revolving like a water-wheel on the unbroken chain of birth and death by my own <s>karma</s>—having thus eventually arrived at this body, weary of the revolving of the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, I have approached the venerable one for the cessation of the revolving of the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>.' Therefore I am indeed eternally other than the body. Bodies come and go like garments of a person. // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.12 //

body.text: ācāryo brūyat -- sādhv avādiḥ samyak paśyasi / kathaṃ mṛṣāvādīr brāhmaṇaputro 'donvayo brahmacāry āsam, gṛhastho vā, idānīm asmi paramahaṃsaparivrāḍ iti // SamUpad_II,1.13 //
body.translated_text: The teacher should say: 'Well have you spoken; you see correctly. But how did you speak falsely—"I am the son of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, of such-and-such lineage, I was formerly a <s>brahmacārin</s>, or a householder, now I am a <s>paramahaṃsa parivrāṭ</s>"?' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.13 //

body.text: sa yadi brūyāt -- bhagavan, katham ahaṃ mṛṣāvādiṣam iti // SamUpad_II,1.14 //
body.translated_text: If he should say: 'O venerable one, how did I speak falsely?' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.14 //

body.text: taṃ prati brūyād ācāryaḥ -- yatas tvaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ śarīraṃ jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjitasyātmanaḥ pratyajñāsīr brāhmaṇaputro 'donvaya ityādinā vākyeneti // SamUpad_II,1.15 //
body.translated_text: The teacher should reply to him: 'Because you identified the body—which has different birth, lineage, and purificatory rites—with the Self that is devoid of birth, lineage, and purificatory rites, by the statement "I am the son of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, of such-and-such lineage" and so on.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.15 //

body.text: sa yadi pṛcchet -- kathaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ śarīram, kathaṃ vāhaṃ jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjita iti // SamUpad_II,1.16 //
body.translated_text: If he should ask: 'How does the body have different birth, lineage, and purificatory rites, and how am I devoid of birth, lineage, and purificatory rites?' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.16 //

body.text: ācāryo brūyat -- śṛṇu somya yathedaṃ śarīraṃ tvatto bhinnaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ tvaṃ ca jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjita ity uktvā taṃ smārayet -- smartum arhasi somya, paramātmānaṃ sarvātmānaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ śrāvito 'si "sad eva somyedam" ityādi[bhiḥ] śrutibhiḥ smṛtibhiś ca / lakṣaṇaṃ ca tasya śrutibhiḥ smṛtibhiś ca // SamUpad_II,1.17 //
body.translated_text: The teacher should say: 'Listen, O dear one, to how this body is different from you, with different birth, lineage, and purificatory rites, and how you are devoid of birth, lineage, and purificatory rites.' Having said this, he should remind him: 'You ought to remember, O dear one—you have been taught the supreme Self, the Self of all, with the characteristics as described, through the <s>Śruti</s> passages beginning with "<s>Sad eva somya</s>" (Existence alone, O dear one) and through <s>Smṛti</s> passages. And its characteristics through <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.17 //

body.text: labdhaparamātmalakṣaṇasmṛtaye brūyāt -- yo 'sāv ākāśanāmā nāmarūpābhyām arthāntarabhūto 'śarīro 'sthūlādilakṣaṇo 'pahatapāpmatvādilakṣaṇaś ca sarvaiḥ saṃsāradharmair anāgandhitaḥ "yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ... eṣa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ", "adṛṣṭo draṣṭā, aśrutaḥ śrotā, amato mantā, avijñāto vijñāta" nityavijñānasvarūpo 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ, "vijñānaghana eva", paripūrṇa ākāśavat, anantaśaktiḥ, ātmā sarvasya, aśanāyādivarjitaḥ, āvirbhāvatirobhāvavarjitaś ca svātmavilakṣaṇayor nāmarūpayor jagadbījabhūtayoḥ svātmasthayoḥ tattvānyatvābhyām anirvacanīyayoḥ svasaṃvedyayoḥ sadbhāvamātreṇācintyaśaktitvād vyākartāvyākṛtayoḥ // SamUpad_II,1.18 //
body.translated_text: For one who has recovered the memory of the characteristics of the supreme Self, he should say: 'That which is called "<s>ākāśa</s>" (space), which is an entity different from name and form, which is bodiless, characterized as "not gross" and so on, characterized as "free from evil" and so on, untouched by all the attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>—"that which is directly and immediately <s>Brahman</s>... this is your Self, the innermost of all," "the unseen seer, the unheard hearer, the unthought thinker, the unknown knower"—of the nature of eternal consciousness, without interior, without exterior, "a mass of consciousness alone," complete like space, of infinite power, the Self of all, free from hunger and the rest, free from appearance and disappearance—it is the substratum of name and form which are different from the Self, which are the seeds of the world, which abide in the Self, which are indescribable as either identical with or different from it, which are known only to itself, and which constitute the manifest and unmanifest due to its inconceivable power.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.18 //

body.text: te nāmarūpe 'vyākṛte satī vyākriyamāṇe tasmād etasmād ātmana ākāśanāmākṛtī saṃvṛtte / tac cākāśakhyaṃ bhūtam anena prakāreṇa paramātmanaḥ sambhūtaṃ prasannāt salilān malam iva phenam / na salilaṃ na ca salilād atyantabhinnaṃ phenam / salilavyatirekeṇādarśanāt / salilaṃ tu svaccham anyat phenān malarūpāt / evaṃ paramātmā nāmarūpābhyām anyaḥ phenasthānīyābhyāṃ śuddhaḥ prasannas tadvilakṣaṇaḥ / te nāmarūpe 'vyākṛte satī vyākriyamāṇe phenasthānīye ākāśanāmākṛtī saṃvṛtte // SamUpad_II,1.19 //
body.translated_text: Those name and form, being in the unmanifest state, becoming manifested from that very Self, assumed the form and name of '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space). And that element called space came into being from the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) in this manner, like foam or impurity from clear water. Foam is neither water nor entirely different from water, since it is not seen apart from water. But water is clear, different from foam which is of the nature of impurity. Similarly, the supreme Self is different from name and form—which stand in the position of foam—pure, clear, and distinct from them. Those name and form, being in the unmanifest state, becoming manifested—standing in the position of foam—assumed the form and name of 'space.' // <s>Upadeśasāhasrī</s> II.1.19 //

body.text: tato 'pi sthūlabhāvam āpadyamāne nāmarūpe vyākriyamāṇe vāyubhāvam āpadyete, tato 'py agnibhāvam, agner abhāvam, tataḥ pṛthvībhāvam ity evaṃkrameṇa pūrvapūrvo[ttaro]ttarānupraveśena pañcamahābhūtāni pṛthivyantāny utpannāni / tataḥ pañcamahābhūtaguṇaviśiṣṭā pṛth[i]vī / pṛth[i]vyāś ca pañcātmakyo vrīhiyavādyā oṣadhayo jāyante / tābhyo bhakṣitābhyo lohitaṃ śukraṃ ca strīpuṃsaśarīrasaṃbandhi jāyate / tad ubhayam ṛtukāle 'vidyāprayuktakāmakhajanirmathanodbhūtaṃ mantrasaṃskṛtaṃ garbhāśaye niṣicyate / tat svayonirasānupraveśena vivardhamānaṃ garbhībhūtaṃ daśame navame vā māsi sañjāyate // SamUpad_II,1.20 //
body.translated_text: Then, as [name-and-form] assume an increasingly gross state, they become the nature of air; from that, the nature of fire; from fire, [the nature of] water; and from that, the nature of earth. Thus, in this order, through the successive mutual interpenetration of the preceding and the following, the five great elements (<s>pañcamahābhūta</s>) ending with earth are produced. From these [arises] earth possessing the qualities of all five great elements. And from earth are born the herbs—rice, barley, and the like—having a fivefold nature. From these, when eaten, blood and semen are produced, belonging to the female and male bodies. Both of these, at the proper season, churned forth by desire impelled by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), consecrated by <s>mantras</s>, are deposited in the womb. That, growing through the absorption of the fluids of its own source, having become an embryo, is born in the tenth or ninth month. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.20 //

body.text: taj jātaṃ labdhanāmākṛtikaṃ jātakarmādibhir mantrasaṃskṛtaṃ punar upanayanasaṃskārayogena brahmacārisaṃjñaṃ bhavati / tad eva śarīraṃ patnīsaṃyogasaṃskārayogena gṛhasthasaṃjñaṃ bhavati / tad eva vanasthasaṃskāreṇa tāpasasaṃjñaṃ bhavati / tad eva kriyāvinivṛttinimittasaṃskāreṇa parivrāṭsaṃjñaṃ bhavati / ity evaṃ tvatto bhinnaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ śarīram // SamUpad_II,1.21 //
body.translated_text: That [body], once born, having acquired a name and form, consecrated by <s>mantras</s> through birth-rites (<s>jātakarma</s>) and other [sacraments], again through the sacrament of investiture (<s>upanayana</s>), receives the designation <s>brahmacārin</s> (student). That same body, through the sacrament of union with a wife, receives the designation <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder). That same [body], through the sacrament of forest-dwelling, receives the designation <s>tāpasa</s> (ascetic). That same [body], through the sacrament occasioned by the cessation of [ritualistic] activity, receives the designation <s>parivrāj</s> (wandering renunciant). Thus, the body—different from you—has the sacraments of different castes and lineages. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.21 //

body.text: manaś cendriyāṇi ca nāmarūpātmakāny eva "annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ" ityādiśrutibhyaḥ // SamUpad_II,1.22 //
body.translated_text: The mind and the sense organs too are of the nature of name-and-form alone, from <s>śruti</s> texts such as 'the mind, O dear one, is indeed made of food' and the like. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.22 //

body.text: kathaṃ cāhaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāravarjita ity etac chṛṇu / yo 'sau nāmarūpayor vyākartā nāmarūpadharmavilakṣaṇaḥ sa eva nāmarūpe vyākurvan sṛṣṭvedaṃ śarīraṃ svayaṃ saṃskāradharmavarjito nāmarūpa iha praviṣṭo 'nyair adṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃ paśyaṃs tathāśrutaḥ śṛṇvann amato manvāno 'vijñāto vijānan -- "sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vicitya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadan yad āste" iti / asminn arthe śrutayaḥ sahasraśaḥ "tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviṣat". "antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānām", "sa eṣa iha praviṣṭaḥ", "eṣa ta ātmā", "sa etam eva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata", "eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā", "seyaṃ devataikṣata hantāham imās tisro devatāḥ", "aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu" ityādyāḥ // SamUpad_II,1.23 //
body.translated_text: And how you are free from the sacraments of different castes and lineages—hear this. He who is the unfolder of name-and-form, distinct from the properties of name-and-form—that very one, unfolding name-and-form, having created this body, himself free from the property of sacraments, has entered into name-and-form here, unseen by others yet himself seeing, likewise unheard yet hearing, unthought yet thinking, unknown yet knowing—'The wise one, having contemplated all forms, creating names, sits speaking' [Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 3.12.7]. On this subject, <s>śruti</s> texts are [available] by the thousands: 'Having created it, it entered into that very thing' [Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.6], 'The inner controller, the ruler of all people' [Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 3.11], 'That one has entered here' [Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.5.18], 'This is your Self' [Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.4.1], 'It broke open this very seam and entered through this door' [Aitareya Upaniṣad 1.3.12], 'This Self hidden in all beings' [Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.12], 'That deity thought: "Let me enter these three deities"' [Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.3.2], 'The bodiless one among bodies' [Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.22], and the like. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.23 //

body.text: smṛtayo 'pi "ātmaiva devatāḥ sarvāḥ", "navadvāre pure dehī", "kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi", "samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu", "upadraṣṭānumantā ca", "uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ" ityādyāḥ / tasmāj jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjitas tvam iti siddham // SamUpad_II,1.24 //
body.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> texts also [confirm this]: 'The Self alone is all the deities' [Manusmṛti 12.119], 'The embodied one in the city of nine gates' [Bhagavadgītā 5.13], 'Know me also as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field)' [Bhagavadgītā 13.2], 'Equal in all beings' [Bhagavadgītā 13.27], 'The witness and the approver' [Bhagavadgītā 13.22], 'But the Supreme Person is another' [Bhagavadgītā 15.17], and the like. Therefore, it is established that you are free from the sacraments of caste and lineage. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.24 //

body.text: sa yadi brūyāt -- anya evāham ajñaḥ sukhī duḥkhī baddhaḥ saṃsārī, anyo 'sau madvilakṣaṇo 'saṃsārī devaḥ, tam ahaṃ balyupahāranamaskārādibhir varṇāśramakarmabhiś cārādhya saṃsārasāgarād uttitīrṣur asmi, katham ahaṃ sa eveti // SamUpad_II,1.25 //
body.translated_text: If [the student] should say: 'I myself am one thing—ignorant, happy, suffering, bound, a transmigrating being; and that [Supreme Self], distinct from me, is another—a non-transmigrating deity. I wish to cross over the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) by worshipping him through offerings, oblations, obeisances, and the like, and through the <s>karmas</s> prescribed for [my] <s>varṇa</s> (caste) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life). How can I be that very one?' // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.25 //

body.text: ācāryo brūyat -- naivaṃ somya pratipattum arhasi, pratiṣiddhatvād bhedapratipatteḥ / kathaṃ pratiṣiddhā bhedapratipattir ity ata āha -- "anyo 'sāv anyo 'ham asmīti na sa veda", "brahma taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmano brahma veda", mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati" ityevamādyāḥ // SamUpad_II,1.26 //
body.translated_text: The teacher should say: 'You should not think in this way, O dear one, because the perception of difference is prohibited. How is the perception of difference prohibited? [The <s>śruti</s>] says: "He does not know, [who thinks] 'that is one, I am another'" [Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.4.10], "<s>Brahman</s> rejected him who knows <s>Brahman</s> as other than the Self" [Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4.6], "He goes from death to death who sees multiplicity here, as it were" [Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.4.19]—and the like.' // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.26 //

body.text: etā eva śrutayo bhedapratipatteḥ saṃsāragamanaṃ darśayanti // SamUpad_II,1.27 //
body.translated_text: These very <s>śruti</s> texts show that from the perception of difference comes transmigration. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.27 //

body.text: abhedapratipatteś ca mokṣaṃ darśayanti sahasraśaḥ -- "sa ātmā tat tvam asi" iti paramātmabhāvaṃ vidhāya "ācāryavān puruṣo veda" ity uktvā "tasya tāvad eva ciram" iti mokṣaṃ darśayanty abhedavijñānād eva satyasandhasyātaskarasyeva dāhādyabhāvadṛṣṭāntena saṃsārābhāvaṃ darśayanti, bhedadarśanād asatyābhisandhasya saṃsāragamanaṃ darśayanti taskarasyeva dāhādidṛṣṭāntena // SamUpad_II,1.28 //
body.translated_text: And they show liberation from the perception of non-difference, by the thousands: having established the identity with the Supreme Self through 'That is the Self; that thou art (<s>tat tvam asi</s>)' [Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7], having stated 'A person who has a teacher knows' [Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.14.2], they show liberation through 'For him, there is that much delay [only until he is freed from the body]' [Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.14.2], showing the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> from the knowledge of non-difference alone, by the illustration of the absence of burning and the like for one who is truthful and innocent, and showing transmigration from the perception of difference for one who is untruthful, by the illustration of burning and the like for a thief. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.28 //

body.text: "ta iha vyāghro vā" ityādinā cābhedadarśanāt "[sa] sarvāḍ bhavati" ity uktvā tadviparītena bhedadarśanena saṃsāragamanaṃ darśayanti -- "atha ye 'nyathāto vidur anyarājānas te kṣayyalokā bhavanti" iti pratiśākham / tasmān mṛṣaivāvādīḥ -- brāhmaṇaputro 'donvayaḥ saṃsārī paramātmavilakṣaṇa iti // SamUpad_II,1.29 //
body.translated_text: And having stated, through 'Whether it be a tiger or...' and the like, that from the vision of non-difference '[one] becomes all,' they show transmigration from the contrary vision of difference: 'But those who know otherwise than this, having other rulers—their worlds are perishable,' in each <s>śākhā</s> (branch of the Veda). Therefore, it was entirely false what you said—that a brāhmaṇa's son, of such-and-such lineage, a transmigrating being, is different from the Supreme Self. // Upadeśasāhasrī II,1.29 //

body.text: tasmāt pratiṣiddhatvād bhedadarśanasya, bhedaviṣayatvāc ca karmopādānasya, karmasādhanatvāc ca yajñopavītādeḥ karmasādhanopādānasya paramātmābhedapratipattyā pratiṣedhaḥ kṛto veditavyaḥ / karmaṇāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ ca yajñopavītādīnāṃ paramātmābhedapratipattiviruddhatvāt / saṃsāriṇo hi karmāṇi vidhīyante tatsādhanāni ca yajñopavītādīni, na paramātmano 'bhedadarśinaḥ / bhedadarśanamātreṇa ca tato 'nyatvam // SamUpad_II,1.30 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, since the vision of difference is prohibited, and since the undertaking of <s>karma</s> has difference as its object, and since the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>) and the like are instruments of <s>karma</s>, the prohibition of undertaking the instruments of <s>karma</s> should be understood as having been made through the realization of non-difference from the Supreme Self.
